topic: Further discovery needed before design
statement: Jumpr asked for more discovery with WagerTech and its teams to get business context and validate the PRD solution. Joyce agreed that more discovery is needed.

topic: PRD defines what, Jumpr defines how
statement: Joyce stated the PRD describes what WagerTech wants, not how to build it, and WagerTech looks to Jumpr to define the how.

topic: Business process review format and duration
statement: Waleed proposed a one to one-and-a-half hour business process review where end users run an entire deal on screen share, with Jumpr returning next steps two to three days after. Emily said one hour would be more than enough.

topic: Interim notes or recorded signup walkthrough
statement: Joyce noted an internal walkthrough session happened the day before with detailed notes and asked if some content could be shared in the interim. Lina and Emily suggested having Jay run through a signup and record it. Format was left to be sorted offline.

topic: Walkthrough must cover end-to-end deal flow
statement: Joyce said the walkthrough must start from initial link generation and show how a deal flows from affiliate link tracking to rep attribution, the rep flow, and into Salesforce.

topic: Schedule discovery walkthrough for tomorrow
statement: WagerTech (Lina) will sync offline with Jumpr to arrange the walkthrough call; Jumpr has availability the next day and expects to give its position by early next week.

topic: Jumpr to send meeting hold 3-4:30
statement: Emily asked Jumpr for a calendar hold for the next day between 3:00 and 4:30; Waleed confirmed Jumpr will send it.

topic: WagerTech to confirm walkthrough attendees
statement: WagerTech will figure out who can join the next-day walkthrough and coordinate on the who.

topic: Existing org built with Claude, not scalable
statement: Emily said a junior employee built the current Salesforce implementation heavily using Claude, with custom building that moved fast but that WagerTech knows is not scalable.

topic: Start fresh or reuse existing build
statement: Waleed asked whether to start fresh or continue the existing build. Joyce said it depends on Jumpr's recommendation after review; WagerTech is open to either.

topic: Grant Jumpr admin access to Salesforce
statement: WagerTech agreed to give Jumpr admin access to its Salesforce org, to the address consulting+wt at Jumpr; Emily and Lina will handle it offline.

topic: License capacity for consultant admin user
statement: Emily flagged a possible licensing/capacity constraint for an admin user and said they may need to remove a user; Waleed said any consultant needs a minimum of one license.

topic: Org is Sales Cloud Enterprise Edition
statement: Lina confirmed WagerTech has Sales Cloud Enterprise Edition; Jumpr will double-check once it has access.

topic: Below Enterprise edition would not support design
statement: Waleed said that on an edition below Enterprise the PRD design would not be supported because many automations would be scaled back.

topic: Market: countries plus states/provinces selectable
statement: Market should allow selecting applicable countries (Canada and US) and applicable states and provinces; deals vary from nationwide Canada to one or two US states.

topic: Market as standalone object vs multi-select
statement: Joyce asked whether Market needs to be its own object or just attached to deals. Waleed said the non-custom option is a multi-select picklist, which will not support reporting pivots (e.g., 'show me Ontario'). No direction was set.

topic: Market drives deal-specific CPA rates
statement: Market matters for reporting and for configuring deal-specific CPA rates: each state an operator is active in can have unique rates by player type (sportsbook, casino, sweeps, social casino).

topic: CPA based on location first, then vertical
statement: Lina said the solution should always account for CPA changes, based on location first and then vertical (sports, casino, or sweeps); not every agreement is structured that way.

topic: 'Vertical' replaces 'operator type' label
statement: Joyce agreed to use 'vertical' as the label for what the PRD called 'operator type'.

topic: No percentage split of amounts across markets
statement: Amounts (redeposits, signups) do not need to be split by percentage across a deal's regions; attribution goes back to the deal, and each signup originates from a single location.

topic: Track signup location per signup
statement: Each signup records where the player signed up from (a single location); CPAs do not need to be attached at the signup level.

topic: Redeposits relate to signup origin
statement: Lina said redeposits are related to signups: as signups grow, the retention budget grows, and it is always tied to where the signup originated.

topic: Player enters location; rep validates
statement: On the website the user specifies state/province and country; at the signup flow stage a rep logging and confirming the record validates it.

topic: Bet Lab is legacy agency brand
statement: 'Bet Lab' is one legacy agency-branded site; 'Betlab hub/API' is an internal name, not user-facing, and Joyce said such internal tools should be renamed through this process. 'Agency' is used synonymously.

topic: Agency sites feed Salesforce via shared API
statement: Multiple agency websites share a common backend (the Betlab hub API); consolidated data flows into Salesforce. WagerTech owns the websites and the full data pipeline. In the PRD only signups were seen as automated input.

topic: Website-to-Salesforce data discrepancies
statement: WagerTech has discrepancies between website submissions and Salesforce (leads submitted but not appearing); WagerTech is troubleshooting this outside this engagement.

topic: Prior signup-flow launch was flat
statement: WagerTech tried to launch a signup-flow-only version with website data flowing in; it was flat, did not scale and did not use native objects.

topic: Standard over custom objects stance
statement: Waleed said Jumpr prefers standard objects and uses custom only when standard cannot work, and that for these requirements they do not think custom objects should be used; he also said they had no hard opinion yet and would determine it through the process.

topic: Players: person account vs custom object
statement: Jumpr is evaluating whether players can be person accounts or need a custom object.

topic: Players are always individuals
statement: Joyce confirmed players are never businesses; they are always individuals.

topic: Track partner/operator contact relationships
statement: WagerTech does not track contacts at partners/operators yet but will; they want to store primary contact information and create a more typical CRM environment.

topic: Future B2B sales lead flow
statement: Joyce said that as WagerTech expands B2B sales efforts there is an opportunity to use a more typical lead flow; no timing was set.

topic: Partners and operators as Accounts
statement: Waleed said the answers point to modelling partners and operators as full Accounts so contacts can sit under them, and said Jumpr will look into it. Joyce responded 'Mhm'; no explicit confirmation.

topic: Deals not built on Opportunity
statement: Jumpr does not want to use Opportunity for deals because opportunities are for forecasting with open/closed states, while deals are executed agreements that are living records. Joyce asked why, heard the reason, and said 'Okay, keep going' with no pushback.

topic: Lead object not required for signups
statement: Miko asked if WagerTech is dependent on the Lead object for signups as the PRD states. Joyce said no; PRD object names can be disregarded if Jumpr is not aligned.

topic: One player record linked to many signups
statement: Core principle: one centralized object that can be associated with multiple signups, with a one-to-many structure in place; the object type (custom or native) is Jumpr's call.

topic: Signup flow requirements being reworked
statement: Joyce said the PRD signup flow section was based on recreating the Google Sheets logging process and has been rethought; Jumpr should not read too closely into the table vs card view, which may not survive.

topic: Joyce to send signup flow mockup
statement: Joyce will send Jumpr an AI-generated mockup of the revised signup logging flow before attaching detailed requirements; Jumpr (Miko) will advise whether it is implementable natively and the right direction. Joyce said she could circle back on the signup flow that night.

topic: Custom UI only where value justifies
statement: Miko said table/card views would need custom components; Jumpr favors out-of-the-box for maintainability and builds custom only where there is clear value, though it does not shy away from custom.

topic: Signup data volume for storage forecast
statement: Miko asked to understand signup volume during discovery to forecast Salesforce data storage, since moving off Dropbox for cost savings is part of the project's value.

topic: Salesforce file storage is limited and costly
statement: Miko noted Enterprise includes 10 GB storage scaling with licenses, extra storage is pricey, and third-party tools are alternatives. Emily said Salesforce storage looked expensive compared with their single Dropbox account.

topic: Store links to external files
statement: Waleed suggested storing a link to the file in Salesforce instead of uploading it, using Google Drive, Dropbox or AWS file storage for high volume. WagerTech did not explicitly confirm.

topic: Miko to verify Snowflake media storage
statement: Joyce asked if Snowflake can store images and videos. Miko said it stores them as blobs and he would not recommend it right away, but will check for updates and get back.

topic: Phase one go-live mid-July
statement: Joyce wants phase one live by mid-July, maybe sooner. Jumpr did not agree; Waleed said a typical Sales Cloud implementation takes two to three months and July is tight, with feasibility to follow.

topic: Jumpr to report July feasibility
statement: Waleed said Jumpr would tell WagerTech by the end of the week whether mid-July is possible, once requirements are understood; later he said the design coming early next week will include Jumpr's view on timing and whether July can be hit.

topic: MVP: foundation, signups, redeposits, referrals
statement: Lina defined the MVP as foundation, signups, redeposits and referrals, the core of the business for brand ambassadors; later PRD phases follow.

topic: Jumpr to present system design early next week
statement: Jumpr will determine the system design from the PRD and discovery and come back early next week with what the design looks like.

topic: Discovery scoped to end-user process demos
statement: Waleed said Jumpr's discovery usually produces a shorter design document, but because WagerTech already has a PRD, Jumpr will only focus on end users demoing how they do the process today (data for new players and signups, Google Sheets), then validate against the PRD.

topic: Manual versus automated data inputs
statement: Waleed said Jumpr needs to understand which data will be input manually versus automatically; in the PRD he saw only signups coming in automatically through the Betlab hub. Joyce then described the shared API; no full answer on other transactions was given.

topic: Lead dedup and Betlab API insert dependencies
statement: Miko said that during discovery Jumpr wants to understand native Salesforce duplicate handling on Lead and any dependencies on how the Betlab hub API inserts records into Salesforce, before deciding the signup object.

topic: Waleed to review client PRD
statement: Waleed confirmed he received the PRD from Joyce and said he will go through it.

topic: Waleed to validate Salesforce login
statement: Waleed told Emily he will validate the Salesforce login.

topic: Share meeting recording with client
statement: Emily asked Jumpr to send the recording after the meeting; Waleed said he is happy to share it.

topic: Current sign-up intake via WhatsApp group chat
statement: Current process: the referrer creates a WhatsApp group chat with the BA and the new sign-up; the BA sends a script asking for welcome-email screenshots, survey confirmation and the e-transfer email, in a fixed format (full name, ET email, casinos).

topic: 24h proof turnaround and 48h cutoff
statement: Current rule: sign-ups have 24 hours to return deposit/wager proof (transaction history); after a reminder, if there is no proof in 48 hours they are not considered for redeposits or other sites. Some reps take four or five days.

topic: High-volume referrers act as proxy
statement: Very high-volume referrers (200-300 sign-ups a week) act as a proxy and forward sign-up details in an operations chat; Jay still requires a group chat with each sign-up for direct contact, but many do not do this.

topic: Referrer is always a person
statement: Client confirmed that a referrer (referral name) is always a person, never a company.

topic: Current fraud handling: immediate ban
statement: Current process: when a BA finds faked proof, the person is banned immediately (ban list), the referrer is told and the sales chat is alerted; associated people are investigated. The ban list is not checked up front because sign-ups arrive at random hours.

topic: Fraud flags at sign-up and player level
statement: Joyce said the PRD has flagging at both sign-up and player level, but not the relationship between them; both capabilities are needed, with exception handling and flag reasons on sign-ups that tie back to the linked player. Waleed agreed.

topic: Ops user type with separate visibility
statement: Fraud escalation should be flagged to the operations team, a separate user type not yet in the PRD; operations members need different visibility and workflows than reps. Waleed agreed.

topic: More fraud controls in system to scale
statement: Ops mainly detects scams monthly through tracking reports. Joyce said that if they scale and add reps, the technology should have more controls and visibility over flagged players; Jay agreed. No specific control was defined.

topic: Book deposit range and average
statement: Current process: when operations opens a book for a BA it gives a deposit range and an average; the BA chooses an amount within that range and varies amounts per book for tracking. Ranges and averages are kept in AirTable.

topic: Deal active start and end dates
statement: Waleed asked whether there are start and end dates and how the period a book is active (opened/closed) is controlled. The transcript has no direct answer.

topic: Ops assigns books to reps under caps
statement: Reps do not choose which book to offer; operations (Owen, Jess, Ilas) decides which book is open for each rep based on rep volume and the affiliate's player cap, and distributes each affiliate's monthly cap across reps.

topic: Bring deal management into Salesforce
statement: Joyce said the AirTable book/cap work is the deal management work they are hoping to bring into Salesforce, and that it is where everything starts; Owen agreed. The wording is 'hoping to', not a confirmed scope call in this meeting.

topic: Deal = operator (book) + partner
statement: Joyce described a deal as the combination of operator (same as book) and partner; today it is one concatenated value (e.g. DraftKings C) instead of two split fields. Book suffixes (GD, CTM, C) identify the affiliate partner.

topic: Book list is fixed reference data
statement: All books are always listed on the logging sheet; reps select the correct book. New books are rarely introduced and are added to the sheet when they are; books are mainly opened and closed.

topic: Operator data join out of initial scope
statement: Joyce said pulling in operator data and joining it with internal logging data is scoped outside the initial Salesforce implementation because it needs a data-cleaning/matching process; Waleed accepted.

topic: No operator-side sign-up verification
statement: Today the team cannot verify on the operator side that a player signed up; they rely on rep-provided proof and later reports. Operators/affiliates also update data on different timelines.

topic: Current sign-up log fields
statement: Current BA log captures customer email, sales rep (BA), sign-up date (date deposited), referral name, referral payout, customer first/last name, one line per sportsbook/casino book, region (e.g. Ontario, Canada), amount sent and amount the company covered, and three proofs: welcome email, deposit proof, wager proof.

topic: Proofs uploaded to Dropbox
statement: Proof screenshots and videos (welcome email, deposit, wager transaction history) are uploaded to Dropbox and linked in the BA sheet. The existing API does not handle these proofs.

topic: Referral payout fixed at $40 (Canada)
statement: Client confirmed the referral payout is always $40 for Canada with no negotiation; it differs for the USA (regional split).

topic: Payout types: e-transfer, cash, bet credit
statement: Referral payouts are e-transfer; alternatively $25 cash if the referrer wants it or $40 in bet credit (which must be deposited and wagered).

topic: Payout amount from payout matrix
statement: Joyce said the payout amount cannot be chosen by the person setting up the payout; it comes from the payout matrix (different for US). She suggested a table that admins may edit in the background, not editable by the payout creator.

topic: Default payout preference at referrer level
statement: Joyce recommended a default payout preference (e.g. bet credit vs cash) at referrer level, with the rep able to override it per sign-up/commission; Waleed and Jay agreed.

topic: Existing API pulls study-link sign-up data
statement: Emily said the first build's API pulled name, user, email, book and date from the agency websites/study links, matching sign-up, survey completion and book click as the happy path. BLH entries come from the Play can admin reporting.

topic: Sign-up status reflects completion checks
statement: Waleed proposed the sign-up record status represents completing the checks; Emily confirmed: account sign-up, survey completion, book click (from the API), plus deposit/wager validation from screenshots.

topic: AI extraction of proof metadata
statement: Joyce said they want an AI process to extract sign-up, deposit and first-wager dates/times from screenshot proofs, and was unsure if Jumpr would build it. Waleed said Jumpr can but does not have to; no owner was assigned.

topic: Phase one is capture infrastructure
statement: Waleed said phase one is about building the infrastructure to capture the information (implying AI extraction is later); Joyce said yes.

topic: Make logging simple; reps work on phones
statement: BAs do sales on their phones and log on a computer at end of day; logging is tedious and takes time from sales. The top wish is to make logging as simple as possible so BAs focus on sales.

topic: WhatsApp integration not yet explored
statement: Asked whether they had looked at integrating WhatsApp with Salesforce, Joyce said not yet and that it can come later potentially.

topic: WhatsApp integration in Jumpr recommendation
statement: Waleed said a WhatsApp integration will be part of Jumpr's recommendation (can be phased), using existing tools; Jumpr has not built a WhatsApp integration before. Joyce agreed to include it in the recommendation, with sequencing still to be discussed.

topic: WhatsApp sequencing open
statement: Sequencing of the WhatsApp integration (which phase) is not decided; Joyce said they can talk about sequencing.

topic: Ops-assigned redeposit budgets by book and window
statement: Current process: operations assigns redeposits on each BA sheet by book with set amounts from a budget and a sign-up date window; the BA picks eligible players from their sign-ups in that window, sends the money and requests deposit/wager proof. Assignments change monthly and must be finished by month end.

topic: Player choice for redeposit by rep
statement: There is no method for which players get a redeposit; the rep chooses from knowledge, aiming to reach as many players as possible.

topic: Redeposit proof and approval flow
statement: The rep enters the name when sending money, uploads proof to Dropbox, adds the link and date; the redeposit owner in operations confirms it and moves it to a master sheet, highlighting it yellow as approved.

topic: Redeposit frequency per person
statement: Ideally no more than two, sometimes three, redeposits go to the same person; exceptions happen, e.g. a rep paying a weekly top referrer $100 through a redeposit.

topic: Additional redeposits for BetMGM
statement: 'Additional' redeposits are assigned for some books, mainly BetMGM, after a sign-up completes; the rep chooses an amount within a range (about $30-$80) and they are marked 'additional' so they can be separated in company calculations. BetMGM expects re-engagement within one to three days.

topic: Bank payments via Salesforce API
statement: Jay asked if Salesforce could send payments through an API instead of reps using BMO accounts; Waleed said it will be a while before they touch the banks.

topic: Bank transfer log for monthly audit
statement: Each bank transfer is logged (recipient, book, type such as redeposit, amount, date) on a transfers tab so the monthly audit can match the bank account. Reps also keep inflow/outflow logs, write-offs with reasons (e.g. no response) and audit corrections.

topic: Most important trackers named
statement: Jay said the most important sheets are the redeposit tracker, the BetLab transfers and the sign-ups; the others are less important.

topic: Tactics (TT) in initial build?
statement: Jay asked whether TT is in scope; Joyce said not yet, that it should be in the system as a core process and was the original thought, but she is not sure it will be in the initial build. She asked Jay to cover it at high level in the meeting.

topic: TT subscription bonus redeposits
statement: Current TT process: reps sign users up for TT packages (tiers 1-7) and record phone, referral, email, package, subscribed/end dates and price; the company gives bonus redeposits (e.g. $150 for a $50 package) that the rep assembles from the redeposit tracker, aiming for zero unassigned extra spend.

topic: Weekly Wednesday CPA vs logs reporting
statement: Completed sign-ups move automatically to a master sheet used for back-end reporting (sign-ups per book vs cap vs CPAs). The main report is every Wednesday; operator/affiliate data timelines vary and need follow-up; the CPA-vs-logs report takes about one to two hours.

topic: Other ops reports
statement: Other reports cover deposit data, redeposit timelines (e.g. BetMGM timely retention), completion percentages for books, and progress against targets and caps.

topic: Bundled referral payouts with proof
statement: Referrers earn $40 per client per book; BAs let referral payouts accumulate and send one large transfer on a set day. Proof of deposit and wager is required, as for redeposits; larger transfers get a little more grace period.

topic: Priority books for referral payouts
statement: Operations decides which books referral payouts should use (mainly DraftKings CTM, Proline C, some BetMGM GD); this changes with active deals and each salesperson is told.

topic: PRD payout record bundles completed leads
statement: Joyce said the PRD scopes the referrer payout flow, bundling completed leads into a new record type called payouts.

topic: Player payouts tracking and payout dashboard
statement: The PRD does not include tracking payouts to players (Joyce thinks it can be inferred from the sign-up process). She flagged for later discussion that a payout dashboard should show all money out to referrers and players for sign-ups or redeposits.

topic: Return by Tuesday with next steps and plan
statement: Waleed said Jumpr expects to come back by Tuesday with next steps and a plan for converting the current process in line with the PRD.

topic: Align with client data architect
statement: Joyce asked Jumpr to include steps with their new data architect (senior engineer) so his data mapping for matching operator data downstream aligns with Jumpr's Salesforce structure, possibly via joint sessions; Waleed agreed.

topic: Reach out Monday to schedule follow-up
statement: Waleed will reach out on Monday to book a follow-up meeting (Tuesday or Wednesday); Emily agreed and said it is top priority for them.

topic: Jumpr now has org access
statement: Emily said Jumpr has access now and asked to be told if not; she said there is context in the initial build to glean.

topic: V1 scope and phased approach
statement: Waleed asked for agreement that the work is phased as adoption grows; Joyce restated V1 as the foundational data structure capturing the sign-up flow, redeposits and payouts, with other items to be discussed for the initial release.

topic: Sign-ups come only through referrers
statement: Current process: WagerTech works only with people referred by others (referral bonuses drive this); there are no lead lists that reps work from.

topic: Manual proof validation checks for fraud
statement: Current process: BAs validate sign-up screenshots by eye for manipulation, e.g. edited dates, presence of usernames on old BetMGM accounts, and email/name mismatches in welcome emails.

topic: Case-by-case judgement before banning
statement: Jay said there is context to everything: for genuine mistakes (e.g. not knowing a new account was needed, language barriers) he uses caution, while obvious fakes are banned. This nuances the 'banned immediately' statement and is the basis for Joyce's exception-handling need.

topic: Tracking links live in Play can admin
statement: Joyce said that once deals are configured, the specific tracking links live in a different system (Play can admin), and asked for a walkthrough of it. No walkthrough of Play can admin happened in this meeting.

topic: Affiliate attribution by promo code or link
statement: Some affiliates attribute sign-ups by promo code/campaign, so the link is identifiable; others give only one or two generic links with no such ID.

topic: Operator verification delays sign-up completion
statement: Some sign-ups cannot complete quickly because the player hits operator account verification issues (e.g. Caesars) and must wait a few days to deposit; such sign-ups stay incomplete on the log (example from early May still not done).

topic: Proof rules: full deposit, matching wager type
statement: Current rules: the player must prove they deposited the full amount sent and wagered the full amount; casino books need a casino wager and sportsbooks a sports bet.

topic: Ops works across all BA sheets
statement: Operations creates each BA's sheet and all operations members work in BA sheets during the day; Owen strongly agreed operations would benefit from a centralized system. No specific ops feature was defined.

topic: Cash referral payout practically unused
statement: Jay said no referrer has ever taken the cash option on the example rep's sheet, because cash is $25 versus $40 otherwise.

topic: PRD automatic redeposit = 'additional' entry
statement: Waleed checked that the PRD's automatic redeposit is the 'additional' entry the rep adds right after a sign-up; Owen confirmed, and said the rep owns following that timeline so the client gets and completes the redeposit quickly.

topic: Start fresh, do not reuse existing code
statement: The existing org already has over 8,000 lines of code. WagerTech confirmed the earlier proof-of-concept build is not usable, and both sides agreed to start fresh without reusing the existing code.

topic: Native-first build over custom code
statement: Jumpr recommended a native-first approach (flows, standard layouts, Lightning web components in native pages) instead of custom code, to support growth and avoid reliance on a single developer. WagerTech accepted this.

topic: WhatsApp integration not in Phase 1
statement: Using WhatsApp as the place where rep work is captured (for example API integration or reading chats with N8N) is not part of Phase 1 and needs a separate conversation. WagerTech agreed.

topic: Pivot notifications to WhatsApp
statement: Joyce suggested that the PRD notifications and alerting section could pivot from native Salesforce app or email notifications to WhatsApp. Waleed said this could happen; the notification automation lives in Salesforce and an app may be needed to send to WhatsApp. No final decision was made.

topic: Dedicated WhatsApp Business sending account
statement: For notifications only, one WhatsApp Business account that sends notifications is enough; reps would not need to switch their personal accounts. Lina said WagerTech could get a dedicated WhatsApp Business account for this. No commitment was made.

topic: Person accounts for players and referrers
statement: Jumpr proposed Person Accounts for both players and referrers instead of B2B account plus contact. Waleed stated this is not final and the design will be finalized in about the first week.

topic: Native User object for reps and managers
statement: Jumpr proposed dropping the custom rep and manager objects in the current PRD/org and using the native User object instead.

topic: Operator and partner as Accounts; market custom
statement: Jumpr proposed that operator and partner are Account records (allowing account hierarchy later) and that market is a custom object.

topic: Deal rep assignment object kept
statement: Jumpr endorsed WagerTech's deal rep assignment object as the key to automating book assignment and monitoring reps, and to moving off Airtable. Deal stays as WagerTech designed it.

topic: Sign-up intake flow and email matching
statement: Proposed flow: the API sends the sign-up and creates a Sign-Up record; the system checks the email. Unknown email creates a Lead (unverified player); known email matches the sign-up to the existing player Person Account. Sign-ups would no longer be leads converted to contacts.

topic: When lead converts to player
statement: The trigger for converting a Lead to a player Person Account is not decided; likely after first deposit proof is verified.

topic: Add payout line item object
statement: Jumpr proposed a payout line item object (not in WagerTech's design) so each payout amount can be traced and the books closed.

topic: Bank transfer object in Phase 2
statement: Jumpr proposed an automatically maintained bank transfer object to show a ledger of player bank transactions. Joyce confirmed it is right to have it in Phase 2.

topic: Payment processor integration later
statement: WagerTech is exploring fintech payment processors that could integrate with Salesforce; Joyce called this a down-the-line conversation. Waleed said the bank transfer object could interact with the processor (draft, sent to processor, result back to Salesforce).

topic: Bank API connection in scope?
statement: Lina asked to include an API connection with WagerTech's current bank in scope discussion. Jumpr has never connected to a bank and did not agree; it will research and get back.

topic: Research bank API connection
statement: Jumpr will research connecting Salesforce to WagerTech's current bank via API and report back to Lina.

topic: Data engineer ERD as source of truth
statement: WagerTech asked that its data engineer's ERD be the source of truth, with Jumpr and the data engineer finalizing the object design together and the data engineer owning the final outlook. Waleed agreed; finalizing this design is the first week's work if the engagement proceeds.

topic: Phase 1 scope definition
statement: Phase 1 is proposed as building the object model, having sign-ups flow in from the API, and completing the first sign-up flow.

topic: Mid-July Phase 1 too tight
statement: WagerTech asked for mid-July. Waleed said mid-July is really tight even with two resources and put end of July as the proposed date. The date was not agreed in this meeting.

topic: Phase 2 scope definition
statement: Phase 2 is proposed to add redeposits (automated ones from BetMGM and incentivized ones), move the Airtable operations cadence into Salesforce, and add the book assignment logic.

topic: Phase 3 scope definition
statement: Phase 3 is proposed to add payouts, payout line items, and additional reporting.

topic: Each phase a self-contained release
statement: Each release is proposed as its own contained package with no work bleeding from one phase into the next.

topic: Pause after Phase 1 before Phase 2/3
statement: Waleed recommended pausing after Phase 1 to review before agreeing on Phase 2 and 3 details.

topic: Rep UX via list/console views, custom LWCs in native pages
statement: Rep experience covers list views and console views. Joyce's mockup resembles a Lightning page but is optimistic about native capability; best practice is custom LWCs inside native pages, not fully custom pages.

topic: Flag fraud buttons may need custom
statement: Buttons such as flag fraud might need small custom components, but native options also exist; to be discussed.

topic: Migrate current Google Sheets data
statement: Data migration of WagerTech's current Google Sheets is included in the proposed scope.

topic: Rollout and rep training in scope
statement: Rollout and training the reps are included in the proposed scope, with weekly meetings with WagerTech.

topic: Primary consultant and Slack channel
statement: Proposed delivery model: one day-to-day primary consultant, with Waleed or Miko overseeing, attending weekly calls and active on a shared Slack channel. WagerTech uses Slack.

topic: Decommission old code; client help offered
statement: Jumpr expects to decommission the existing code as part of the build. Emily said WagerTech is open to picking up pieces of that work; Joyce clarified the in-house junior developer could help or ride along.

topic: Include junior developer Eric in meetings
statement: WagerTech's in-house junior developer (Eric) will be included in project meetings to ride along and support later enhancements.

topic: Eric to learn Salesforce via Trailhead
statement: Waleed recommended that Eric start learning Salesforce on Trailhead and work toward Salesforce Administrator certification. No one was assigned to support this.

topic: CEO approval required
statement: The engagement must be approved by WagerTech's CEO; the three attendees are decision makers but not the final approver.

topic: Send concise follow-up summary email
statement: Waleed will send a concise follow-up email in a short format for the CEO, including the phase breakdown and an updated, more realistic timeline with reasons. Due most likely end of day, otherwise next morning; Emily said tomorrow is fine.

topic: Connect with data engineer after alignment
statement: Emily suggested that soon after alignment Jumpr connects with WagerTech's data engineer to find optimization in the first two work streams (project setup/design and object build).

topic: Salesforce storage vs external storage

statement: Emily (Director of Operations) confirmed she will manage the project on the WagerTech side and be the primary point of contact for Jumpr questions. She will not work in the Salesforce back end.

topic: Lina signs off on major milestones
statement: Lina (COO) said her role is key stakeholder who signs off on major milestones and guides operations and process decisions.

topic: Live, clean data; reps sell not admin
statement: Lina said WagerTech wants live, clean data. Brand ambassadors enter data themselves today and are not reliable at it. A goal is for reps to sell and spend less time in Google Sheets.

topic: Joyce to update PRD in Notion
statement: Joyce said some areas were fleshed out or added since the PRD was sent. Kobi asked for the updated version. Joyce will update the PRD in Notion within about a day and message Kobi when done.

topic: Straw's operator data warehouse workstream
statement: Strahinja is working on a data warehousing project: third-party data from operators (casinos), not entered by users, goes into a data store that may link to Salesforce, to validate what sales reps record.

topic: Centralize in Salesforce, retire spreadsheets
statement: The project goal is to bring everything into Salesforce as one central system and retire the Google spreadsheets. Lina said retiring Google Sheets is what she is most excited about.

topic: Dropbox/uploads storage options and recommendation
statement: Kobi said the Dropbox and upload handling needs more discussion, with low cost in mind. Jumpr will look at the options and come back with recommendations; this could be a temporary solution first and a better one later.

topic: Single-entry sign-up logging with fraud flags
statement: Kobi described rep interfaces to log sign-ups more easily, with fraudulent users flagged up front, and one point of entry instead of entering data in several places.

topic: Real-time reporting on sign-ups, referrals, players
statement: Kobi said data in Salesforce will support real-time reporting on sign-up volumes, utilization rates, referral counts and player counts. Report details are to be worked out during design.

topic: Native-first build, flows over Apex
statement: Kobi said Jumpr will keep the build simple and as native as possible, preferring flows over Apex and adding customization only if really needed, so any Salesforce admin can maintain it.

topic: Holistic data model design in Phase 1
statement: Phase 1 includes solution design and data architecture for the whole project, including payouts and deposits. Jumpr might build later-phase objects now for relationships, with their automations and interfaces coming in later phases. This is to be planned after discovery.

topic: Phase 1 core data model components
statement: Kobi listed Phase 1 core data model work: attribution, deal tracking, and intake and lead-to-player conversion (sign-up forms and API endpoints). Jumpr needs to review the sign-up forms and API endpoints that week. He said everything is negotiable.

topic: Sign-up logging UX, fraud flags day one
statement: Kobi called the sign-up logging experience the most important part of the project for rep adoption. He said fraud flags and exception handling are also part of day one, and that the PRD is about 80% there.

topic: PRD phase breakdown: deposits P2, payouts P3
statement: Kobi restated the PRD phases: Phase 1 foundation and sign-ups; Phase 2 deposits, caps and bank transfer tracking; Phase 3 payouts and reporting. These could change after discovery. This differs from Waleed's earlier remark that the second phase covers payouts.

topic: Build everything in a sandbox
statement: Joyce asked about a test environment. Kobi confirmed Jumpr will build everything in a sandbox, because auto-generated IDs and number fields would start counting in production. Joyce accepted.

topic: Iterative testing plus end-to-end test guideline
statement: WagerTech will test components during the build in weekly cycles, followed by full end-to-end testing near the end. Kobi will provide the sandbox and a guideline of what to test.

topic: Reuse WagerTech ERD, propose changes
statement: Joyce asked whether Jumpr would make a separate data model document. Kobi said he will not rebuild from scratch: the existing ERD is 80-90% there. He will propose some changes (for example master-detail vs lookup) for agreement and does not expect major changes. Joyce accepted.

topic: Historical data migration in Phase 1 for go-live objects
statement: Joyce asked to include historical data migration, for example sign-up data in Phase 1 and redeposits and payout tracking later. Kobi confirmed data migration is in Phase 1, at least for the objects that go live.

topic: Possibly load later-phase object data early
statement: Kobi said that if later-phase tables (for example payout objects) are built in Phase 1 for relationships, Jumpr could also load that data, even without automations or validation rules.

topic: Return Salesforce unique IDs to legacy trackers
statement: Waleed said Phase 1 will create the entities (players, operators such as BetMGM) with unique IDs. Jumpr could work with WagerTech to take those IDs back into the existing tracking systems so later data loads do not need remapping.

topic: Payout data may need transformation before import
statement: Waleed warned that payouts (from the Airtable work) may need more objects (helper, rollup, payout lines), so data may need transforming before import. Payout line design may not be known until Phase 2. Data imported early would also need to be kept up to date.

topic: Payouts modeled with payout lines
statement: Waleed said the plan is to model payouts with payout lines, but how payout lines work is still unknown.

topic: WagerTech transforms data; Jumpr imports
statement: Joyce said WagerTech can do the data transformation if Jumpr says what is needed. Jumpr would do the import and make sure the data fits the structure. Waleed agreed.

topic: Iterative delivery, internal UAT, one-week UAT
statement: Kobi described the delivery approach: iterative build with two-week cycles, demos as components are ready, Jumpr internal UAT, about a week of client UAT, then go-live deployment, training and post-go-live support.

topic: Asana for user stories, tasks and updates
statement: Joyce asked whether Asana would hold release notes. Kobi confirmed user stories, tasks and updates will be in Asana, with story-specific communication kept in the Asana tickets.

topic: Set up Slack channel
statement: Kobi will set up a Slack channel for day-to-day communication and add everyone to it.

topic: Train-the-trainer approach
statement: Kobi said Jumpr usually uses train-the-trainer: train a few WagerTech staff who then train the wider team. Sessions will be recorded. Jumpr can also train end users if WagerTech wants. Not confirmed.

topic: Training and go-live at end of Phase 1
statement: Joyce asked whether training and go-live are for all of Phase 1 or for each two-week release. Kobi said they come near the end of Phase 1, once data migration is done and users can move off the spreadsheets. Demos and testing happen during the build.

topic: Involve end users early in demos
statement: Kobi invited WagerTech to bring end users into demos and testing from the start so they know the system before UAT.

topic: Connect Salesforce to redeposit/payout sheets
statement: Joyce said work is needed at the end of Phase 1 to connect Salesforce to the redeposit and payout tracking spreadsheets, because users will still use the redeposit flow and sheets while redeposits are built. Kobi parked it for a discovery session.

topic: Keep systems connected until all flows live
statement: Joyce and Lina said the sign-up, redeposit and referral sheets are linked. Salesforce sign-ups must keep feeding the redeposit and referral tracking until all flows are live, because referrals and redeposits depend on sign-ups.

topic: Google Sheets plugin to sync sign-ups
statement: Waleed suggested a Google Sheets plugin or a Salesforce sign-up report that syncs to the sign-up sheet (for example once a day), so other sheets keep working off it. Users would do sign-ups in Salesforce and the rest in the sheets. The plugin is to be chosen later; more discussion in discovery.

topic: Pull redeposit/referral inputs into Phase 1?
statement: Kobi said that after discovery they should check whether some redeposit and referral input points should come into Salesforce from the start, and adjust timelines. He said it is too early to tell.

topic: Keep phased rollout, early first milestone
statement: Waleed said WagerTech wants a first milestone as soon as possible to get usage, then add more. Each sheet stands alone, so redeposits cannot be partly migrated. Kobi agreed that phasing also stops reps from being overwhelmed.

topic: Shared Google Drive for recordings and docs
statement: Jumpr will set up a shared Google Drive for meeting recordings, documents and deliverables that everyone on the project can access.

topic: Weekly sync scheduling
statement: Weekly syncs start next week at 30 minutes, growing to an hour later for demos. Kobi will send a scheduling link and coordinate after the call.

topic: Jumpr response-time SLA
statement: Kobi stated Jumpr's response time: non-urgent items in one to two business days, urgent items within one day. He said they are usually close to real time on Slack.

topic: Add attendees to Asana board
statement: Kobi will add all attendees to the Asana board after the call.

topic: Tentative Phase 1 go-live August 17
statement: Kobi set August 17 as a tentative Phase 1 go-live date and planned backward from it. Go-live comes after build, UAT, client sign-off and training.

topic: Reporting and dashboards after go-live
statement: Kobi said reporting and dashboards usually start after go-live, because data is needed first (from user activity and data migration).

topic: One-week UAT and sign-off before go-live
statement: Kobi allowed about one week for UAT in the week before go-live, with UAT sign-off hoped for that week and everything ready for UAT the week before. UAT can be extended if needed.

topic: Trial data migration in sandbox first
statement: Kobi usually does a sandbox migration first to find data errors before the production import. This may happen earlier if time permits and the data is complex.

topic: Discovery inputs expected by next Wednesday
statement: Kobi expects to have all the information Jumpr needs by next Wednesday. After discovery he will break the work into user stories and map the build order.

topic: Five-week build; early finish options
statement: Kobi said the build has five weeks and might finish sooner if it sticks to the PRD scope. If so, WagerTech can choose to wait until mid-August, ship early, or bring later phases forward.

topic: Timeline optimism not aligned within Jumpr
statement: Waleed said openly that he is less optimistic than Kobi about the timeline for turning the workflows into a good user experience, and that it is too early to discuss the timeline.

topic: Set up sandbox this week
statement: Jumpr will set up a sandbox this week so work in Salesforce can start.

topic: Extra discovery session on API integration
statement: Only one discovery session is booked. Kobi said at least one more is needed for the API integration and the technical setup already in Salesforce, and Jumpr will set it up.

topic: Follow-up ERD deep dive
statement: Emily said a deeper ERD session will not happen today and a follow-up should be planned. Kobi said it is not urgent and he will set up a call if he has specific questions after learning the process.

topic: Salesforce access and license provided
statement: Kobi confirmed WagerTech has already given Jumpr Salesforce access and a license.

topic: WagerTech reps available for UAT
statement: Kobi asked WagerTech to have a few reps set aside time for UAT in the last week of July or first week of August, and ideally to give early feedback during the build.

topic: WagerTech time needed during discovery
statement: Kobi said Jumpr needs time from WagerTech teams for the next one to two weeks of discovery to finalize the design.

topic: Spreadsheet templates for historical data prep
statement: Once the data model and approach are set, Kobi will create spreadsheet templates for WagerTech to fill in with historical data. He expects them around mid-July.

topic: Separate data store integration with Salesforce
statement: Strahinja asked for a chat about WagerTech's separate data store, which may pull data from Salesforce and in some cases push to it. He wants to confirm the chosen store will not get in Jumpr's way. Kobi suggested covering it in the ERD walkthrough.

topic: Tell Jumpr about ongoing Salesforce work
statement: Kobi assumes the build is more or less from scratch. He asked WagerTech to tell him about anyone currently working on Salesforce, so Jumpr can coordinate and not wipe their work.
