statement: WagerTech will bring its Salesforce administrator (who will take over from Jumpr) in after discovery, not now; the person is still being decided internally. Waleed asked why not now. Emily and Joyce said this was intentional, to keep this round to the main business stakeholders. Waleed accepted.

topic: Review existing Salesforce setup and custom UIs
statement: Kobi wants to go through the current Salesforce setup, including the custom-built UIs, to learn what did not work for the business and avoid repeating it. Emily agreed and said she will probably set up a separate call.

topic: WagerTech to review Asana plan and timeline
statement: Kobi asked WagerTech to look at the Asana project and tell Jumpr about anything glaring, anything they disagree with, or timelines that do not make sense, so the plan can be negotiated and updated. No one confirmed in the transcript.

topic: PRD shortens discovery; decisions are bulk of work
statement: Kobi said most projects take four to five discovery sessions, but the PRD already has the answers and field definitions, so discovery and design should be shorter. He said building objects and fields is not the main effort; deciding the content, workflows and interface is the bulk of the work.

topic: Timeline depends on feedback cycles and UI changes
statement: Kobi said he feels the team may reach the timeline sooner than expected, but this depends on the number of feedback cycles, changes, UI design and simplifications needed.

topic: Joyce leads product management; PRD owner
statement: Joyce (Head of Integration) said she serves a product management function on the project, translating pain points and requirements into technical terms. The PRD came from discovery between Joyce, Emily, Lina and other stakeholders. Emily said Joyce leads from the product side.

topic: Jumpr team roles on the project
statement: Kobi said he is the project manager and primary consultant. Miko is the solution architect. Jester (name as heard) is Kobi's right hand for implementation: configuration, communication, updates and demos.

topic: Follow-up on Ali's trend analysis
statement: Waleed asked to understand how Ali spots trends and rep performance and his blind spots; Ali agreed to set up a call, and Waleed said to bring it up when they meet.

topic: Ali to validate the build
statement: Kobi said Jumpr looks forward to Ali validating the solution once it is built; Ali responded positively but no formal UAT role was set.

topic: Simplified UI for non-CRM users
statement: Reps have little or no Salesforce or CRM experience, so Kobi said Jumpr will want the UI and inputs to be simpler than out-of-the-box Salesforce and will shape training accordingly.

topic: Mobile vs desktop usage
statement: Waleed noted mobile support is a separate workstream and asked the team to call it out early; Owen said ~99% use phones generally, but logging is more split and Jay estimated logging is about 90% on laptop.

topic: Poll reps on logging device
statement: Lina said she will run a poll in the sales chat on device use (mobile vs desktop) for logging.

topic: Mobile logging less required than PRD
statement: Joyce said reps log on desktop mainly because the current Google Sheet process is complex; a mobile-friendly UX could shift behavior, so mobile may not be as required as the PRD initially stated.

topic: Desktop vs mobile trade-offs escalated
statement: Kobi said that where optimizing desktop over mobile creates trade-offs, Jumpr will call it out so the team can decide day one vs later, to keep to the timeline and budget for this phase.

topic: Desktop-first, mobile-compatible build
statement: After Waleed and Joyce discussed supporting both, Kobi stated Jumpr will build desktop first and make sure it still works on mobile; no one objected.

topic: Salesforce user groups
statement: Salesforce users top-down are the operations team, sales (brand) managers, brand ambassadors under them, and the BA's sales assistant if they have one; every BA uses Salesforce.

topic: Brand manager definition
statement: A BA becomes a brand manager only once managing another BA; brand managers remain BAs running their own network. The brand operations team manages brand managers and BAs without a manager.

topic: Brand manager team rollups
statement: Today the team views performance by BA; the ideal state is easier brand-manager rollups (team view of how each brand manager's team is doing).

topic: Hierarchy rollup referrer to ops
statement: Joyce described primary and secondary referrers under BAs and said the Salesforce hierarchy must reflect what needs to roll up; Kobi agreed the key is what rolls up from referrers to BAs, brand managers and operations.

topic: Referrers get no Salesforce access
statement: Only users at BA level or above have Salesforce access; referrers will not have access.

topic: Assistants use BA's license
statement: Lina said sales assistants who log on behalf of a BA would just log in using the BA's license and are not tracked for numbers. Joyce then questioned this (separate role for audit trail) and Kobi said no decision is needed on the call.

topic: Separate assistant role for audit trail
statement: Joyce asked whether assistants should have their own role (within the license cap) so logging history shows assistant vs rep; Emily floated a shared view-only license; Kobi said no decision is needed now but Jumpr needs to know early if an assistant-vs-BA indicator must be designed.

topic: Assistant sign-off comment on logs
statement: As an alternative, Joyce suggested a business rule or comment box so assistants sign off on what they log.

topic: No read-only licenses; platform license option
statement: Waleed said Salesforce does not offer read-only licenses; a platform license could be an option, but the leads object they need for logging is an issue, and shared licenses lose accountability for who made a change.

topic: Deal management possibly phase three
statement: Emily mentioned Owen and Jay's ops and partnership deal management role and referred to it as phase three; this was not confirmed further.

topic: Restrict deal configuration access
statement: Kobi said BAs presumably should not configure deals or operator-deal combos, so access to those objects should be restricted to prevent user errors.

topic: User counts for licensing
statement: Current counts given: 6 brand managers and 22 brand ambassadors (Jay estimated 24, projected about 20).

topic: 30 licenses; 10 ops users
statement: WagerTech has 30 licenses now; about 10 operations users need access who are not also sales; some people will be dual rep and ops.

topic: Add license setup to project plan
statement: Kobi noted Jumpr will add a section to the project plan for getting licenses (account/role setup) set up.

topic: Permission groups and shared ops access
statement: Lina said some ops people could share access and suggested groups: brand ambassador, brand manager, brand ambassador/ops, ops, and maybe an executive layer; whether to split ops further is to be discussed.

topic: Admin vs reporting access in ops
statement: Kobi suggested separating admin-level access from reporting-level (view-all, no record changes) access within ops.

topic: Executive view-only access
statement: Kobi suggested executive-level users get view-only access, mainly for reports and dashboards; Lina said yes. Kobi later said nothing is final and Jumpr will put together a proposal.

topic: Exec reporting vs future BI tool
statement: Kobi noted WagerTech is building a data warehouse; if the eventual plan is a BI tool, executive reporting in Salesforce could be trimmed, but for now executives need read-only access to reports.

topic: Jumpr roles proposal
statement: Kobi said Jumpr will put together a proposal on roles and responsibilities/access for the team to decide on before go-live.

topic: Current book allocation process
statement: Master affiliates offer volume on books; Owen announces it in chat; Ali splits volume per rep based on logging trends, timeliness and redeposits; allocations are tracked in Notion, sent via WhatsApp BA chats, put on the rep's link, and the book is closed in Notion when done. Operators may also warn of caps.

topic: Allocation by player quality and vertical
statement: Ali allocates volume to high-volume BAs and to BAs who bring better-quality players, still gives lower-volume reps opportunities, and matches sports vs casino preference of each BA's network.

topic: Partner type for direct operator deals
statement: Joyce said deals are either direct with an operator or through a partner (master affiliate), and a direct operator relationship was conceived as a partner type too; Waleed had not seen the need for a partner type and said they can talk about it.

topic: Deal = partner+operator+vertical+market
statement: Deal rates depend on the combination of partner (if any), operator, vertical, and market (national or specific states/provinces); verticals must be future-proofed for prediction markets, sweeps and daily fantasy sports.

topic: Operator detailed reports for auditing
statement: Operator detailed reports (no names; FTD amount, registration date, FTD date, bets/hands) are cross-referenced with each BA's unique code and logs to audit player value and tracking; these reports exist only for some operators.

topic: Keep forecast and actual for gap analysis
statement: Signups tracked internally are the forecast; actuals come from operator confirmation. Even after operator integrations, both must be kept to see the gap (logged vs tracked).

topic: Per-operator tracking benchmarks
statement: Each operator has a baseline for expected tracking discrepancy; a sharp drop below an operator's historical benchmark (e.g. DraftKings below ~80%) usually indicates fraud rather than an operator issue.

topic: Internal attribution-gap initiatives
statement: Emily said WagerTech is working on internal initiatives to close the attribution gap, but both sources will always need validating.

topic: Fraud flags and write-off reason codes
statement: Reps need to flag sign-ups as potential fraud (malicious intent) and record write-offs (e.g. locked account, duplicate operator sign-up) as rejections with reasons, with an audit trail; Joyce referenced a reason-code list in the PRD.

topic: Reconcile only on poor tracking
statement: Today ops does not chase the untracked portion for well-tracking reps; they investigate (and may ban a referrer) only when a BA or book is tracking poorly.

topic: Live staged sign-up visibility
statement: Lina wants live data from reps on staged sign-ups (register, deposit, wager, pending verification) so logged vs tracked can be compared daily instead of only before Wednesday pay day.

topic: Link click auto-creates sign-up
statement: Waleed confirmed with Jay that when a player clicks the rep's link, a sign-up is created in Salesforce tagged to the deal; the rep may still add proof and details later.

topic: Unlogged sign-up reminders and SLAs
statement: Jay wants pending sign-ups to act as a reminder to log or write off; Waleed noted timelines allow SLAs (e.g. 24 hours); Jay agreed.

topic: Automated outreach as future phase
statement: Waleed said automated outreach to players (e.g. reminders after sign-up) is something to look into in future phases.

topic: Payouts based on rep logs
statement: Joyce stressed that WagerTech pays based on what the rep logs (forecast), not on operator confirmation, which is why closing the tracking gap matters.

topic: Moving communication into Salesforce
statement: Waleed said WhatsApp is a blind spot for Salesforce and wants to know how far WagerTech is from moving rep-player-referrer communication so it originates from or through Salesforce, to anticipate automations; not to be solved now.

topic: Surface signals to brand managers
statement: Emily said surfacing items needing action or attention to brand managers is top of mind, applies to redeposits, and there is opportunity in the sign-up flow.

topic: No player-communication change in 3 phases
statement: Waleed said he does not expect player communication methods to change in the next three phases; Cases might be a communication method, but this is a design consideration with no real impact on scope or timeline.

topic: Record reconciliation process demo
statement: Kobi asked for a recorded video of the current reconciliation process (spreadsheets, decisions, operator reports vs internal sheets); Emily agreed.

topic: Daily book and link updates
statement: Airtable is updated daily as books are turned on, off or swapped and to record which links each BA has for each operator, so tracking numbers stay accurate.

topic: Show operator the player registered through
statement: When reps are switched mid-month between deals for the same brand (e.g. BetMGM), they must manually change how they log; Ali liked that Salesforce (from his testing) shows which operator the player clicked or registered through.

topic: BA view of own network tracking
statement: Ali mentioned sharing tracking details with BAs so they can see CPAs tracked vs logged in their own network; it is unclear whether this is current or desired.

topic: Two link types
statement: There are two link concepts: the BA-specific agency website link (internal attribution) and operator/partner affiliate tracking links, which can be one per BA or shared across BAs.

topic: Affiliate link allocation and history
statement: Affiliate links from operators/partners are allocated to BAs and added to their agency site; when links are limited they are split or reassigned (avoiding two high-volume reps on one link), and Airtable tracks assignment, unassignment and who had a link previously.

topic: Airtable deal/link setup walkthrough
statement: Ali offered to show his screen; Kobi asked for a screen recording or call next time Ali sets up a deal and distributes links; Ali agreed.

topic: Current click-based sign-up capture
statement: Sign-ups are currently captured on click of a study (mapped to a book) on the agency website; WagerTech is changing to a middleware redirect closer to conversion.

topic: Postbacks cover only 50-60%
statement: WagerTech hopes to integrate server-to-server postbacks with partners and operators but expects at most 50-60% coverage; the rest relies on manual logged-vs-tracked confirmation.

topic: Sign-up-to-API recording
statement: Kobi wants to see how a link click becomes a sign-up record and what data comes with it; Emily said they can send that over, will cover it in the API walkthrough, and can have someone record a sign-up end to end showing the API flow.

topic: Single agency site before go-live
statement: Agency sites use a slug per rep, with US and Canada sites; WagerTech is hopefully migrating to one site for all markets, which should be in place before go-live unless there is a major concern.

topic: Roll up sign-ups per link and rep
statement: Kobi said Salesforce needs to roll up sign-ups per affiliate link (e.g. 20 links on one deal) and per rep, which may need more objects; he will confirm after seeing the full process.

topic: Recordings-first discovery approach
statement: WagerTech will provide recordings, then book follow-ups: a sit-down between Kobi and Ali, and smaller items via Loom; Kobi agreed. Waleed added that a live conversation with Ali (not just a recording) is key.

topic: Record day-to-day spreadsheet workflows
statement: Kobi asked WagerTech to send recordings of other day-to-day spreadsheet work (deal setup, sign-up process, logging) not yet shown; Emily is coordinating Loom recordings.

topic: Send outstanding items list
statement: Kobi will send Emily a list of what was discussed and outstanding items.

topic: Salesforce walkthrough call sooner
statement: Kobi suggested setting up the previously discussed Salesforce walkthrough call sooner while waiting for recordings.

topic: ERD quick connect timing
statement: Kobi said the ERD can wait; Emily suggested a quick connect so 'draw' can validate the database solution on his end and avoid short-term blockers; Kobi acknowledged ('Sure', 'Yes') but no session was scheduled.

topic: Import operator reports; exec reports
statement: Kobi wants to see executive-level data and reporting, whether operator reports can be imported into Salesforce to help reconciliation, and what other spreadsheet-based reports must be supported; via a session or example reports.

topic: Email executive ideal-state mockups
statement: Joyce will email the ideal-state executive reporting mockups.

topic: Kobi-Ali-Jay session Monday
statement: Ali can meet Kobi Monday next week (afternoons work); Jay will join; Emily to help set the time.

topic: Send scheduling link
statement: Kobi will set up a scheduling link and send it to Emily for future meetings.

topic: Discovery done mid next week
statement: Emily said Kobi expects to be through discovery by mid next week (by Wednesday or before), after which design would start; WagerTech will prioritize supporting that.

topic: Ops member logs sign-ups for a BA
statement: Jay (ops/sales hybrid) logs the sign-ups for one of WagerTech's BAs, which Lina called out as important to note.

topic: Current Salesforce instance tested by one BA
statement: Ali has spent time in WagerTech's existing Salesforce instance through their discovery testing and was the BA it was tested with; Salesforce usage among the other reps is low.

topic: BA reporting team needs visualization access
statement: Emily said, besides BAs and ops/partnership deal managers, WagerTech has a BA reporting function that would need access to help with visualization.

topic: Shared licenses and combined permissions
statement: Waleed noted that sharing licenses is not acceptable to Salesforce (though acceptable to Jumpr), and if people share a license the permission design must cover all their jobs rather than one role.

topic: Salesforce player activity as quality signal
statement: Waleed asked if Salesforce player data (sign-ups, deposits, redeposits, payouts) helps judge player quality before operator actuals arrive; Joyce said all of that data is useful but is not held with 100% confidence.

topic: Rep sales pipeline for started sign-ups
statement: Lina said reps may forget people who started a sign-up journey, and having a true sales pipeline would bring them more sales.

topic: Embed operator requirements in reminders
statement: Lina said reps send hundreds of deposit/wager reminder messages and certain requirements do not change, so it would be good to embed them (e.g. bet on sports) in the message. Raised in the context of automated outreach that Waleed placed in future phases.

topic: Varied BA practices slow adoption
statement: Ali said chat automation could be done but would be a process because each BA has their own system, some leave referrers to run the network, and referrers are not all reliable; the same applies to moving off manual logging.

topic: Reps delay or withhold sign-up logs
statement: Ali said some reps complete sign-ups but do not log them, leave them until called out at month end, or deliberately log only part and hold the rest until pay day or the next week, which forces manual audits of sheets and networks.

topic: Agency site sign-up form vs operator form
statement: Kobi asked whether the sign-up form on the agency site is the form players get; Joyce said it is, but it comes through a tagged link and players still complete all the same details. Kobi wants to see it in practice.

topic: Current reporting data hard to access
statement: Emily said WagerTech has some reports but the data is hard to get at, and much analysis is currently done with AI on the data they feed it; there is a lot of opportunity in reporting.

topic: Sample table not needed for migration mapping
statement: Per Gemini notes, Marc suggested requesting a sample table to start migration field mapping; Kobi replied that the PRD already holds the field definitions, so a sample table is less critical for now.

topic: Hesitation on PRD Lead object for signups
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi questioned the PRD's use of the Lead object for signups, because the process involves quick conversion decisions and not lead nurturing.

topic: Interim manual entry from WhatsApp
statement: Per Gemini notes, Marc suggested that manual data entry from WhatsApp information may be needed in the interim until signup data becomes available.

topic: Custom Signup object, record per submission
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi proposed a custom Signup object where every form submission creates a new record that reps work directly (not the Player object), with validation only when a signup is linked to a contact, to avoid deduplication and validation failures. Marc agreed. Internal Jumpr discussion only; no client confirmation.

topic: Composite callout for real-time signup creation
statement: Per Gemini notes, Marc suggested a composite callout so signup records are created in real time, so reps do not need to check whether a signup completed.

topic: Current signup API caller and data location
statement: Per Gemini notes, it is unclear who calls the current API and where the data is stored; a deep dive is to check how signups appear and whether existing builds can be reused instead of a new batch process.

topic: Schedule API signups deep-dive call
statement: Per Gemini Next steps, Kobi is to send instructions to the relevant parties and schedule a deep-dive call on API signups to analyze the data structure.

topic: Vendor writes directly into Salesforce preferred
statement: Per Gemini notes, Marc noted that if the vendor can populate data directly into Salesforce, technical complexity drops a lot compared to an external batch process.

topic: Back-trace existing API integration
statement: Per Gemini Next steps, Marc is to explore the existing interface and API integrations and back-trace the existing API integration to identify the current setup.

topic: Single account for operator and deal levels
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi and Marc agreed internally that a single account will serve both operator and deal levels.

topic: Per-casino and casino-plus-partner reporting
statement: Per Gemini notes, reporting needs one entry per casino and also casino-plus-partner combinations, with both individual and consolidated reporting; the approach (related lists or structural combinations) is not settled.

topic: Console view (Player 360) for signup entry
statement: Per Gemini notes, complex UIs are acceptable for ops teams but the end-user interface must stay simple; Kobi proposed a console view like a 'Player 360' layout for signup forms, so reps can enter deposit information and see related player data.

topic: Design finalization target next Wednesday
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi aims to finalize the design by next Wednesday (about 2026-06-24) to start the build phase.

topic: Schedule stakeholder meetings on workflow gaps
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi plans to send follow-up instructions to schedule meetings with stakeholders to address critical gaps in the current workflow.

topic: Set up sandbox with shared WagerTech login
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi asked Marc to set up a sandbox for the org using the shared consulting+wagertech address instead of the email used for production access, for shared login and verification.

topic: Jumpr access to rep sales spreadsheets
statement: Kobi said Jumpr does not have access to the WagerTech rep sales spreadsheets. Ali was not sure if Jumpr needs them and said it could be figured out later.

topic: API docs: lead logged at study click
statement: Kobi stated that, per the API docs Emily sent (from Ryan), a lead is logged at the time a user clicks a study. He wants to understand how this links back to the rep.

topic: Signup logged once per book
statement: Client described the current process: every registration through WagerTech is logged individually per book, so a person who signs up for three books appears three times, each with the live operator.

topic: One live operator per book per rep
statement: Client described the rule: a rep never has two operators live for the same book (for example Proline GD and Proline C). The company can hold multiple deals for one book at the same time, but each rep is assigned one operator per book.

topic: Target CPA per operator drives rep switches
statement: Client described that each operator deal has a target CPA. Ilas, Owen, Lena and the team decide whether to switch high-volume reps to a different operator to hit targets.

topic: Volume distributed across BAs when deals limited
statement: Client described that when deals for a book are limited, volume is split evenly across BAs or assigned to reps who track well; when volume is plentiful, it is broken down by rep volume and trends.

topic: Reps log by operator after switch date
statement: Client described that sales reps are only told when they are switched to a different operator, and after the switch date they must log signups under the new operator. Reps check Airtable to see their live books and the date they were changed.

topic: Completed signup log fields
statement: Client showed the completed signup log: email, date, referral, referral bonus, and a bet credit option where referrals are paid to deposit into a book they registered for through WagerTech.

topic: Three proof screenshots per signup
statement: Client described three proofs logged per signup: the welcome email (received once the player is verified), the deposit amount screenshot (exact amount sent), and the transaction/wager history.

topic: One account per player per book
statement: Client stated a player cannot have more than one account per book; a person who already registered for a book on their own cannot register for it through WagerTech.

topic: Deposit range per deal, BA picks amount
statement: Client described that each operator deal has a deposit range (for example 50 to 160) maintained manually in Airtable. The BA picks the amount per client within the range and should vary it. The deposit range is per deal and can change month by month.

topic: Wager vertical per deal must match
statement: Client described that the wagering requirement (sports or casino) depends on the operator deal. If a player registers through a sports link but wagers on casino, it will not track and the CPA does not trigger.

topic: PlayCan CMS turns books on/off per rep
statement: Client showed PlayCan CMS, where operators/books are turned on and off on each rep's agency site URL. A book is live on a rep's page only if it is live in PlayCan; PlayCan is what runs everything.

topic: Only managers/ops manage PlayCan links
statement: Client confirmed BAs cannot access PlayCan at all. Only Jay, Ali, Andy and Owen set up links; Lena and Emily rely on them.

topic: Managers own brand sites; reps have own links
statement: Client described the brand model: managers own a brand site (Ashurix is Andy's, not Ali's as first stated) and reps under a manager use that banner but have their own dedicated links and URL slug, so clicks are attributed to the specific rep.

topic: Referral code prefilled from rep slug
statement: Client confirmed rep attribution at signup comes from both the slug link and the referral code: a link such as ashurik.net/alvaro pre-fills the referral field with the rep.

topic: Only rep's active study links shown
statement: Client confirmed that after login and location selection, a player sees only the study links active for that rep at that time; live books differ by rep based on volume and availability.

topic: Airtable master links, tracker codes, effective dates
statement: Client showed Airtable master links: each operator provides a limited number of links, each with a tracker code used to identify the rep in operator reports, and Airtable records effective from / effective to dates for when a link was live, closed or paused.

topic: Airtable first, then PlayCan (fail-safe)
statement: Client stated link assignment is done in Airtable first, then activated in PlayCan; Airtable is meant to act as the fail-safe so incorrect links are not put live in PlayCan.

topic: Manual PlayCan/Airtable sync discrepancies
statement: Client said the process is still manual even with the bot; if someone turns a link on in PlayCan without updating Airtable, discrepancies occur.

topic: Rep mislogging after mid-month operator switch
statement: Client said BAs switched between operators mid-month often log late-completing signups under the new book, causing inaccurate tracking that ops must investigate using welcome email dates.

topic: Log by welcome email date vs switch date
statement: Client explained that signups are supposed to be logged by registration date as shown on the welcome email, compared with the switch date in Airtable; mislogging still happens.

topic: Ali uses Salesforce to see clicked lead
statement: Ali said that since he started using Salesforce it clearly shows which lead a player clicked, which helps him log the right books. He is the only WagerTech user who has been testing Salesforce.

topic: Study clicks create signup records per click
statement: Kobi and Ali confirmed that every study click creates a signup record in Salesforce, including clicks by referrers (not players) and repeat clicks, which Ali said is not as important to WagerTech.

topic: Rework Salesforce to match actual process
statement: Kobi said he wants to focus on the process outside Salesforce so that when Jumpr updates and fixes Salesforce it lines up with WagerTech's actual day-to-day process. Ali replied "All right." No specific change or owner was assigned.

topic: Live links per rep vary; NFL peak
statement: Client said the number of live links per rep varies (two up to six or seven) and depends on the time of year, with the most volume near NFL season.

topic: Owen manages deal updates and extra volume
statement: Client said Owen looks into deals and gets updates (with Jess), and lets Ali know when extra volume is available; it is then assigned to BAs who can handle the volume and track well.

topic: Shared links when operators limit supply
statement: Client said ideally each rep has their own link to track erosion (signups that did not track), but some operators limit links so multiple reps share one link (for example Caesars D1 shared by six reps). Sharing is tracked in Airtable, and attribution then needs manual log checks.

topic: Shared-link attribution via rep slug/site login
statement: Kobi proposed that even on a shared link, Salesforce attribution comes from the rep's slug because the player is logged in on that rep's site; Jay agreed the site knows who clicks the link.

topic: PlayCan does not expose click/signup data
statement: Jay said ops cannot see signups in PlayCan as players click study links; it is easy to implement but was not done because Salesforce was expected to do it. He described PlayCan as archaic and said that is why WagerTech is moving to Salesforce.

topic: API sends click data to Salesforce
statement: Kobi said the API docs indicate PlayCan captures click data and sends it to Salesforce, which would be a good way to check data. Jay said this was added because signups were going missing.

topic: Duplicate rules may suppress lead creation
statement: Kobi said the current setup creates leads directly, and if duplicate rules apply, Salesforce will stop creating records for signups it thinks are duplicates.

topic: CPA triggers only after wagering complete
statement: Client said some BAs complete the full signup up to a week later; if wagering is not completed the CPA does not trigger and the signup cannot be logged as complete.

topic: Missing completed signups in Salesforce week view
statement: Ali said signups completed last week were not showing for that week in Salesforce, unlike the spreadsheet. Ali said it could be resolved later; Kobi said Jumpr will need to figure out what data is being dropped and can troubleshoot later.

topic: Paused link status when volume exhausted
statement: Client said a Paused link status means the link may be opened live again later, for example when a rep used up an assigned amount of volume. Links are paused, not given new rows, when deals end or volume is reached.

topic: Separate links per state for same book
statement: Client explained the same book can have different links per state (for example Hard Rock in Michigan and New Jersey).

topic: Bot-assisted link reassignment with confirmation
statement: Andy described the bot: when moving a rep between operators, it finds the rep's last used or available link, handles link sharing if links are short, and asks for confirmation before changes. Ops then manually copies the link into PlayCan.

topic: Owen loads operator links into Airtable
statement: Jay said operators provide the links, and Owen manually adds the links, books and assignments into Airtable.

topic: New link new row; reactivate existing link
statement: Andy confirmed a new link is a new row on the master sheet; swapping a rep to an existing link pauses the current link and reactivates the previous one. Some reps have static links.

topic: Operator sets volume per link
statement: Client confirmed links are activated for an amount of volume (signups) that the operator specifies.

topic: Resume updates status, no new record
statement: Client confirmed that reactivating a book for a rep in a later month, or resuming a paused link, only changes the status; no new row or new effective-from date is created.

topic: Manual link reassignment to another rep
statement: Jay showed reassigning a link: add an assignment on the rep's page with the link code, it autofills, choose the BA, set effective from today and active, pause it on the previous rep, then add and turn on the link manually in PlayCan.

topic: Pause/resume history lost on shared links
statement: Kobi said resuming by status change loses the history of when a link was paused and resumed, which makes reporting and allocation murky when reps share links. Jay agreed it can cause a real data reporting problem and said Ali has raised it with management before.

topic: Does Airtable store pause history
statement: It is unknown whether Airtable stores pause/resume dates. Andy thinks it shows only effective from/to; Jay thinks the bot can report pauses so the data is stored somewhere; Kobi noted 17 hidden fields may hold it.

topic: Find time with Ilas on Airtable setup
statement: Ali suggested WagerTech may try to find time with Ilas, who originally set up Airtable, to answer questions such as pause history. No owner or date was confirmed.

topic: Previous Assignment field, same casino
statement: Jay said Previous Assignment populates automatically when a rep's assignment is replaced, always within the same casino (for example DraftKings GD to DraftKings CTM), so ops can see who was on a link when tracking reports arrive late.

topic: Priority book designation
statement: Client said books are marked priority or non-priority based on operator perks, benefits, relationship and profitability; higher profit books go to higher-volume reps and lower profit books to lower-volume reps.

topic: WhatsApp switch notices cause logging errors
statement: Client said reps are told of operator switches in WhatsApp, effective the minute the message is sent; reps forget or log late, which causes many incorrect logs.

topic: Signup complete only after proofs submitted
statement: Kobi summarized and Ali confirmed: clicks reach Salesforce or the PlayCan database, but completion is only verified when proofs (screenshots) arrive, mostly via WhatsApp, and are added to the player signup info.

topic: Survey required once per account
statement: Andy said for compliance every client who participates in a study must complete a survey. Kobi asked if it is per person or per study; Andy confirmed it is once per account, after which the user can participate in several studies.

topic: Survey timing before or after study
statement: The timing of the survey is unclear: Andy said clients submit feedback after testing the platforms, and also that users should do the survey before participating in a study.

topic: WagerTech to send challenges for SF design
statement: Kobi asked WagerTech to send any challenges or improvements they want so Jumpr can try to incorporate them into the final Salesforce design. Ali said they will send emails or messages and get back right away.

topic: Kobi to open shared Slack channel
statement: Kobi offered to open a Slack channel with WagerTech; Ali agreed and Jay confirmed the team is on Slack.

topic: Airtable adopted only a few months ago
statement: Ali said WagerTech started using Airtable a couple of months ago. Before that, links were only turned on and off in PlayCan and tracked through messages, which he called a mess.

topic: Stale Airtable statuses show duplicate active links
statement: While reviewing Andy's Airtable records, Ali said that if two different Caesars links show as active, it is because the record was not updated. Airtable link statuses can be stale.

topic: Shared link reassigned mid-month: review both reps
statement: Ali said that when links are shared and one rep is unassigned and another assigned to the same link within the same month, ops must look at both reps' numbers when reviewing tracking. With enough links, a tracker code stays with one rep until that rep is live again.

topic: No click visibility without Salesforce
statement: Ali said that without Salesforce, ops do not know when a player clicks a study; they act only when the referrer sends the welcome email and details. He said Salesforce click visibility is good for leads.

topic: Rep assignment calculation logic not reviewed
statement: Kobi said WagerTech likely runs its own calculation on which rep gets which link and was not sure it needed to be covered now. Jay gave only a high-level rule (low profit books to low volume reps, high profit books to high volume reps). The detailed assignment logic was not walked through.

topic: Postgres chosen for operator data store
statement: WagerTech (Strahinja) will store external operator data in a scale-to-zero Postgres instance instead of Snowflake, because volume is low (high estimate 5 to 10 GB a year) and the main use is reporting. Jumpr agreed Postgres makes sense.

topic: Data flows mostly out of Salesforce
statement: Salesforce is one source for the complete reporting picture. Most of the use case is pulling data out of Salesforce to join with operator data, not feeding data into Salesforce.

topic: Operator data not in Salesforce scope
statement: Waleed restated the earlier position that operator data is messy and is not in scope now; the operator data is organized outside Salesforce (Postgres) and matched to Salesforce player and rep data. Strahinja confirmed.

topic: Match Salesforce sales data to affiliate data
statement: Lina stated the goal: match what Salesforce takes in from sales data to affiliate/operator data and report seamlessly whether they are on track or eroding.

topic: Website insights handled by Strahinja
statement: Emily said website insights married back to operator data will be handled by Strahinja within the Postgres setup.

topic: Reporting/visualization tool not defined
statement: WagerTech has not yet defined the reporting or visualization tool; the current goal is only to get the data pulled in.

topic: Jumpr ensures IDs join across systems
statement: Waleed said a BI tool could join Salesforce and Postgres directly, and that Jumpr's job is to make sure IDs across both systems are logical to join. Joyce accepted.

topic: Joins needed; DataBox weak at joins
statement: Joyce expects WagerTech will need to join data, so loading it into the database makes sense. WagerTech already has DataBox (underused), but DataBox does not join well and recommends joining at the database level.

topic: Postgres path not a blocker for build
statement: Postgres is not a blocker. Worst case, middleware moves Salesforce data into Postgres for joins. Kobi said this makes no difference to the Salesforce build for now.

topic: Joyce to check DataBox agreement
statement: Joyce will check what agreement WagerTech has signed with DataBox, and is open to revisiting DataBox as the end solution.

topic: Jumpr to check DataBox capability
statement: Waleed suggested that he and Kobi look at whether DataBox can do this (the reporting/joins).

topic: Operator data ready before SF model
statement: Strahinja expects the bulk of the operator data to be in Postgres before Jumpr finishes the Salesforce object model.

topic: Player/sales data sourced from Salesforce
statement: Postgres will not have its own player or sales objects; that data is to come from Salesforce. Integration details will be worked out together when needed.

topic: Signups not reaching player database
statement: Joyce reported a data flow issue: some signups do not register in WagerTech's agency-site player database (front-end event tracking or back-end issue), so they never reach Salesforce, although reps' manual tracking shows them. WagerTech is unpacking it.

topic: Historical signups load into Salesforce
statement: Joyce asked whether historical signups load directly into Salesforce or through Postgres. Waleed said probably directly in Salesforce, and Kobi said CSV imports are probably best.

topic: Market object and shared entities
statement: Operator, market and deals are the shared entities between Salesforce and Postgres. Jumpr must discuss with Strahinja whether market is an object or a value. Stronger collaboration is needed when these are built.

topic: Strahinja added to shared Slack channel
statement: Emily added Strahinja to the Slack channel so he has context and can respond when deal/market questions come up.

topic: SF build need not follow client ERD
statement: Kobi will proceed with the Salesforce build without strictly following Strahinja's ERD, share the final data model, and transform later when operator data is joined. Strahinja agreed.

topic: Call out deviations from ERD
statement: Strahinja asked to be told about deviations from his model as work proceeds. Joyce said ideally Jumpr does not deviate much, but WagerTech is open to fundamental model changes with a valid use case.

topic: Consistent naming: signup record, rep ID
statement: Joyce asked that naming stay consistent across systems, for example "signup record" not "lead record", and rep ID rather than BA ID.

topic: Kobi to write object user stories
statement: Kobi will write user stories for the objects to create or update, with field names, API names and display labels, and share them so Strahinja can review. Kobi aims to finish user stories by mid to end of this week.

topic: Mid-build ERD review with Strahinja
statement: Once Kobi is part way through, the team will pause and pull in Strahinja to run through the model and make decisions. This goes into the plan.

topic: Two discovery sessions completed
statement: Jumpr completed two discovery sessions, one on kickoff day and one the day before this meeting.

topic: Build start and first demo target
statement: In progress: document review, follow-up questions and user stories. After review the build starts, with a demo possibly next week or the week after, depending on progress.

topic: Storage decision: keep Dropbox or switch
statement: Storage is a pending decision: keep Dropbox or switch to something else.

topic: Joyce to update PRD
statement: The PRD updates are the only outstanding client input. Joyce will finish them by end of day tomorrow (2026-06-24); they are mostly for later phases.

topic: Payout requirements may change materially
statement: Joyce said the only PRD items that might change materially are payout-related, which is a later phase.

topic: Replace Lead object with signup record
statement: Kobi proposed not using the Lead object (overkill with person accounts and conversion) and creating signup records directly from study link clicks, related to the player. Joyce said WagerTech is not married to Leads and defers to Jumpr's recommendation.

topic: Survey tracking: completed flag plus timestamp
statement: For surveys (not studies), WagerTech only needs whether the player completed it and when. Reps do not need survey contents; it is a compliance check.

topic: Survey contents not brought into Salesforce
statement: Joyce said survey data should be kept elsewhere and does not need to come into Salesforce scope. Monetizing survey data is a separate conversation.

topic: Survey custom object for later phase
statement: Kobi leans toward a lightweight survey custom object (better for API error handling) but said it can go into a later phase and be revisited.

topic: Create signup first, then match player
statement: Kobi described the flow: create a signup record on every inbound API call whether or not a player exists, then a flow matches by email to an existing player or creates one, so API calls are never blocked.

topic: Re-clicks must not be dropped as duplicates
statement: Today a player's repeat click on the same operator link is treated as a duplicate and not registered. Joyce wants repeat clicks reflected because conversion timing is unknown; Kobi agreed.

topic: Resurface one signup on re-click
statement: Joyce's preferred method: a re-click resurfaces the same signup record (timestamp updated, moves to top of the rep's queue) with an audit trail of clicks, instead of separate duplicate rows.

topic: Kobi leans to signup per click
statement: Kobi leaned toward a signup record for every click, with non-completing signups marked not converted (he believed after about three to four days) and moving out of the rep queue, and full history on the player. WagerTech pushed back.

topic: Rep metrics must not penalize later conversions
statement: Joyce said rep reporting must not count a first-click signup as not converted when the player converts later. Waleed agreed and said a signup has a life cycle with defined completion steps.

topic: Every click cannot be a signup
statement: Lina said every click cannot be a signup because people click links without completing; Joyce said there must be an action, such as the rep claiming it, to make it official. Waleed noted non-converted clicks may still be worth keeping as potential future leads.

topic: Contact lifecycle status instead of Lead
statement: Waleed proposed a contact life cycle status (potential player to player) instead of a lead lifecycle; the same signup is tracked and updated until completion converts the contact to a player. Joyce said she was super aligned and Kobi said that's better, but the overall signup model is still pending Kobi's document.

topic: Staging object for every click
statement: Waleed suggested a staging object that captures every click, matched to an existing signup with the same parameters (which is updated). Kobi said that was his fallback too: no click data is lost and one signup holds the history.

topic: Signup uniqueness key
statement: Waleed said a signup is unique by player, operator and deal (book), so a repeat click with the same identifiers could update the existing signup.

topic: Kobi to document signup model
statement: Kobi will write a document of the signup model (including duplicate click handling) for review. He said it is by no means a final decision; the team will confirm before the object is set up.

topic: Duplicate click handling unresolved
statement: Whether each click becomes its own signup record or clicks go to a staging object linked to one signup is not decided; it waits on Kobi's document.

topic: Email is primary player match key
statement: Email is the starting match key for players. Joyce agreed email is a great starting qualifier; Kobi said email is the most reliable because it has one format.

topic: Name/phone fallback matching not adopted
statement: Joyce asked for fallback matching on first and last name and phone number. Waleed said name is not a good match key, and Kobi said names cause wrong matches and phone numbers have format issues.

topic: Fraud: same email, different name
statement: Lina said fraudsters reuse the same email with a different name, which is another reason to want two matching indicators. No direct resolution.

topic: Secondary (e-transfer) email field
statement: Kobi suggested extra email fields on the player record (e-transfer email versus player email) for matching; Lina said there should be a spot for two. The first time, a player may need manual matching to add the second email so future signups match automatically.

topic: Unmatched signups go to rep review queue
statement: If a signup does not match on email, the system does not create or match a player; it creates a review queue item for the rep with likely candidates. Kobi and Lina agreed. This differs from the auto-create-player step Kobi described earlier (line 678).

topic: Kobi to share storage options doc
statement: Out of time, Kobi will share the storage options document for review.

topic: Kobi to recheck Salesforce storage figures
statement: Miko questioned Kobi's Salesforce storage figures and noted file storage and data storage are priced differently. Kobi will double-check the numbers. (Price figures withheld under rule 5.)

topic: Dropbox usage is proofs only
statement: Joyce reported 396.3 GB used in Dropbox, all proofs (including large 4K videos).

topic: Salesforce native storage near term
statement: Kobi asked whether the Salesforce native approach (about 72 GB included) is enough for now, with an upgrade or switch later.

topic: Cloud storage needs custom upload UI
statement: Google Cloud or AWS is cheapest long term, but there is no native Salesforce integration, so Jumpr would build a custom upload UI and new API, possibly reusing concepts from the existing Dropbox upload build. Salesforce native is easiest.

topic: Scope storage with GCP preference
statement: Joyce said WagerTech would probably prefer GCP because they use Google Workspace, and asked Jumpr to scope with that in mind. No final platform selection was made.

topic: Build GCP storage in initial phase
statement: Kobi suggested that, if GCP is the preference, it be built now as part of the initial signup process so it does not change later. Joyce said "Sounds good", but Kobi will first come back with what the GCP interface looks like and cost depends on usage data.

topic: Kobi to outline GCP storage interface
statement: Kobi will tell Joyce what building a Google Cloud storage interface looks like; cost will be estimated once updated usage is known.

topic: Joyce to confirm current storage usage
statement: Joyce will confirm the exact current Dropbox usage (the snapshot may be from May) and check with Emily. Kobi asked to check usage again in a couple of weeks to extrapolate growth.

topic: Deep ERD review deferred
statement: Emily and Strahinja agreed not to do a deep ERD review in this meeting. Strahinja expects to go deeper as more is built in Salesforce.

topic: Current state: study link click creates Lead
statement: Kobi described his understanding of the current state: a study link click creates a Lead record in Salesforce, and a survey completion updates the lead with a survey-completed checkbox. Calls to Salesforce come from the WagerTech back end. The client did not correct this.

topic: Kobi to find SF-to-Postgres loader name
statement: Kobi said he will find the name of a low-cost tool he used before to load Salesforce data into Postgres. (Cost detail and other-engagement reference on the same line withheld under rule 5.)

topic: How ERD deviations get communicated
statement: Strahinja said Jumpr does not need to edit his ERD; if a change is coming, Jumpr can point him to the Salesforce diagram and he will update the ERD. Kobi answered that his user stories (field, API and display names) are a good way to review changes. No single mechanism was confirmed.

topic: Salesforce naming will differ from ERD
statement: Kobi said Salesforce naming conventions (custom field suffix, separate API name and label) mean names cannot match the ERD exactly, and Salesforce will likely end up with many more fields (reporting, formula, display) than the ERD. He left it to Strahinja whether to bring all fields into the ERD. This partly limits the naming-consistency request in item -20.

topic: Existing build lacks design rationale
statement: Emily said the existing build was not meant to work through the bigger model design questions, and WagerTech may not have a sound reason for many existing decisions that Jumpr will question. Joyce said the Lead setup came from the previous developer.

topic: Client feedback on current build not covered
statement: Kobi noted the plan to walk through the Salesforce build and get the client's feedback on what they liked and did not like. The meeting ran out of time after the signup discussion; the transcript shows no such walkthrough in this meeting.

topic: Test name matching with data analysis
statement: Waleed suggested that, if WagerTech really wants name matching, Jumpr could run the client data set through an AI analysis to see how often name matching would have worked. No one took this up.

topic: Reduce proof storage cost to minimum
statement: Joyce said WagerTech wants to bring its current proof-storage (Dropbox) cost down as far as possible and asked Jumpr for a specific recommendation based on actual usage. (Figures withheld under rule 5.)

topic: Joyce sent Dropbox usage and licenses
statement: During the meeting Joyce sent Kobi the exact Dropbox usage amount and the number of licenses.

topic: Staging object replaces Lead for signups
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi and Marc agreed internally to stop using the Lead object for WagerTech signups and use a staging object, tentatively named "study link clicks", to capture user clicks and relate them to signups. Gemini lists this under 'Aligned' decisions; no transcript confirms it and no client confirmation is recorded.

topic: Record-triggered flow instead of batch class
statement: Per Gemini notes, Marc suggested a record-triggered flow rather than a batch class for the study link clicks object, and Kobi supported it because volume is unlikely to need high-performance processing immediately. Gemini Decisions also says the object deduplicates signup records via flow automation.

topic: Client owns API error handling and retries
statement: Per Gemini notes, Marc advised that the client should handle API error handling on their side because they use a standard Salesforce API that returns status codes and record IDs; Kobi agreed the client can monitor their interface and re-sync records that fail. This is an internal Jumpr position; no client acceptance is recorded in this doc.

topic: Kobi to draft signup spec and stories
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi will draft a specification for handling unique link clicks and signups, and finalize the signup specifications and user stories for team review.

topic: PRD vs current org: automations obsolete
statement: Per Gemini notes, Marc presented an analysis comparing the PRD to the current WagerTech Salesforce org and noted that many automations and flows are obsolete.

topic: Clean existing org or start fresh
statement: Per Gemini notes, it is open whether it is more efficient to clean the existing WagerTech org or start with a fresh org; process builders, validation rules and other automations need review first.

topic: Kobi to check fresh-org feasibility internally
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi will consult the internal team on whether a fresh Salesforce org is more efficient than cleaning the current WagerTech org.

topic: Marc to compare GCP vs Salesforce storage
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi assigned Marc a cost-benefit analysis of GCP storage versus native Salesforce file storage for WagerTech, with implementation estimates for both options so the client can see upfront versus long-term impact.

topic: Marc to assess Platform vs Cloud licenses
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi assigned Marc to assess the functional implications of Platform licenses versus Salesforce Cloud licenses and whether current requirements support that switch.

topic: Recommend Platform Plus licenses
statement: Per Gemini notes, Marc recommended Salesforce Platform Plus licenses for WagerTech to support 110+ custom objects, as a hybrid: about five full licenses for admins and integration users, the remaining 25 users on Platform Plus. Gemini lists this as an aligned recommendation to the client, not a client decision.

topic: Include Lightning Console in architecture
statement: Per Gemini notes, the team agreed the Lightning Console is needed for usability even if it adds licensing cost; Marc will investigate console availability and pricing for Platform license users.

topic: Investigate console availability for Platform users
statement: Marc to investigate Lightning Console availability and pricing for Platform license users.

topic: Video comparing console vs standard view

statement: Kobi will load sample data (operators/deals) to review, and so the client can see data and reports in the sandbox.

topic: Operator view is a dashboard of inputs
statement: The operator view is a dashboard of existing inputs, not a place to add more data; operators are configured once and then rarely changed.

topic: Operator sales pipeline later

Emily said she does not disagree with the approach.

topic: Optional flag for players who are users
statement: Kobi offered to add a flag on players who are also users, if wanted.

statement: Unique logins for BA assistants (even with lower permissions, for audit) are ideal, but depend on how many users WagerTech's current Salesforce agreement allows; Joyce expects shared logins. User count needs scoping; agreement details to be discussed with Lina.

statement: Emily asked about uploading proofs outside Salesforce and pushing a reference back. statement: Open: whether the payload's book ID maps to a deal, a deal assignment or a deal rep assignment; may need to be broken out if more granular.

statement: Profiles and permission sets will differentiate an admin/ops view (everything) from a simpler sales rep view; WagerTech asked what the reps should be shown, since showing everything overwhelms them.

statement: Reps would work from list views (for example new players that have not completed signup) as queues, replacing manual entry in their spreadsheets.

statement: All signups are created with status New; per the PRD, if nothing is logged within 3 days the signup is automatically marked past due/overdue. Reps add first-time deposits and other information to progress the signup.

topic: Seamless signup logging is biggest hurdle

statement: WagerTech raised analysing when players are most active to time re-engagement; this is not done today. Jumpr noted player-signup relationships allow rollups (first signup time, signup counts) and list views to support it.

statement: Currently reps manually tick proof checkboxes, which drive the proof completion status (e.g. partial); upload interfaces are not built yet.

statement: Discussions are ongoing about an interface to upload through Salesforce that would hook into Google Cloud Platform 'potentially' for storage, eliminating Dropbox.

statement: WagerTech is piloting server-to-server postbacks (URLs, click IDs, dynamic URL-parameter reporting); those events need to be stored against the signup.

statement: Jumpr suggested replacing manual status edits with a 'move to next stage' button backed by screen flows that require stage-specific information before the transition.

statement: WagerTech wants Won't Do and Fraud consolidated so reps do not choose between two options; Jumpr agreed, modelling it like closed-lost with a loss reason (fraud or other) to track root cause.

topic: Fraud button with required reason built
statement: The sandbox build has a Fraud button on the signup that requires a reason and updates the signup status to fraud (shown in the demo).

topic: Fraud flag manual vs automated
statement: Won't Do was planned to be set manually by the rep, while the fraud flag could be a mix of manual and automated, with fraud as one of the reasons. No final direction beyond the consolidation item.

statement: Someone suggested an initial In Review status so ops can confirm fraud before the signup is closed as fraud/won't do; Jumpr said it could do that.

statement: There is no logic yet to roll a signup fraud flag up to the player; it can be added, dependent on reason code (e.g. edited screenshots = banned, lesser offense = watch list), with the logic to be supplied by WagerTech.

topic: What happens to banned/flagged players
statement: Still to decide what happens at the player level once a player is banned or flagged for fraud.

topic: Deal fields configured from PRD
statement: The deal record has partner, operator, market, country, state, effective date, deal version, vertical and cap (from the PRD), with bonus details and deposit amount now trackable.

topic: Guided flow for deal creation
statement: Jumpr suggested a guided process for deal creation, similar to signup, that walks users through key fields.

topic: Cap with unlimited option
statement: The PRD calls for the cap to allow 'unlimited'; Jumpr suggested a CPA target type picklist (numeric or unlimited) that blanks the numeric field when unlimited.

topic: Reps see only their own records
statement: WagerTech confirmed sales reps must only see their own records (a 'deal breaker'); org-wide sharing should be private.

topic: Sync rep field to owner for sharing
statement: The owner field is not yet used for reps; Jumpr suggested having the separate rep field update the owner so ownership drives privacy, with managers able to see their team's records.

topic: Team reporting for managers
statement: There will be reporting for managers covering people in their teams, but not full back-end access; what data they see is to be figured out.

topic: Primary and secondary referrers tracked
statement: Referrals and referrers are tracked for signups, with a concept of primary and secondary referrers.

topic: One DRA per rep per deal, history child
statement: Instead of a new Deal Rep Assignment row for each assignment event, there is one DRA record per rep per deal, with assignment history captured in a related child object, as discussed the day before.

topic: Signups linked to rep's DRA
statement: Each study-link-click signup will be associated to the respective rep's assignment for that deal, allowing all-time signup rollups per assignment.

statement: Deal-level caps are divided among reps (e.g. 200 split into 50s). Enforcing per-rep caps with notification was not scoped until phase 3/4; Jumpr suggested discussing and including it.

topic: DRA system of record: CMS or Salesforce
statement: Assignment happens in the CMS, not Airtable. Options: Salesforce pushes assignments to the CMS, or the CMS creates DRAs in Salesforce (Jumpr has no problem with that if all IDs are provided). WagerTech needs to talk it through internally.

statement: Deal rep assignment, originally phase 4 in the PRD (with its automations and affiliate links, after payouts and redeposits), was brought ahead so signups can be mapped to the deal rep, since it is part of the signup flow. statement: It is too early for reps; the WagerTech core team will play with the UI and give feedback first, then Eric and Jay (sales side) together. Jumpr cautioned screen flows should be worked through before reps get it.

statement: WagerTech will email Jumpr the details for Eric and Jay so they can get access, in addition to the three core team members.

statement: A Monday start for Eric was raised; readiness for Monday was questioned and screen flows may need work before reps get access. It was noted that it is July 8, so integration and feedback must happen early or there will not be time to rework before end of July.

topic: Simplified rep view before screen flows
statement: Suggested sequence: one first pass to clean out fields and create a simplified view (no screen flows yet), then reps work with it, then build the guided flow. Jumpr said this is quick for it to do.

topic: Hybrid rep/ops user informs UI early
statement: WagerTech has access to a rep who also works on the ops side and could inform the UI; involving him as early as possible was suggested. Not confirmed as a named tester.

topic: Phase 1 on track for end of July
statement: Phase 1 (the signup logging process and all supporting objects) is still on track, assuming the API work, storage and feedback come through.

topic: Phase 1 depends on API, storage, feedback
statement: Phase 1 delivery depends on the API integration working out, the storage solution being settled, and WagerTech feedback.

statement: Scoping starts later this week on keeping Phase 1 connected to spreadsheets not yet migrated (e.g. redeposits); worst case, Salesforce reports exported to the spreadsheets via a Google Sheets add-on.

topic: Research sprint for later phases
statement: Toward the tail end of Phase 1 (in a week or two), start scoping deposits and payouts, and run a research sprint for later-phase PRD items.

topic: Deposits/payouts core objects straightforward
statement: Jumpr expects the core object and components for deposits and payouts to be fairly straightforward to scope, roughly a week to a week and a half.

topic: Order of redeposits vs payouts
statement: Jumpr suggested redeposits first then payouts, moving everyone off Google Sheets for each, but said the order is up to WagerTech.

topic: Sprint-based delivery after Phase 1
statement: After Phase 1 go-live, delivery moves to sprint-based releases by functionality (e.g. redeposits, then payouts) instead of large phases; WagerTech confirmed it is aligned.

topic: Discuss affiliate links this week
statement: Affiliate links are a big part of the signup process and need a separate discussion this week; affiliate link management is also in the later-phase research list.

statement: WagerTech asked for bi-weekly documented release notes once the initial build is done and sprints start; Jumpr agreed and said it usually provides videos.

statement: End of July: signups into Salesforce and reps logging there; deposits hopefully in September; payouts hoped for November. The timeline depends on how much build and customization is needed.

statement: Phase 1 covers signups, logging and deal configuration, not notifications; notifications and reports are not explicitly scoped into Phase 1, but the speaker suggested adding a light version.

statement: WagerTech had confused Jumpr's phase numbering with WagerTech's own PRD/BRD phase numbering; the timeline walkthrough was used to align them. Phase numbers in other sources may not mean the same thing.

statement: The idea is that Airtable can be decommissioned by the end of 'our phase three', and Dropbox as soon as the new storage solution exists.

statement: Per Gemini notes, most of the WagerTech 'PC' stories and recent changes were complete as of 2026-07-09.

The actual direction cannot be established from this doc.

statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi was concerned about giving users full admin rights, and the team discussed a specific permission set that lets authorized users override validation rules instead.

topic: Banner LWC for dynamic record alerts

topic: Scope fraud flagging for sign-ups and players

statement: The planned custom work for the storage options is mainly Apex-driven API callouts to Google Cloud Platform (GCP) to do the upload.

statement: The team said WagerTech's developer is supposed to create sign-up records in Salesforce, and Jumpr's side is to process the payload when the record is created.

topic: UAT end of July, go-live August

topic: Initial build to finish end July
statement: The near-term WagerTech need is to finish the initial build by the end of July.

topic: Client wants November go-live
statement: The team said WagerTech wants to go live in November. This appears to be the end of the full roadmap; elsewhere the team targets sign-up go-live in August.

topic: Roadmap includes redeposits and custom objects
statement: The team said the coming WagerTech roadmap includes redeposits and a couple of other custom objects.

topic: Sign-up live by end of August
statement: The team's internal target is that by the end of August WagerTech is live in Salesforce for the sign-up process and the build of the next process has already started.

Kobi said Jumpr gave the client the pros and cons and the client made the decision. The transcript does not clearly say which option was chosen or which field it was for.

statement: Kobi will finish and send a draft document on fraud tracking: what happens to the related player when a signup is flagged as fraud, for each player status, before automations are added.

topic: Reporting feed into Google Sheets later
statement: Kobi will scope the reporting feed into Google Sheets, probably not this week but maybe next week, because the team is finalizing the build first.

statement: Kobi shared with Joyce a spec document on how signups are created from study click links, for the API developer. He offered a walkthrough call if needed.

statement: Emily said WagerTech is rebuilding the CMS. The developer demo is Friday and testing can start early next week. The developer will build to the spec.
