statement: Kobi said the API payload fields came from the PRD and the current PlayCan version and are not set in stone. The data available in PlayCan and what is sent to Salesforce can be balanced.

topic: Deal ID: none sent; SF-generated ID option
statement: Emily said WagerTech is not sending a Deal ID. Kobi said Salesforce can match deals from operator, partner and market fields, or Salesforce can generate a Deal ID that PlayCan stores in a field. Emily took the Deal ID option away to decide; it is not final.

topic: Deals not created from study click links
statement: Kobi said deals are assumed to be created first in Salesforce. The SLC payload is used to find the rep, player, operator/partner/vertical, deal and deal rep assignment and link the signup. Creating deals from SLCs was not scoped.

topic: GCP proof storage on hold one week
statement: WagerTech asked Jumpr to hold the GCP proof storage decision while it scopes a new internal fraud-detection tool and timeline. WagerTech will give its internal decision by next week.

topic: Ideal state: tool sends completion statuses
statement: Emily said that if WagerTech builds the new tool, the tool would send Salesforce proof completion statuses, and Salesforce would not do storage and upload. She leaned toward sending information through the API.

topic: Proof checkboxes stay; no proof files in SF now
statement: For now the existing proof checkboxes on signups stay, set by reps or by API. Emily confirmed that proof files are not required in Salesforce at this time.

topic: About two weeks left to UAT done
statement: Kobi said there are about two full weeks left before UAT is supposed to be done. Emily said there are only two weeks left in this phase build.

topic: Storage delay risks GCP route this month
statement: Emily said a delayed decision will have impact if WagerTech chooses Google Cloud Storage. Later Kobi flagged that if there is no decision soon and GCP is still needed, storage is at risk for this month.

topic: Three URL fields to paste proof links
statement: Kobi offered three URL fields on the signup so reps paste Dropbox proof links as they do in Google Sheets, as a bridge. Lina said it would be a good bridge if not a big lift. Emily framed it as 'if needed' after the decision next Tuesday, and Kobi closed with 'leave it as these three check boxes for now' until next week.

topic: Revisit proof direction next week
statement: Kobi said proofs stay as the three checkboxes for now. Next week the team will decide whether to build GCP, something else, or bring proof info from an external API.

topic: Automated fraud detection sets Flagged for Review
statement: Emily said, to be confirmed, that an automation would detect possible fraud and trigger a flagged-for-review status.

topic: Only Ops can unflag flagged signups
statement: Lina said, not fully confirmed, that when a signup is flagged only Operations can unflag it. The BA sees it greyed out and cannot bypass it.

topic: Mapping external fraud-tool results to signups
statement: Kobi said that if the external fraud tool updates Salesforce, it must identify the signup record. If not, Salesforce must match on payload fields like the SLC process, which is extra work. Emily will take this back to Joyce.

topic: Two and a half weeks may be tight
statement: Kobi said that with two and a half weeks left, a major build for fraud flagging may be tight.

topic: Status set: remove Won't Do and Flag
statement: Kobi restated last week's decision: signup statuses are New, In Progress, Completed, Won't Do and Flag; Won't Do and Flag are removed and a Flagged for Review status with a reason code is added.

topic: Lock flagged record; unflag returns to In Progress
statement: Kobi said the record could be locked for reps so only Ops can clear Flagged for Review. Lina said Ops would probably move it back to In Progress so the rep still marks it complete. Kobi said that works and he will scope it and show it next call.

topic: Read access to signup sheet and Airtable
statement: Kobi asked for read access to one example signup logging spreadsheet and to the Airtable assignment tables, for historical migration and mapping. No one on the WagerTech side explicitly took the action.

topic: Airtable assignment IDs as external IDs
statement: Kobi said the Airtable master assignment list has a column that looks like unique IDs, probably for deal rep assignments. If still relevant, those IDs might be used for mapping from Airtable.

topic: Proof-submitted fields in CMS API
statement: Joyce said that if Jumpr adds proof-submitted data fields to the API ticket, WagerTech can include them in the CMS database structure it is revising.

topic: Two-way CMS-Salesforce connection
statement: Signups live in Salesforce and nothing passes back to the CMS today. Joyce wants a two-way connection regardless of the proof approach. Kobi agreed in principle; it needs a CMS REST endpoint and he will say if extra stories are needed.

topic: External IDs follow CMS ERD
statement: Kobi expects external IDs (for example players and rep mapping) to connect CMS and Salesforce records. Joyce said the CMS structure will follow the ERD and players will have their own IDs.

topic: Single API requirements doc to Straw
statement: Kobi shared one document with everything needed from the API, to use as the working starting point. Joyce asked that Straw sees it; Emily agreed. Owner is not explicit.

topic: Program split; dual-system cutover period
statement: Kobi said the program value (for example the BetMGM-style operator+partner combo) will be split into two fields. How reps manage both Salesforce and the old sheets/Airtable during the in-between period must be discussed.

topic: Import spreadsheets after fields finalized
statement: Kobi will not import data now. He will prepare import spreadsheets for confirmation after fields, objects and SLC intake are finalized. Historical import is not the next step.

topic: Historical player import depth
statement: Emily asked if launch includes all historical signup data. Kobi recommended importing players at least as far back as relevant to avoid duplicates and keep rep ownership. Emily and Lina said player stealing is not a concern; the cutover is.

topic: Cutover: in-flight signups seen as net new
statement: Emily said that at cutover, items started in the spreadsheet could appear net new in Salesforce, or a book could be added to a player not found in Salesforce. Cutover needs planning.

topic: Import approach for players, signups, deals
statement: Kobi proposed: players by spreadsheet; signup history is the bigger job; half-done signups need a manual rep path or player import; historical signups and rep assignments must relate to imported deals; multi-step import; import as far back as relevant.

topic: WagerTech reviews player/operator/partner fields
statement: Immediate next step: WagerTech reviews player accounts, operators and partners in the sandbox, checks fields and statuses against PlayCan and the PRD, and gives feedback per screen. Emily said they will prioritize the review.

topic: Country/province stay free text
statement: Player country and province are free-text because the data comes from the WagerTech back end; picklists could make SLC mapping fail.

topic: Field formats change only on client feedback
statement: Kobi said all fields are changeable but only when WagerTech asks; Jumpr will not change formats such as the state and country picklist without a request.

topic: Flag missing functional fields vs PRD
statement: Jumpr implemented only fields used in this phase, not the full PRD. WagerTech should report any field missing that is critical to signup logging, completion, proofs or fraud.

topic: CPA per deal visible on operator view
statement: Joyce wants deal-level data such as CPA per deal visible on the operator record and will give it as feedback. Kobi said a related-list column is easy; rollups like total deals need scoping.

topic: CPA stays at deal level, not from operator
statement: Kobi checked if Joyce meant last week's default CPA passed down from the operator. Joyce confirmed no; CPA stays at the deal level.

topic: CPA target type field: numeric or unlimited
statement: A CPA Target Type field will be added. If Unlimited, the CPA target field is greyed out; if Numeric, it is editable. Calculations use both fields.

topic: Reps see only their assigned deal target
statement: Miko asked for views by persona. Lina said reps only need their specific assigned deal target and progress, not CPA or other deal details.

topic: Rep screens: Signup list and DRA list
statement: Kobi said reps would mainly work from the Signup tab and the Deal Rep Assignment list view filtered to their own assignments, with fewer fields on the signup. Lina agreed.

topic: Four permission levels; reps cannot edit operator/partner
statement: Per the design document there are four permission levels (rep, manager, ops, admin). Reps can access their signups and upload proofs but cannot edit operator or partner information.

topic: Persona field access via screenshots
statement: Kobi asked WagerTech to screenshot each object and mark each field by persona (rep, manager, ops, admin) and read/write. Lina said the first step is to decide what reps should see.

topic: Working session to theory-craft deal assignment entry
statement: Miko suggested walking the deal assignment user journey (for example splitting a large set across reps). Emily will book a working session with Joyce; Joyce offered as early as tomorrow.

topic: Manual DRA splitting is tedious
statement: Miko said with the current setup, splitting a deal across five reps means creating five records under the deal, which is tedious.

topic: Rep-level monthly CPA targets and caps
statement: Emily asked for monthly, date-ranged targets at rep level rolled up for reporting. Kobi said it is only at deal level now, not in phase 1 currently; it could be added on the DRA or a child object if scoped, and might fit in the two weeks.

topic: One DRA per deal-rep with status child
statement: The original design had a new deal rep assignment per assignment period. Per last week, it is one record per deal-rep combination, with a child object tracking status history.

topic: Emily to sketch reporting needs
statement: Miko suggested Emily visualize the reporting she needs so Jumpr can work backward from the data model to find missing data.

topic: This week: sharing, DRA UI mockup, fraud doc
statement: Kobi said Jumpr is finalizing sharing rules, permission sets and roles, will create a DRA UI mockup or proof of concept this week, and is writing the fraud tracking doc. Not blocked.

topic: Weekly sync for status; separate solutioning sessions
statement: Joyce proposed the weekly meeting covers roadmap, status and blockers, with dedicated meetings for big bodies of work like fraud. Kobi agreed.

topic: Possible Friday session: API and fraud
statement: Joyce offered Friday for a working block. Kobi will meet Friday on API/SLC if answers are ready and send the fraud tracking doc ahead; a meeting will be scheduled if worthwhile.

topic: Referral Bonus Amount field on signup
statement: Lina asked for a Referral Bonus Amount field on the signup with a set list of options. Kobi said it is not there yet and he will write the user story and add it at signup level.

topic: Bonus automation later; manual entry now
statement: Lina said automating the bonus from the payment matrix could come later; for now reps input the amount, as free text or a drop-down of the fixed amounts. Kobi will use a drop-down.

topic: Referral is signup-level, optional, consistent amounts
statement: The bonus options are the same for all signups and books. Referral data is at signup level and is not mandatory; direct BA signups have no referral. The bonus also feeds total acquisition cost.

topic: Referral Information section on signup
statement: Kobi proposed a Referral Information section on the signup holding referral fields (currency, bonus drop-down). Lina agreed and asked for the secondary referrer there, with separate signup details and referral details.

topic: Secondary referrer threshold payout
statement: Lina said a secondary referrer is paid after hitting 10 referring signups (Canadian side). The secondary referrer goes in the referral section.

topic: Lina posts payment matrix in Slack today
statement: Lina will post the referral payment matrix in the shared Slack channel today.

topic: Fixed, manually updated FX rate to CAD
statement: Lina wants reporting to auto-convert FX to CAD. Kobi said Salesforce uses a static configured exchange rate. Lina confirmed a fixed rate WagerTech decides, and Emily said it is manually updated.

topic: Write-up: bonus picklist feeds currency field
statement: Kobi said the bonus amount will probably be a picklist that updates a currency field; he will flag how it works in the write-up and noted that the amount must roll up.

topic: Referral currency independent of signup currency
statement: A US signup can have a Canadian referral payout and vice versa. Referral fields will be standard number fields with Referral Currency deciding USD or CAD; the signup base currency governs signup amounts.

topic: Signup base currency from API or state/country
statement: The signup base currency will come from the currency in the API or be derived from the state/country in the API.

topic: Survey completion needs separate back-end callout
statement: Survey completion is at player level. SLCs do not confirm survey completion, so WagerTech's back end must send a separate update; Kobi scoped this as an optional phase 1 story. Emily said WagerTech will take a look.

topic: Referrer not in payload; rep selects via lookup
statement: Emily said the referrer will not come from the payload. She wants a lookup, not free text. Kobi confirmed the referrer field is a lookup the rep must pick.

topic: Player and Referrer separate record types
statement: Not all referrers are players. Player and Referrer stay separate person-account record types; the same person can have both. Emily agreed they must be separate.

topic: Restrict new-account choice to Referrer
statement: Kobi will look into restricting the new-account option in the referrer lookup to the Referrer record type; fallback is a guided button.

topic: Screen flow to link player as referrer (V1)
statement: Kobi proposed a screen flow to create a new referrer or pick an existing player, creating and linking the referrer record. Lina agreed. Kobi will scope it, build after fields are final, and include it in V1 but not in the testing build.

topic: Crawl-walk-run: manual first, automate later
statement: Kobi said many steps are manual on purpose; automations come after fields, timing and reporting are approved. WagerTech should flag 'too many steps' in feedback. Emily agreed.

topic: Lina access today; watch Loom video
statement: Kobi will give Lina access before end of day, and asked her to watch the Loom video on first-time org use.

topic: Feedback channel: Asana triage or shared doc
statement: Kobi offered two options for feedback: cards in Asana triage, or a Google doc/spreadsheet as staging, which he would move into Asana. No choice was made in the meeting.

topic: Feedback priority: signup, SLC, deal assignment
statement: Kobi said the top feedback priorities are signup, study click links and deal assignment, because they affect automations; descriptive fields are lower priority.

topic: Sandbox access: Emily added, Straw resolved
statement: Kobi said he added sandbox access for Emily (email from Salesforce). Straw had trouble logging in and that was resolved. Kobi did not know if Joyce had logged in yet.

topic: Hold API until Friday/Monday; spec to Slack
statement: Emily asked the team to hold on the API until Friday/Monday and then reconvene. She will make sure Joyce sends the spec over, and asked Kobi to also put the spec in the Slack channel.

topic: URL fields quick; GCP needs custom UI
statement: Kobi said adding the URL fields is very quick (he could do it after the call), and API-fed proof checkboxes are simple enough to do even in the last week. GCP storage is much more work because it needs a custom UI and API callouts.

topic: Editable vs formula/automated fields
statement: In answer to Joyce, Kobi said fields with a pencil are editable on the record; Player ID is a formula field, and the signup Proof Completion Status is not editable because it is automatically driven.

topic: Record referral type, amount and paid date
statement: Lina said there are two referral types (referral bonus/redeposit or cash back/bet credit) and reps need somewhere to record the referral type, the amount sent, and when it was paid. Kobi said referral type and bonus amounts are not added yet and he could write the user story; the paid date was not addressed.

topic: Referral tracking automation in later phase
statement: Lina understood referral tracking is in a different phase. Kobi confirmed the referral object exists but there are not many referral automations now; referrals can be imported manually.

topic: Marc to review WagerTech API document
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi shared an API document for the WagerTech project and asked Marc to review it for potential issues. The Next steps list labels the same action as the 'Octo' API documentation.

topic: GCP integration likely dropped, decision Monday
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi said Jumpr is likely not moving forward with the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) integration in Salesforce, with a final decision expected by Monday (2026-07-20 if the next Monday is meant). Not a confirmed decision.

topic: Fallback: proof URLs in three custom fields
statement: Per Gemini notes, if GCP is not used, the team plans to store proof URLs in three custom fields to simplify the process. This is a contingent plan, not a confirmed decision.

topic: Kobi to clean up WagerTech board
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi will confirm the list of completed WagerTech story components by reviewing the board.

topic: Marc to list built components in stories
statement: Per Gemini notes, Marc will provide a list of the components he created in the comments of the WagerTech stories.

topic: Fraud and migration talks next week
statement: Fraud was deferred to Monday / early next week, and historical migration approach will be discussed early next week once WagerTech has more context.

topic: Emily feedback tracker not fully reviewed
statement: At the start of the meeting Kobi said he had not yet gone through all of Emily's feedback tracker; they agreed to go through it on the call.

topic: Condense views for rep adoption
statement: The PRD fields are to be captured as data, not necessarily surfaced to users. WagerTech wants condensed, more digestible views built from the rep's point of view first.

topic: Apply end-user lens before client review
statement: WagerTech expects Jumpr to apply the end-user (rep) lens to the other screens before WagerTech takes time to review them. Kobi agreed.

topic: Current screens are admin view
statement: Kobi stated the screens shown so far are the admin view with all fields for this phase. Role-based page layouts and permission sets can tailor and hide fields for reps.

topic: Tooltips and remove duplicate fields
statement: Even for admins, screens should use hints or tooltips (for example to mark a section as read only) and remove duplicate fields that appear in different blocks.

topic: UI labels match ERD and dictionary
statement: UI labels must line up with the ERD and data dictionary. Legacy labels from the existing API (for example 'book name') are to be replaced to match the go-forward model.

topic: Build in week two
statement: Joyce stated the project is about week two going into the build.

topic: Build is starting point, client drives customization
statement: Kobi said the current build is a starting point to work from, and WagerTech is welcome to drive the customization from here. Joyce accepted. (Open-ended; see the scope check at item -61.)

topic: Mockup is AI prototype, feasibility unverified
statement: Joyce's mockup is a Claude-generated clickable HTML prototype, not real code, and covers only the click/lead and signup screens. Joyce said its Salesforce-native feasibility is not verified and it is a starting point for Jumpr to correct.

topic: Rename study link clicks to leads
statement: Joyce proposed calling study link clicks 'leads' and calling repeat attempts on the same player/deal/market combination 'clicks' (many clicks per lead). Kobi deferred feedback; no explicit agreement on the naming.

topic: Lead queue statuses For Review and Archived
statement: In Joyce's mockup the lead queue has only 'For review' (default for new clicks) and 'Archived' (not a real signup but kept for record). Later superseded in direction by the single-object status model.

topic: Names not IDs in queue
statement: The queue should not show record IDs. It should show player first and last name plus the operator and partner combination.

topic: Recency ordering with relative dates
statement: Joyce proposed ordering the queue by recency, showing relative dates (for example '5 days ago') up to one week, then the actual date.

topic: Lead detail shows attribution and key player info
statement: The lead detail panel should show attribution and quickly relevant player information (signup date, age). Deeper player details (address, postal code, city) are seen by clicking through to the player record. Joyce said the field list still needs pressure testing.

topic: Click history reorders by latest click
statement: A history list should show all clicks with the same permutation, and the lead should move to the top of the list on the most recent click attempt.

topic: Lead actions archive or progress
statement: In the mockup the lead record is clearly read only, and the rep either archives it or progresses it to signup from the record.

topic: Bulk archive and hover quick actions
statement: Joyce asked for bulk editing (at least bulk archive of selected records; bulk sign-up likely not needed) and hover quick actions to view, archive, or move to signup. Kobi later committed only to test bulk edit feasibility.

topic: Current SLC to signup build
statement: Kobi described the current build: study link clicks are a staging area for incoming API payloads; a signup record is created for each unique study link click combination, and duplicates roll up into the existing signup record.

topic: Rep-triggered lead to signup step
statement: WagerTech requires an explicit rep action to move an automatically created lead into a signup, so the signup queue is not cluttered with dead records. Jumpr agreed to deliver this as a step within the same object.

topic: Future automated lead progression
statement: Future state: data from WagerTech (post-back or proof data) could automatically move a lead to a signup. For now reps must be able to progress leads manually.

topic: Track non-converted leads for follow-up
statement: WagerTech wants a bucket of leads that did not progress, to enable follow-up (for example email) and to project or report on how many do not convert.

topic: Single Signup object with lead status
statement: Leads and signups will be one Signup object, with a lead status/stage, instead of a separate Lead object. Kobi proposed it to avoid conversion, duplicate and lookup logic; Joyce accepted as long as the end-user result is the same.

topic: Fields and buttons vary by status
statement: Kobi proposed that fields shown differ by status: in lead status only base intake info shows, and other buttons appear after the rep clicks a 'proceed to sign up' button that moves status to in progress.

topic: Filtered list views by status
statement: Rep workspace uses filtered list views such as 'my leads' (lead status needing review, default) and pending/in-progress signups; progressed records drop off the leads view.

topic: Lead stage rework is small
statement: Kobi said adding a lead stage to the existing signup object is limited rework and fairly quick, unlike adding a new object.

topic: Group queue records by player
statement: WagerTech asked to group both queue views by player; Emily said it is important for usability. Kobi was not sure it is possible in Salesforce and will check.

topic: Spike player grouping and LWC with Jester
statement: Kobi will review player grouping / custom LWC console features with Jester and report back with feasibility, time and cost (a spike).

topic: Custom LWC cost and mobile risk
statement: Kobi flagged that custom LWCs are expensive to build and maintain, have platform limits on record page placement, and may not port easily to mobile.

topic: Fallback sort by player and side panel
statement: If grouping is not feasible, Joyce suggested sorting by player; Kobi suggested a right-side panel listing the player's other in-progress signups. Kobi will see what can be done.

topic: Status color indicators replace chevron
statement: The signup record drops the path/chevron in favour of a simple status indicator, with queue quick-view colours mapped to status (for example flagged for fraud, past due). Kobi agreed.

topic: Client to send status ideas
statement: Joyce said WagerTech could send some status ideas for the colour-coded indicators. No firm commitment or date.

topic: Reps edit only referral and proof
statement: On the signup record the rest is read-only context; reps input only the referral information and proof sections. The mockup's Edit button has no purpose; no other fields should be rep-editable.

topic: Referrer lookup with create modal
statement: The rep searches for the referrer by name; if not found, a pop-up modal lets them create the new person/referral record from the signup.

topic: Player info on signup clickable
statement: Joyce said the read-only player info on the signup record should probably be clickable (to open the player record). No Jumpr confirmation.

topic: Secondary referrer lookup on signup
statement: The signup needs a secondary referrer field, as another lookup below the primary referrer.

topic: Payout type editable at signup level
statement: Payout type (bet credit vs cash) is the only referrer data point customizable at signup level. Other referrer data (currency, country) is static and edited on the referral record.

topic: Surface payout amount from matrix
statement: Payout amount, derived from the payout matrix based on referrer and payout type (not rep-entered), should be surfaced next to payout type.

topic: Payout amount and currency from referrer
statement: When the rep selects the primary referrer and payout type, the referrer's currency and country determine the payout amount and payout currency. Kobi described it and Joyce confirmed.

topic: Admin-configurable payout values
statement: Joyce suggested an admin panel in Salesforce where admins configure payout values; values do not change day to day but are subject to change. Jumpr did not explicitly confirm the admin panel.

topic: Snapshot payout values via flow
statement: Because payout values can change, payout information will be stamped as a snapshot by a flow when the rep chooses bet credit or cash, not pulled by formula, so old records do not change retroactively.

topic: Secondary referrals tracked at referral level
statement: Secondary referrals pay on a milestone (about every 10 secondary referrals for a bet credit); reps only capture the secondary referrer on the signup. The count lives on the referral record, not the signup.

topic: Threshold push for secondary payout
statement: Emily said ops will probably need the system to calculate secondary referrals and push them for payout at the threshold (every 10); Lena can confirm the exact rule.

topic: No payout object yet
statement: Kobi stated there is no payout object yet; it would track what has been paid out and what is pending.

topic: Referral screen shows referral counts
statement: The referral record screen should show the number of primary and secondary referrals.

topic: Wager proof is optional
statement: The wager proof is not always mandatory, so it is marked optional.

topic: External proof upload system
statement: Open whether a proof upload system will be built outside Salesforce; if so, Salesforce only needs a verified/missing status, with the date possibly prefilled from AI-scan metadata.

topic: Proof URL fields set verified
statement: As an interim bridge, each proof gets a URL field; populating it sets that proof to verified and counts toward 'X of 2 proofs verified'. When the integration is built, the fields can be hidden while the interface stays the same.

topic: Date field per proof
statement: Joyce asked for a date field per proof and Kobi said it can be done, but Emily noted reps do not record a date against proofs today (only a signup date). No final decision on a per-proof date.

topic: Vertical on signup from deal
statement: Vertical must be captured on the lead/signup, sourced from the related deal (same vertical as the deal).

topic: Existing signup date and first bet date
statement: Kobi said he thinks the build already has a separate signup date and first bet date that are editable. Hedged ('I think'); not confirmed.

topic: Distinct agency and affiliate signup dates
statement: There must be two distinct fields: agency signup date (from the click payload, view-only to reps) and affiliate signup date (entered manually by the rep).

topic: Agency signup date lives on player
statement: Agency signup date should live at the player level and be referable, and can come out of the signup queue view; the rep-entered signup date moves into the editable area.

topic: Progress indicator on editable blocks
statement: Joyce asked for a progress indicator (for example '0 of 1') on the editable blocks, a check on each completed step, and a header indicator of what is left on the signup record.

topic: Flag and archive via screen flow
statement: Archive and Flag actions each open a screen flow modal to pick a reason code and add notes, replacing the current checkbox plus dropdown fraud flag.

topic: Signup history tab shows clicks
statement: In the mockup, a History tab on the signup record shows the clicks against that signup. Kobi acknowledged; no explicit build commitment.

topic: Flag merges won't-do and fraud
statement: Flag is a blanket for anything the rep wants to highlight, combining won't-do and fraud (for example suspicious gameplay, hedging). Archive is for non-alarming reasons (not responding, cannot access account). Each has its own reason set; the exact split is still to be worked out.

topic: Flagged review view for ops
statement: Flagged records go to a separate view for ops review; archived records get their own filterable tab.

topic: Exclusive end states with reason sets
statement: A signup ends in exactly one of flagged, archived or complete, held in a single status, with a different reason set for archive versus flag. A flagged or archived signup is not past due.

topic: Auto-complete with manual override
statement: Status automation: past due follows logic for in-progress records; Complete could be set automatically when all required fields are filled. Joyce wants a manual Complete with an 'are you sure' modal for edge cases and ops visibility. Because Complete triggers payout, they will work it through with Lena.

topic: Complete edge cases with Lena
statement: Open: which edge cases justify manually completing a signup without all required fields; to be worked through with Lena (WagerTech ops).

topic: Status read-only, actions top right
statement: The status shown on the record is display only (not a dropdown) and locked; the top-right controls are actions.

topic: Flag sub-status lifecycle
statement: Flagging gets a sub-status lifecycle from the PRD (suspected, under review, confirmed, dismissed) so ops can track the flag through review.

topic: Separate timing status and signup status
statement: Joyce said she is open to two status fields (a timing status and a signup status) so a record could be past due and flagged at the same time. Kobi answered with a flag sub-status instead (item -55). Not resolved; this sits against the earlier point that a flagged or archived signup is not past due (item -51).

topic: Remove Won't Do status
statement: The 'Won't Do' status is removed. Primary statuses become lead, new, in progress, completed, archived, plus flagged.

topic: Confirmed flag updates primary status
statement: Kobi proposed that when ops confirm a flag, the primary status updates with a status reason (he said to Won't Do). Won't Do was then removed (item -56), and the target primary status for a confirmed flag was not restated.

topic: Design status workflow, demo next week
statement: Kobi to think through the signup statuses and workflow, and next week show how a lead progresses to a signup and how a signup moves to each end route, screen by screen.

topic: Mobile-ready 50/50 block layout
statement: To future-proof for mobile, Joyce suggested using 50/50 blocks that stack. Emily said mobile could reduce delayed logging by letting reps log on the go.

topic: Prioritize signup at rep permission level
statement: Immediate next step: nail the signup record at the rep permission level, then apply the cleanup to the other views as needed.

topic: Icons and copy phone/email
statement: Emily asked for icons and quick copy of fields such as phone number and email to help reps and reduce manual error. No explicit Jumpr confirmation.

topic: Console LWC left bar scope
statement: Asked whether the UI refinement adds scope, Kobi said nothing unusual was asked except possibly the custom LWC for the console left bar, which he will confirm. Most else can be done in the standard console view; player grouping feasibility is unknown.

topic: Console view shows four fields
statement: Kobi stated the console view can show four fields, and he does not know whether they can be made clickable or hold buttons.

topic: Test bulk edits in console
statement: Kobi will run a test and confirm whether bulk edits are possible (checkboxes with configured actions).

topic: Define bulk vs individual actions
statement: Jumpr needs WagerTech to define which actions are bulk versus individual so they can be configured.

topic: DRA business needs note shared
statement: Emily said she put a high-level note for Kobi on what the business needs from Deal Rep Assignment.

topic: Monday 10am DRA working session
statement: A working session on Deal Rep Assignment is set for Monday at 10 a.m. Joyce booked it herself through Google (not Kobi's booking link); Kobi had offered to book it and accepted.

topic: Scope today, hand to Jeff and Pia
statement: Kobi will scope the discussed changes today and hand the work to Jeff and Pia.

topic: Show-and-tell of updated signup screens
statement: Joyce asked Kobi to say when updated signup screens are ready to demo. Kobi said likely not Monday but probably by Tuesday (estimate, not a firm date).

topic: Weekly show-and-tell demo cadence
statement: The team agreed to aim for a weekly show-and-tell demo of updated screens. Kobi prefers early conversations to avoid rework from design changes.

topic: Signups stay on lead-based structure
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi described new mockups where sign-up management uses the existing lead-based structure instead of a separate object.

topic: Status transitions from holding queue
statement: Per Gemini notes, status transitions such as new, in progress and completed move a record from a holding queue to an accepted signup.

topic: Archived and flagged signup statuses
statement: Per Gemini notes, new status values include archived for non-active signups and flagged for fraud or other issues, and the two are distinct.

topic: Duplicate signups roll into existing record
statement: Per Gemini notes, duplicate signup attempts with identical information roll into the existing signup record instead of creating new records, keeping one-to-one with the signup and retaining click history.

topic: Define signup uniqueness criteria
statement: Per Gemini next steps, Kobi is to clarify the criteria that identify a new signup versus rolling an attempt into an existing record.

topic: Dynamic forms by signup status
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi proposed dynamic forms that show only relevant fields based on signup status, separating lead details from referral and proof information.

topic: URL fields for proof documents
statement: Per Gemini notes, URL fields will be added to capture links to proof documentation; the Decisions section frames this as a bridge until a backend solution exists.

topic: Proof checkbox to drop-down option
statement: Per Gemini notes, there is an option to change the current proof checkbox to a drop-down for more explicit verification; no decision recorded.

topic: Capture proof document load date
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi and Marc discussed capturing the date when proof documents are loaded, possibly shown in a three-column layout.

topic: Rich text banners for status
statement: Per Gemini notes, banners were discussed for proof status updates, possibly rich text banners instead of complex components, which Marc said might be feasible.

topic: Evaluate dynamic rich text banners
statement: Per Gemini next steps, Marc is to evaluate using rich text banners for dynamic field values and decide if custom components are needed for complex status indicators.

topic: Custom grouping and bulk actions complex
statement: Per Gemini notes, the client's desired grouping and bulk actions in a console view are technically complex; Marc suggested a fully custom page with two LWCs might be the only way, with data-display complexity.

topic: Custom list view grouping shelved
statement: Per Gemini Decisions only, custom list view grouping is shelved in favour of standard sorting for the initial release, with possible future research.

topic: Single record page, role tabs
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi proposed one record page with different tabs for admins and representatives instead of maintaining multiple record pages.

topic: Configure layouts with user tabs
statement: Per Gemini next steps, Kobi is to create separate tabs for different user views and streamline information without adding filtering logic yet.

topic: Auto-populate payout amount from matrix
statement: Per Gemini notes, there is a requirement to automate population of the payout amount field based on a matrix of sign-up and referral currency.

topic: Custom metadata for payout matrix
statement: Per Gemini notes, Marc suggested storing the payout matrix in custom metadata so the system preloads the correct values based on user selections.

topic: Split build work Kobi/Marc
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi takes layouts and field names and Marc takes flows and actions.

topic: Create WagerTech user stories
statement: Per Gemini notes, Kobi will create user stories and task assignments for WagerTech before the next check-in.

topic: Not all due by Tuesday call
statement: Per Gemini notes, there is a call on Tuesday, but the team does not need everything completed by then.

topic: Regroup to assign tasks
statement: Per Gemini next steps, Kobi and Marc will regroup later that day to assign work on flows, layouts and field updates.

topic: Figma-style layout mockups before build
statement: As relayed by Waleed, the client (Joyce) asked whether Jumpr could show layouts in a Figma-style tool before building. Waleed told her this does not really work with Salesforce and it is easier to update the layouts in Salesforce directly; Kobi said he told her the same.

topic: Client wants example starting points for layout feedback
statement: As relayed by Waleed, when Jumpr asks the client for feedback on UI layouts (what sales reps want to see), the client wants Jumpr to provide examples as starting points and to give criteria for the feedback wanted.

topic: Build phase: fields and objects, layouts later
statement: Waleed described the project as still early: the team is building fields and objects, and front-end layout work usually comes later.

topic: Subset of PRD fields built; rest held until process defined
statement: Kobi said fields were brought in from the client's PRD, ERD and API doc, but he added only a subset of the fields per object and kept the rest out until the process is defined; the client still found it too many fields.

topic: Conflicting client stakeholder feedback blocks decisions
statement: Kobi said feedback from Emily and Lena differs from Joyce's, the client is still clarifying the process among themselves in calls, and he needs a decision to implement.

topic: Update Asana project status before tomorrow
statement: The Asana project plan is out of date (much POC work is done, and feedback from Friday and today is not yet in). Waleed asked to update it today ahead of tomorrow's meeting; Kobi agreed.

topic: New object added; UI cleaned up
statement: Kobi said another object has been added and the UI has been cleaned up quite a bit.

topic: Layout aligned to client's updated lead/sign-up mockup
statement: The client (Joyce) gave an updated mockup of the lead and sign-up process; Kobi is making the layout as close as possible to it.

topic: Deal rep assignment and history cleanup in progress
statement: The team is cleaning up deal rep assignment and its history portion; more stories are still to be written and are not yet in the plan.

topic: Backend API is biggest risk
statement: With less than two weeks left, Kobi named the backend API piece as his biggest risk.

topic: Bridge gap: paste Dropbox links into Salesforce
statement: Last week (Friday) it was decided, on Kobi's proposal, to bridge the gap for file uploads: the client uploads files to Dropbox and pastes the links (URLs) in Salesforce, with the rest handled in Salesforce.

topic: Client now wants GCP file uploads
statement: Yesterday the client said they want to move forward with Google Cloud (GCP) for file uploads, after the Friday bridge-gap decision. Kobi told the client there is a good chance it will not work for end of month.

topic: GCP uploads as fast follow after go-live
statement: Kobi proposed to the client that the bridge gap (Dropbox links) be used at go-live and the GCP components be broken down and worked on after, possibly as a fast follow after go-live. Client acceptance is not stated.

topic: Which fields client back end can send
statement: API discussion is planned for tomorrow; Jumpr is still waiting for the client to confirm which fields their back end can send. The client is revamping their CMS; they seem able to send many expected fields, but this is not yet aligned.

topic: Data entry and automation cleanup ETA
statement: Kobi said the data entry portions are straightforward and automation cleanup will probably be done by end of this week, maybe mid next week.

topic: Re-plan next two weeks in Asana
statement: Waleed asked Kobi to update Asana with where things stand for the next two weeks and give the remaining work an honest assessment so they can review the timeline; Kobi agreed.

topic: No separate lead object; one sign-up record with status layouts
statement: The client's updated mockup asked for a read-only lead object with player info and click history that creates a sign-up record on sign-up. Kobi pushed back (overhead) and proposed using the same record with page layouts by status; they agreed.

topic: Rep view field set still being decided
statement: The rep view is to be a clean layout showing only the fields Joyce highlighted (of about 20 PRD sign-up fields); after seeing the mockup, Emily said more fields will need to be added.

topic: Reps update sign-up status via action buttons
statement: Reps get a simplified layout and update the sign-up status through action buttons (flag, complete, archive, and a log sign-up button still in progress by Jester).

topic: Grouped list view not possible
statement: The client asked for a grouped list view; Kobi said no, it is not possible. He said organizing the list view by name, operator, created date and possibly icons should be doable.

topic: Sign-up page layout done; list views pending
statement: The main sign-up page layout is good to go; list views are not updated yet.

topic: Layout and editability change by status
statement: The sign-up layout changes by status: New (the default on creation) is read-only; after log sign-up the status is In progress (lead accepted) and the layout becomes editable with checkboxes. Ops fields such as fraud status remain; extra info is hidden or read-only for reps.

topic: Path removed from sign-up layout
statement: The Path component was removed from the sign-up layout at the client's request because the process is not linear.

topic: URL entry marks accepted via formula
statement: On the sign-up record, reps enter the URL; that changes the check mark to accepted, and a formula field updates the status. Only fields reps should update are editable; the rest is read-only.

topic: Fraud review process for ops team
statement: Flagging a sign-up for review shows banners and sends it to the ops team to set the fraud review status (suspected, under review, confirmed). Kobi said the ops review process still needs to be figured out with the client.

topic: Custom click history view (LWC) deferred
statement: The client's desired click-history list view (all attempts) cannot be matched exactly without an LWC; Kobi plans to tell the client not to focus on it now and do it later. Waleed agreed internally. Client acceptance is not stated.

topic: Bulk deal rep assignment screen flow
statement: Jester built a screen flow to bulk create deal rep assignments (pick reps by profile, set active and start date) and to end them in bulk by date; he is working on showing current assignment status.

topic: Simplify crowded rep page; possibly split into tabs
statement: From yesterday's client feedback the page is too heavy; Kobi will clean it up to be closer to the sign-up page and offered to split fields into tabs. He said this will be the reps' main view.

topic: Reports as table view of sign-ups
statement: Kobi plans to create reports giving a table view of the same information, such as sign-ups for review and sign-ups in progress.

topic: Layouts mobile responsive; not yet tested on app
statement: Kobi had not yet opened the build in the Salesforce mobile app, but said the layouts are mobile responsive and nothing fully custom has been built. The work is in a partial sandbox.

topic: No mobile-specific edit changes for now
statement: On mobile the record has no inline edit (pencil), so reps need a button (edit or complete; complete opens the screen flow for referral and proof info). Waleed said not to add anything for mobile right now.

topic: Timeline risk; layouts should be last
statement: Waleed said he is worried about the timeline with about two weeks left, there are open questions, and layouts should be the last thing; Kobi said he may be underestimating the remaining work. Waleed asked for an honest re-plan in Asana.

topic: Sandbox API credentials received
statement: WagerTech received the new sandbox API credentials late the previous day and had not yet confirmed whether they work.

topic: Friday API connect and end-to-end testing
statement: WagerTech aims to book an API connect on Friday and do end-to-end testing.

topic: Welcome-email fraud detection approach deferred
statement: The changing fraud-detection approach for the welcome email was pushed to a later meeting because Joyce first needs to talk to the A3S team.

topic: Demo run as restricted rep user
statement: The signup logging demo was run logged in as a rep user with restricted write access, not as admin.

topic: Signup logging built close to Joyce's mockup
statement: Jumpr built the signup logging process close to Joyce's mockup, within Salesforce platform limits; the New list is the equivalent of the mockup's lead tab.

topic: Click history moved to separate History tab
statement: Because the layout cannot hold a split attribution/player view, Kobi will create a details tab with attribution info and player info as two columns, and click history becomes a second (History) tab. Joyce agreed.

topic: Platform limit on split section layout
statement: Standard record layout does not allow the split two-section view (player info and attribution info side by side with headings); sections cannot be reorganized.

topic: Read-only banner on signup info
statement: Joyce asked for a subtle text banner indicating the signup information is read only; Kobi agreed to add it.

topic: Log Signup screen flow covers all editable fields
statement: The Log Signup screen flow will include every field the rep fills out (including referral information), and the record fields below are prepopulated from it; current fields are placeholders.

topic: Remove first bet date and amount
statement: Per earlier feedback, first bet date and first bet amount are not needed in the Log Signup flow and will be cleaned up.

topic: Log Signup moves status to In Progress
statement: Clicking Log Signup updates the signup status to In Progress (rep accepted the lead); fields then become editable (pencil icon). No input is required to move it.

topic: Standard Edit button removed
statement: Kobi removed the standard Edit button because the out-of-box edit cannot control read-only versus editable fields; the path/actions give a more guided flow.

topic: Check button colour/style options
statement: Joyce asked whether buttons (such as Flag) can be styled to stand out; Kobi does not think colors can be changed out of the box and will check for quick wins.

topic: Emoji flags via formula fields
statement: Lina asked for visual presentation (for example country flags) instead of text; Kobi confirmed emojis driven by formula fields on a display field, with the editable text field underneath. Lina said to try it.

topic: Phase 1: out-of-box UI, no LWC overhaul
statement: Kobi recommended not prioritizing custom LWC layout work in Phase 1 because field changes in LWC cost hours each; LWC polish can follow once fields and flows are final. Joyce accepted.

topic: LWC-first approach threatens August go-live
statement: Kobi stated that starting with LWC, or doing UI enhancement up front, would cause feedback cycles that extend the August go-live date.

topic: Sparing UI polish before full BA rollout
statement: Joyce asked that some polish be applied sparingly where needed before the full rollout, which she described as presenting to all BAs at an in-person day. Emily said this is a time trade-off that needs more understanding.

topic: Status emojis and colour scheme
statement: Status values will use emojis/colors everywhere the status appears, including the signup status at the top. Kobi proposed yellow In Progress, green Completed, gray Archived, red triangle Flagged and will add placeholders that WagerTech can change.

topic: Lina to share status emoji suggestions
statement: Lina will post emoji suggestions for statuses in the chat.

topic: Rename Q list view to In Progress
statement: The list view called Q will be renamed In Progress to match the status; it holds in-progress signups not archived or flagged.

topic: Inbound CMS data does not auto-move from New
statement: Currently, information received against a New signup does not automatically move it to In Progress; it stays in New until the rep acts. Automation can be set up once the source information exists.

topic: Manual vs automated signup conversion field
statement: Joyce asked for an indicator of whether a lead was converted to a signup manually or automatically, for troubleshooting. Kobi will add a field now tracking explicit Log Signup clicks and fill the automated path later.

topic: Timeline for WagerTech proof automation
statement: Kobi asked for the timeline of WagerTech's automation that pulls in proofs; Joyce does not know yet.

topic: Show Operator only for reps, no partner
statement: Reps only need the operator, not the partner (privacy; ops still has the data). The operator/partner combo will not be used; operator alone shows in rep-facing lists and header.

topic: Ops can see partner within signup
statement: Ops need operator and partner when deep diving; partner does not need to be in the queue list. Kobi will add partner (from the deal) under operator in the signup details for ops.

topic: Remove Brand Ambassador field from signup
statement: The Brand Ambassador field is not needed on the rep's signup view and will be removed.

topic: Header/highlight fields for signup
statement: The highlight (header) section will show status (color), signup completion percentage, operator, market and vertical; personal contact details (phone, e-transfer, email) move below as Player Info.

topic: Show player origin state/province
statement: Joyce suggested showing the player's origin state/province to spot conflicts with the signup market as a possible fraud indicator. No confirmation from Jumpr.

topic: Vertical/operator logos via image fields
statement: Lina and Emily suggested casino/sports emojis or logos; Kobi said image fields with an image set and mapping are likely possible. Not confirmed.

topic: Proof info section before referral info
statement: Lina asked to flip sections so the order is signup, proof, then referral; Kobi agreed.

topic: Grouping signups under players not pursued
statement: Joyce asked about grouping signups with players; Kobi said it would be a very big build, recommended against it for now, and suggested a later POC.

topic: Sort queue by player name option
statement: Queue defaults to most recent (created date); Joyce asked to also give reps the option to sort by player name; Kobi agreed.

topic: Large queue hard to navigate without search
statement: The queue could hold 500+ signups including dead clicks; console queue search was not available, raising usability concerns.

topic: Reps will only adopt one view
statement: Joyce and Lina stated reps will not switch between multiple views (for example a report plus the queue); the solution must work within one view.

topic: Build signups dashboard and demo video
statement: Kobi will build a signups dashboard of everything in the reps' queue and record a video to show it before next week, as a way to work large record volumes.

topic: Rep entry point: queue search vs player search
statement: Global search for a name returns the player, not the signup. Waleed will take back improving search to show signups and status; Joyce said there are two entry points (queue vs player record) and Jumpr should work through options for the best workflow.

topic: List view search enabled, fields not mapped
statement: List view search was turned on during the meeting but is not fully working; searchable fields still need mapping, and only 'Jake' is searchable for now. Jumpr confirmed it can be made to work.

topic: Lina's mockup with colour-coded statuses
statement: Lina shared a mockup and asked if the layout can match it or come close; Joyce noted colour-coded statuses on the left. Jumpr did not explicitly confirm and moved to the path question.

topic: Show linear status path or not
statement: Joyce said the path could be reintroduced if it only shows New, In Progress, Completed. After Archived stayed in the status field, Waleed suggested maybe not showing the path and keeping just the status field. No final call was made.

topic: Current fraud flag and review build demoed
statement: As built: rep flags for fraud with a reason, fraud review status becomes Suspected, ops confirm or dismiss; when confirmed the record is flagged and reps cannot act on it.

topic: Fraud tracked separately from main status
statement: Main signup status is New, In Progress, Completed. Fraud is tracked separately (sub-status/checkbox) so a completed signup flagged as fraud stays Completed and can be excluded in reporting; reps cannot act until ops lifts the flag, then it returns to In Progress.

topic: Fraud can be flagged after completion
statement: Fraud may be detected after a signup is completed (sometimes a week later); completed fraudulent signups stay in the system as real events and are excluded via a report column.

topic: Archived status via button with reason
statement: Archived stays in the status field (non-linear) to remove dead signups from the rep queue; reps archive via a button that prompts for a reason. 'Closed' status was not adopted.

topic: Only ops can unarchive signups
statement: Once archived, reps cannot edit or unarchive; only ops can move an archived signup back to In Progress.

topic: Remove Flagged status; rename Flag to Fraud
statement: Flagged is removed from the status picklist; Archived kept. The Flag action/label is renamed Fraud.

topic: Split fraud and archive reason lists
statement: PRD combined fraud and invalid reasons; they are now split: archived reasons (player unavailable, missed deadline, etc.) and fraud-specific reasons, each with notes.

topic: WagerTech to provide fraud and archive reason codes
statement: Emily committed to providing the reason codes for fraud and archived.

topic: Bulk deal rep assignment screen flow built
statement: A new screen flow lets users pick multiple reps, set assignment status and effective start date, and bulk update or deactivate assignments, replacing the one-by-one process. Layout still needs cleanup.

topic: Clean up deal assignment screen and ping
statement: Joyce asked Kobi to ping when the screen is cleaned up so the deal flow and assignment process can be reviewed together.

topic: Status emojis on deal rep assignments
statement: Deal rep assignment screen will use the same status columns/emojis (e.g. green for Active, pause emoji for Paused); Kobi agreed.

topic: Hide, don't delete, non-rep fields
statement: WagerTech will flag fields not needed versus the PRD/ERD and the simplified rep set; unneeded-for-rep fields move to a More Info section/tab for ops rather than being deleted.

topic: WagerTech to flag rep-visible fields
statement: WagerTech will identify the fields reps should see (and fields no longer needed) in the feedback document.

topic: Requirements drifting from PRD/ERD
statement: Kobi noted the fields were built from the PRD and ERD and the conversations are straying away from both.

topic: Automate deal rep assignment sync with CMS
statement: Emily asked whether deal rep assignment info can be connected to the CMS via API; Kobi said in theory yes but the integration still needs scoping.

topic: Direction: Salesforce pushes to CMS
statement: Joyce said to start, Salesforce into the CMS (Salesforce is where assignments are changed/managed); Lina and Emily agreed. Joyce then said there is a lot of discussion needed and she is not confident; to be nailed down.

topic: CMS to define endpoint and payload fields
statement: For SF-to-CMS deal rep assignment callouts, WagerTech's CMS must expose an API endpoint and specify the payload fields it needs; Jumpr then maps Salesforce data and builds a POC. Joyce said they will take screenshots of fields.

topic: SLC deal-determination fields already documented
statement: Kobi said the fields needed to determine the deal from study link clicks were already in the document he shared.

topic: WagerTech to try Salesforce mobile app
statement: Waleed suggested trying the Salesforce mobile app (layouts translate without custom mobile work); Joyce said they will download it.

topic: Emily to give feedback on other screens
statement: Emily said WagerTech will provide more feedback on other screens and help with the status codes.

statement: Autocompleting signups is still an open decision; regardless, WagerTech must confirm which fields are required for the signup completion percentage (listed in the open questions).

statement: User-input date fields will drop the time component; inherited/system timestamps (e.g. click timestamp) keep time. Kobi agreed.

statement: Emily listed a storage scope update (Jumpr had taken it away because of the GCP update) on the agenda. It was not discussed in the meeting, so the update is still open.

topic: WagerTech referral logic addition not discussed
statement: Emily said WagerTech has an addition to the referral logic to talk through. It was not discussed in the meeting; the content of the addition is unknown.

Emily said a lot is changing on WagerTech's back end and the developer needs to familiarize himself.

topic: Log Signup button naming
statement: Joyce's mockup had 'sign up' and 'archive' actions; Kobi named the action 'Log Signup' and invited WagerTech to suggest better terminology. No name was confirmed.
