statement: Emily asked if Kobi had looked at the feedback tracker in parallel with the working sessions; Kobi said he did but treated the working-session feedback as the latest. Emily said she will re-ping him because the points were outlined in the tracker.

topic: Remove duplicate fields from view
statement: Joyce said fields that show up in multiple spots on the screen can be removed from the view, while single-instance fields are fine to keep. Kobi acknowledged.

topic: CMS control vs two-way assignment sync
statement: Emily said the CMS will only receive deal rep assignment information and nobody can turn assignments on or off from the CMS, to avoid the Airtable problem. Joyce said two-way would be ideal but she needs to understand the extra effort and what data is available through the CMS. Not resolved.

topic: CMS can query any SF field via REST API
statement: Jumpr stated that for inbound queries the CMS uses the standard Salesforce REST API, so any field (including fields not on the UI) is available with nothing special to build; Waleed said the CMS can collect any field on the deal rep assignment object through the API.

topic: Reports allow inline edits, no actions
statement: Kobi said reports allow inline field edits but he does not think actions can be run from them; list views can enable search and inline editing. Reps must click into the record to use action buttons.

topic: Polish limited to colours and buttons
statement: Joyce clarified she does not want to change the out-of-box layout; the polish she wants is subtle, such as different colours or button colours to draw the eye. No confirmation from Jumpr beyond acknowledgement.

topic: In-progress fraud review queue; reps see but cannot act
statement: Lina said WagerTech's new welcome-email/fraud detection will include a dedicated person reviewing incoming fraud at the In Progress step, which is new. Reps should see signups under fraud but cannot act on them until ops moves the status back to In Progress, or the signup becomes a write-off/permanent fraud.

topic: Read/edit access obtained for API user
statement: WagerTech (Strahinja) obtained the read/edit permissions needed for the API configuration with help from a WagerTech colleague.

topic: External ID property enabled on SLC object
statement: Strahinja enabled the external ID property on the Study Link Click object himself because record creation complained. Kobi said Jumpr may use a custom external ID field, but this is acceptable as long as records are created.

topic: Last name required at player sign-up
statement: The null last name seen in testing came from the local front end running without backend validation. Emily confirmed a new player account must provide a last name, and Strahinja confirmed it can be passed through on the study link click.

topic: SLC records push to Salesforce sandbox
statement: Strahinja demonstrated a click in a local test environment (disconnected from the site backend) that triggers the event and creates a Study Link Click record in the Salesforce sandbox. Kobi confirmed the SLC records look good.

topic: Site and book country fields not configured
statement: All fields in the API doc came through except site, which was not properly configured, and book country, which is in the doc but does not appear to exist on the object.

topic: Review updated API doc shared via Joyce
statement: Kobi said he shared an updated API document with Joyce with slight field changes and asked WagerTech to review it and leave comments.

topic: Enough SLC data to map to deal?
statement: WagerTech does not have the Salesforce deal ID, so Jumpr needs to know what data the CMS can send with the study link click to look up the deal and the deal rep assignment. Kobi said he is not yet confident there is enough information for deal mapping.

topic: Market data not readily available in CMS
statement: Emily said the market (country and state) must be shared on the study link click but the CMS does not currently expose it easily; she took it offline. Strahinja suggested pulling it for now from a sheet or Airtable to start collecting the data.

topic: Sandbox test data cleared before production
statement: Kobi stated that all data loaded into the sandbox will be cleared when moving to production, so test SLC records are not a concern.

topic: Repeat test clicks rolled into one sign-up
statement: Test SLCs sent with the same information were all related to a single sign-up record, as expected.

topic: Send deal makeup since no CMS deal ID
statement: WagerTech has no deal ID to send. Emily restated that WagerTech passes the parameters and Jumpr resolves the deal; Kobi agreed that if the SLC carries market country/state, operator ID and partner ID, Salesforce will look up and associate the deal.

topic: Sync Salesforce deal ID to CMS later
statement: Salesforce auto-numbers each deal, but that ID lives only in Salesforce; syncing it to the CMS was described as a possible future state, with deal makeup used in the interim.

topic: CMS has no partner concept
statement: Jay confirmed the CMS has no concept of a partner; books owned by a partner are marked with a shorthand suffix (e.g. CTM) on the operator/book name.

topic: SLC data stored raw, no SF processing
statement: Data on the Study Link Click is the raw data WagerTech sends; Salesforce is not processing it yet.

topic: Prefer IDs over names in payload
statement: Kobi proposed reviewing what fields the CMS has at click time and not sticking to the initial API fields; he prefers IDs (e.g. book ID) over names, with a mapping in Salesforce to show names. Strahinja agreed adding IDs would be a good idea going forward.

topic: Unique deal makeup fields
statement: A unique deal is defined by operator, partner, market country, market state and vertical; vertical (casino, sportsbook) is the existing 'type' value.

topic: WagerTech to parse market into SF format
statement: Jay suggested bracket notation such as 'DKC (US)'; Kobi said no because deal country values include United States, Canada, or US and Canada plus state. Strahinja and Jay said WagerTech can parse the market and send it in Salesforce's format, conditional on the information being available in the CMS.

topic: WagerTech maps data to SF data model
statement: Jay said the mapping would happen on WagerTech's side: Salesforce defines the format and WagerTech maps the books to it. Strahinja agreed WagerTech can restructure data to fit the Salesforce data model, if the data is available at click time.

topic: Unique IDs for operators and partners
statement: Operators and partners will get unique IDs set up via import into Salesforce; Jumpr shares a table of operator/partner names and IDs, WagerTech sends those IDs through the API on SLCs, and any new operator or partner must be added in both systems with the same ID.

topic: Tie Airtable to CMS for book changes
statement: Jay suggested making Airtable changes on the CMS side and connecting the Airtable API to the CMS so book changes reflect in Airtable immediately.

topic: Display operator/partner names not IDs
statement: Emily asked that records in the sign-up flow show operator and partner names rather than IDs; Kobi confirmed Salesforce will display the names while IDs are used for the integration.

topic: Clean up Airtable operator list
statement: Jay will clean up the Airtable book/operator list (remove inactive books) so Jumpr gets a refined list before IDs are created.

topic: Define ID system and operator/partner import sheet
statement: Kobi will define the ID format and create an import sheet for operators and partners for WagerTech to help populate; Jumpr then uploads it into Salesforce and shares the ID mapping. Kobi later said he would send the spreadsheets by end of day, with population and import next week. 'Book' was clarified to mean operator.

topic: ID system for market country/state
statement: Kobi proposed an ID system (API name vs label) for market country and state values, since labels like 'Canada and United States' are poor for integration filters. Jay said it sounded good and asked a clarifying question; no explicit commitment followed.

topic: Deal market combination scenarios
statement: Deal market options are: US with a state, Canada with a state, all of Canada (state empty), and US and Canada (country only). The SLC data must carry this so Salesforce can map to the right deal.

topic: Deal data comes from deal, not player
statement: The operator, partner and market data on the click must come from the deal/operator-partner configuration, not from the player's profile, because an operator can have deals in multiple states.

topic: Is book state deal-specific?
statement: Kobi asked whether the book state value is specific to the deal; Strahinja must double-check because the payload is a one-to-one copy of what the old backend receives.

topic: Add field for book country on SLC
statement: Kobi expects that if book state exists, book country exists too, and Salesforce would add a field to capture it.

topic: Split operator-partner into separate IDs
statement: Partner is currently only in the operator-partner dash notation. It should be split into separate operator and partner IDs; names can also be sent, but IDs drive lookups. Strahinja agreed.

topic: Player data from logged-in user; WagerTech owns player external ID
statement: Player details on the click come from the logged-in user, and WagerTech creates the player external ID.

topic: Rep slug optional on SLC
statement: Rep slug is optional on the SLC; Jumpr included it because WagerTech's earlier API sent it and it helps troubleshooting.

topic: Same rep has separate US and Canada slugs
statement: Some reps have separate US and Canada slugs (e.g. Luca with a separate 'play direct' US page). Lena asked for these to be merged, so the 'play' slugs will disappear and merge into the reps' normal slugs; Jay offered a list.

topic: Use rep slug for rep mapping for now
statement: Rep mapping will use the rep slug for now, with a possible move to an ID system later. Kobi noted this commits WagerTech to each slug mapping one-to-one to a single rep. Jay said no rep will have two slugs going forward.

topic: WagerTech to decide on rep ID system
statement: Kobi recommended a unique rep ID that does not depend on slug or site. Emily said WagerTech will get back to Jumpr on the rep ID question; it is not decided. Where the ID is generated was left open (CMS Postgres or Salesforce).

topic: CMS Postgres DB as source of truth
statement: Strahinja said the Postgres database behind the new CMS will also be a source of truth and can auto-generate IDs, or the IDs could come from Salesforce instead.

topic: SLC API milestone; field mapping remaining
statement: Kobi called record creation in Salesforce a big milestone; what remains is agreeing the field combinations and the mapping.

topic: Survey completion not yet tested
statement: Strahinja has only built the study link click; survey completion is stubbed but untested, and he is unsure whether the Salesforce objects exist.

topic: Survey completion upserted on player account
statement: Survey completion is tracked at the player level, not the study level. It is stored on the player record (an Account of a specific record type) via upsert using the player external ID, with a 'survey completed' checkbox and optionally the survey date. Whether record type is needed in the payload is open.

topic: Send survey payload and target object
statement: Kobi will send the survey completion payload details and the object to upsert on, including whether record type is needed.

topic: New CMS goes live just before Salesforce
statement: The new CMS is being built in parallel and will go live before Salesforce, very close in timeline. Getting the CMS validated and tested is Strahinja and Jay's biggest priority; the API work was started to prove the connection.

topic: GCP queue for API error handling
statement: WagerTech will put a queue between the CMS and Salesforce (GCP Pub/Sub) with logging, retry behavior and dead letters, so failed sends can be audited and rerun.

topic: Salesforce owns troubleshooting after success
statement: Once Salesforce returns a success response for a created record, troubleshooting from that point is Salesforce's (Jumpr's) responsibility.

topic: Send updated field list and expected values
statement: Kobi will send an updated list of the final fields needed and the expected values for each. No due date was given for this item.

topic: Import operators/partners and distribute external IDs
statement: Kobi and Emily will work together to import WagerTech's actual operator and partner lists into Salesforce, define the external ID, and make sure the CMS has it.

topic: Update SF automation to test deal mapping
statement: Once the pieces are in place, Jumpr will update its Salesforce automation to test whether study link clicks map to the correct deals.

topic: Pass market and partner on SLC
statement: Strahinja owns adding market country, state and partner to the study link click payload.

topic: Deal mapping spreadsheet and real-deal tests
statement: Besides operator and partner sheets, Kobi will prepare a spreadsheet to map WagerTech deals to Salesforce fields, upload them, and test with real examples of clicks through a rep link. Emily agreed. Kobi aims to send the spreadsheets by end of day, with population and import next week.

topic: Future: deals originate in SF, ID to CMS
statement: Emily raised that in the future deals would originate in Salesforce with the deal ID passed to the CMS. Kobi said sending the Salesforce deal ID on SLCs is his preference because it removes ambiguity. Emily said that is where she would like to get to but WagerTech must still settle deal management ownership internally; not decided.

topic: Deal management ownership pending internally
statement: Emily said she sent a doc on ownership of deal management; WagerTech still needs to solidify this internally, acknowledges work is involved, and will bring it to Jumpr.

topic: One SF deal per state; CMS must align
statement: Kobi restated the earlier Salesforce rule that each state is a separate deal, not one deal for five states, so the CMS needs a deal record per unique combination. Emily took it away ('understood'); CMS alignment is not confirmed.

topic: Interim: SLC carries deal makeup
statement: In the interim, study link clicks will send the deal makeup (operator, partner, market, vertical). Emily confirmed and Strahinja said he is okay with the decisions so far.

topic: No server-side click deduplication
statement: Every click is sent to Salesforce as its own record with no server-side deduplication. Salesforce rolls clicks up to the same sign-up so reps see the relevant one, which captures players who click, drop off, and click again later. Strahinja first assumed dedup was WagerTech's job, then agreed.

topic: Store Salesforce click record ID in CMS DB
statement: Salesforce returns a unique ID for each click record; Kobi recommended WagerTech store it in its database for two-way troubleshooting lookup. Strahinja agreed.

topic: Strahinja to build survey completion push
statement: Strahinja said he has only stubbed survey completion and offered to review the survey sections of the requirements and push whatever information WagerTech has access to; Kobi said yes. Later Emily said WagerTech will action the survey work once Kobi sends the survey details.

topic: WagerTech to send active partner/book list
statement: Emily committed that WagerTech will provide the current list of active partner/book combinations and asked whether Jumpr also wants it by market and province/state. Kobi answered with separate operator and partner sheets, plus a deal mapping sheet for testing.

topic: Jay/Strahinja to work out partner parsing
statement: Emily suggested Jay and Strahinja take offline how the partner is parsed out of the operator name. Unless the CMS changes, a table mapping the partner shorthand codes would be needed on Jumpr's side.

topic: Past data inconsistency; API guardrails needed
statement: Kobi said Joyce reported that data in the previous iteration came through inconsistently, so he wants guardrails on the API side when WagerTech sends data. Strahinja shared the concern and wants proof on his side.

topic: Original kickoff go-live date pushed back
statement: Taryn noted the early-June kickoff recording had go-live set for 'Friday' and assumed it had been pushed back; Kobi confirmed. The original date itself is not stated.

topic: Target pencils-down and UAT start end of week
statement: Jumpr aims to be pencils down and move into UAT by the end of the week of Jul 28, but quite a bit of work remains and Kobi is unsure whether Jumpr or the client will be ready.

topic: UAT, data migration, Aug 17 go-live target
statement: If all goes well: about one week of UAT, a few days of data migration, then go-live around mid-August. Kobi recalls August 17 as the target date previously set. This is a conditional target, not a confirmed date.

topic: Two weeks post-go-live support, later phases
statement: Go-live usually means about two weeks of support from Jumpr; the other project phases follow while the client team uses what was delivered.

topic: Outstanding work on both sides
statement: Many pieces remain on the client side, and Jumpr has many small items to finish that can take a long time; Kobi plans to push through during the week.

topic: Reconcile decision doc into Asana
statement: WagerTech setup decisions live partly in a separate document Kobi kept and the Asana board is outdated; Kobi will reconcile both and bring Asana up to date so decisions and changes can be searched there.

topic: Partner/operator/country/market list IDs
statement: Emily asked to nail down the approach for the partner/operator/country/market reference list and the unique ID for each value. The meeting did not come back to this topic.

topic: Sign-up record two-column layout
statement: Kobi showed the sign-up record combined into two columns: player information/details on one side and end-user entry fields on the other. Full tabs are not possible across the board; Kobi offered to switch the column order if the client prefers.

topic: New status read-only for end users
statement: In New status the sign-up record is read-only for end users; editing needs admin or a permission. Reps only have the two buttons, including the log sign-up action that moves the record to In Progress.

topic: In Progress screen proofs and history
statement: In In Progress the screen shows proof and deposit info and referral info; a history tab shows multiple clicks; player information is not editable because automation sets it. Kobi asked the client to say if any field is missing.

topic: Sign-up completion logic pending
statement: Proof status counts up as proofs are entered, but completion logic is not updated. Jumpr is waiting on the final field set and the open-questions answer on what counts as completion.

topic: No-refer checkbox added
statement: Kobi added the no-refer field Emily asked for; when checked, the other two referral fields disappear.

topic: No secondary referrer when no refer
statement: Lina confirmed that when no refer is checked there is no secondary referrer.

topic: Effort to add referral-section field
statement: Lina asked how hard it is to add one more field to the referral information section (field not yet known). Kobi said adding a field to the layout is easy, but any behavior tied to it (for example with no referral checked) needs scoping.

topic: Add back referral notes field
statement: Lina asked to add back the notes section in referral information; Kobi agreed. Waleed confirmed the notes are for the specific sign-up, not the referral in general.

topic: Move secondary referral lower
statement: Emily asked to move the secondary referral down because payout type and amount link to the primary referrer. Kobi said "Yeah" and moved on to the payout automation; no explicit change confirmed.

topic: Payout amount auto-filled from matrix
statement: Payout amount is automated: choosing cash fills it from the referral matrix the client sent, driven by the sign-up currency. Referral currency is displayed; sign-up currency is in the admin More Info tab.

topic: Keep referral currency visible
statement: Lina confirmed the referral currency must stay visible because it decides which bank (Canadian or US) pays the referral.

topic: Lina to confirm referral info
statement: Lina will try to get Jumpr the referral information and settle an internal workflow question on secondary referrers as soon as possible; she does not expect changes now. Kobi asked to be told if anything on the matrix changes.

topic: Secondary referral automation not built
statement: Jumpr has not built automation for the secondary referral (planned on the referral object); Kobi said it does not block this phase, so a client change there costs no rework.

topic: Operator logos for 60-70 operators
statement: Operator logos now display. Logos for about 60-70 operators must be filled in for go-live (upload to Salesforce, ops paste the image URL); Kobi said the teams may need to work together on how.

topic: Country icons; state stays text
statement: Canada and US country icons display; per-state emojis are not possible, so state stays as text.

topic: Client to provide vertical icons
statement: Kobi asked the client to give the icons they want for verticals, if they want them; Jumpr can then add them.

topic: Sort split-view queue by country
statement: Emily asked about showing market in the split-view queue; Lina suggested a market filter, then asked for a sort by market. Kobi said market is two fields and they can sort by country.

topic: Country flag next to name
statement: Waleed suggested a country flag next to the player name in the list; Emily and Lina agreed, and Kobi confirmed it will show the Canadian or US flag next to the name.

topic: Red highlight for fraud rows
statement: Lina asked to color the whole row red for fraud instead of the red flag emoji. Kobi said no; the list shows up to four fields in a chosen order.

topic: Move red fraud flag next to name
statement: Joyce asked to move the red fraud flag to the immediate right of the person's name; Kobi said they can rearrange. The client then said it would sit with the list view before deciding the final look.

topic: List view per Lina's screenshot
statement: Lina asked if the list view can follow her screenshot (operator logo with progress/status together, proof status and flags on the right). Kobi said yes, but the date may be lost; Lina said the team will take it away and decide.

topic: Client to review list view layout
statement: Waleed suggested the client take a day to get used to the list icons; Emily and Lina agreed to sit with it and confirm how they want it to look.

topic: Split view four-field limit
statement: Kobi explained the split view shows only the first four fields, in order; formula fields can combine data and icons (e.g. player plus country icon).

topic: Drop status text once icons known
statement: Kobi suggested removing the status text later, once users know the icons; Lina agreed it is a good point.

topic: Market filtering without quick filters
statement: Emily confirmed there is no way to filter by market in the split view other than separate list views; table view has user filters but there are no quick filters. Emily will discuss internally.

topic: SLC missing data flagged for review
statement: Study link clicks without enough data to create a sign-up are flagged for review; someone fixes the data and a button reprocesses it through the automation. The test record without operator/partner was forced through and should not happen in production.

topic: Fraud flag locks sign-up record
statement: Any sign-up flagged as fraud is locked for rep editing regardless of status; ops must uncheck the fraud flag to allow editing again.

topic: Sign-ups flagged as fraud at creation
statement: Kobi said he had a question about sign-ups flagged for fraud from the start and would come back to it; he did not raise it again in this meeting.

topic: Archive reactivate button and reasons
statement: Archived records are not editable by reps; a Reactivate button returns them to In Progress. The archive and fraud reasons from the open-questions log are added; choosing Other requires more detail.

topic: Fraud review status; dismiss automation pending
statement: Ops set fraud review status (under review, confirmed, dismissed). The automation that clears the flag and reopens the record on dismiss is not built yet.

topic: Ops keep sign-up edit access for now
statement: Kobi offered to lock down ops editing of sign-up fields (partner, deal, operator). Lina asked to leave it editable for ops just in case and tighten it later when confident; Kobi agreed, with edit only for those who need access.

topic: Agency sign-up date from player
statement: The agency sign-up date comes from the player record (first sign-up), not BA input. It is not feeding in correctly yet.

topic: Affiliate sign-up date entered manually
statement: The affiliate sign-up date is manually entered by the rep, because a click does not mean the player actually signed up with the book.

topic: Relabel affiliate sign-up date
statement: Lina asked to label the affiliate sign-up date simply "Sign up date"; Emily said it can be relabeled and Kobi agreed.

topic: Rename to agency registration date
statement: Agency sign-up date is renamed "Agency registration date" to avoid reusing "sign up". Owen and Jay agreed; Kobi will make the change.

topic: Actual deposit amount checkbox (Phase 1)
statement: Lina confirmed it is needed for Phase 1: when the customer deposits a different amount than the allotted survey compensation, reps check a box under the deposit amount and enter the actual deposit. Kobi agreed to add it.

topic: Rep view of deal record
statement: Kobi showed the deal rep view: operator, partner, market, country at top, read-only; related lists cut to deal assignments and sign-ups. The More Info config tab (CPA, commissions, redeposit ranges) is for admins but is not yet hidden from reps.

topic: Manage deal assignment button in Salesforce
statement: Kobi showed admins/ops/managers assigning a deal to reps with an effective date and ending it with an effective end date; he noted the effective-from date must be kept on update. (Later in the meeting, assignment moved to the CMS.)

topic: Deal name representation
statement: Kobi said the concatenated deal name is long and asked the client for a shorthand for partners/operators. Lina said she does not mind the long title and the four deal parts at the top are key.

topic: Reps must not see partner
statement: Lina said reps must not be able to see the partner (e.g. GDC) on the deal; today the rep view shows it.

topic: Reps use deal assignments, not deals
statement: Waleed suggested reps get access only to deal assignments, not deals. Joyce agreed; Kobi agreed to simplify to a rep view listing assigned deals with operator, market, country, state and vertical only.

topic: Rep on one partner per operator
statement: Lina confirmed a rep is never on the same operator through more than one partner at a time; it is always one study per partner or operator.

topic: Volume target on deal assignment
statement: Lina asked if reps can see their given volume and progress against target. Kobi said Jumpr could add a manager-set target field on deal assignment and count related sign-ups against it; Owen said this covers the deal needs.

topic: SF-to-CMS sending not in scope
statement: Emily said the CMS working session changes where Salesforce owns input and must send information to the CMS, which is not built into the current scope. Kobi later said nothing goes from Salesforce to the CMS today and that side may be a bigger build.

topic: Deal config in SF, pushed to CMS
statement: Deal details and operator links are managed in Salesforce. When a deal is published it is sent to the CMS, where it appears as a dropdown option when ops assign a link to a rep.

topic: Rep assignment moves to CMS
statement: Deal rep assignments will be made in the CMS, not with the Salesforce Manage Deal Assignment button; Salesforce only displays what the CMS sends. Kobi said he had understood it the other way around.

topic: CMS pushes assignments back to SF
statement: When an assignment happens in the CMS it pushes back to Salesforce, with history, so reporting can track rep performance against the deal.

topic: Affiliate links at deal level
statement: Links are configured as a list at deal level in Salesforce, not pre-assigned per rep; in the CMS ops pick from the deal's links when assigning a rep. Emily had pictured it differently but accepted.

topic: Affiliate link list with on/off
statement: The deal page needs a place to add affiliate tracking links with the ability to turn each on and off; the rep link slug field is not needed on the deal.

topic: Where links are deactivated
statement: Joyce said deactivating a link deal-wide happens in Salesforce and inactive-link flow to the CMS still needs thought. Owen asked that link changes (including shutting off a link) be done in the CMS with Salesforce tracking them; Lina summarized that link changes stay in the CMS. Not settled.

topic: Affiliate link child object and API
statement: Kobi proposed a new child object for affiliate links (like deal assignments) with a button to create each link, tied to an API callout to the CMS once the callout is defined. Joyce accepted.

topic: CMS enforces link guardrails
statement: Salesforce will not enforce rules such as a link belonging to only one rep; the CMS must, and Salesforce can surface errors. Joyce accepted.

topic: Deals created in Salesforce first
statement: Owen asked to make link and deal changes in the CMS. Joyce said the CMS has no deal management, so ops must create each deal in Salesforce to make it a CMS option; Salesforce still tracks changes. Owen accepted.

topic: Salesforce replaces AirTable for deals
statement: Salesforce replaces AirTable for deal information, including volume targets; deal data added in Salesforce is pushed automatically to the CMS.

topic: Future CMS and SF convergence
statement: Kobi said the current split is a balance for Phase 1, and the client could later converge on one system (e.g. CMS creates deal config and passes it to Salesforce) to remove the manual step.

topic: CMS assignment built; API not built
statement: Waleed asked if the CMS change is built; Joyce said it is, but the API for the CMS to create and update deal assignment records in Salesforce is not built yet.

topic: CMS creates/updates deal assignments via API
statement: Deal assignments are the critical link between deals and reps for metrics. The CMS will create and update deal assignment records in Salesforce through an API callout with required fields.

topic: Jumpr to send API requirements doc
statement: Jumpr will accelerate and send a requirements doc for the CMS-to-Salesforce deal assignment API. Joyce asked for it ASAP; WagerTech could start on it later this week.

topic: API before data migration this week
statement: Both the API and historical data migration are go-live blockers, but for this week WagerTech will prioritize the deal assignment API over data migration.

topic: Fallback: SF assignment at go-live
statement: If the API is not ready for go-live, Waleed said the team can discuss using the existing Salesforce deal assignment until it is ready.

topic: Data migration needed for day one
statement: Waleed said data migration is needed so reps exist and see their data from day one.

topic: UAT this week; migration next week
statement: Kobi said, assuming the team is ready to go into UAT this week, data migration and spreadsheets can be worked on over the next week.

topic: SF-to-CMS payload and authentication
statement: Jumpr will define what WagerTech sends in payloads, but Jumpr needs WagerTech's input on what the CMS needs from Salesforce and how authentication works. Joyce agreed it is the grayer part and will prioritize it.

topic: WagerTech feedback on remaining screens
statement: Joyce said WagerTech still owes feedback on the rest of the screens and will provide it this week.

topic: Define player/operator/partner fields
statement: Kobi said sign-up and rep assignment screens are probably good enough for go-live, but the fields to show for players, operators and partners are not defined; he suggested the teams look at it this week and prep before go-live.

topic: External ID for SLC processing offline
statement: The external ID question for study click link processing continues offline using the shared spreadsheet.

topic: Records sent successfully on Friday

This is WagerTech's Phase 1 of the tool.

statement: In the fraud tool's Phase 2, results would move from the Google Sheet onto individual player records, likely via API; WagerTech will own the code and will probably build an endpoint.

topic: Fraud check applies post-signup

topic: Welcome email sets In Progress
statement: Once connected via API, receipt of the welcome email notification would move the signup record to In Progress, as an automated trigger discussed previously; endpoint direction to be sorted out later.

statement: Kobi and Waleed agree Jumpr can set up the Google Drive work as a proof of concept on Jumpr's side, confirm it works, then swap in the client's information.

statement: The client sent a new deal mockup with different naming conventions, but it was based on the Sales app rather than the WagerTech console; Kobi incorporated some of it and wants to review the rest with Lena and Emily before major changes.

statement: Kobi says that, for what was committed for phase one from a sign-up logging perspective, the project is in a very good place.

statement: Waleed says many small 'up next' items remain open on the Asana board; Kobi says new client feedback keeps adding items and they need an end in sight, then go live and iterate with real users.

statement: Emily posted an agenda covering API confirmation review, ID mapping worksheet, feedback on the deal list and deal edit modal, key changes to the sign-up object, and a WagerTech-drafted test plan (UAT); Kobi had not seen the test plan.

statement: Kobi will respond to Emily before the meeting, calling out timelines, the client's minimum MVP, and the decision on rep assignment that the client was to come back with.

topic: Brand ambassadors are Salesforce users
statement: Brand ambassadors (reps) are Salesforce users, not contacts; there is no separate brand ambassador screen, only the standard Salesforce user record page.

topic: External ID added to user record
statement: Kobi said the user record has little configuration; an external ID field was added to the user to help with mapping.

topic: Enable user search for Joyce
statement: Joyce could not find user records through search; Kobi said search must be enabled so users can be searched. Joyce agreed.

topic: Player records separate from user records
statement: Players are contacts / person accounts, separate from user records; a person can have an independent player record. To own and be credited for signups (ownership logic), a person must be a Salesforce user.

topic: Survey completion test integration worked
statement: Kobi checked the survey-completion test from the integration (by Strad): the survey completion checkbox and dates were populated by the integration user. Emily confirmed no errors after the unblock.

statement: Kobi said what data WagerTech imports from Airtable is their choice (could be only active accounts, deals, operators); trade-off is that reporting starts from when data is brought in.

statement: Secondary referrers get a bonus based on signup count. Kobi said that logic is not currently in scope; if added, prior signups (with related deal/operator/partner data) must be imported, or manual integer fields can hold signup counts to date.

topic: Import historical signup data
statement: Joyce said Airtable has no historical signups (only a current snapshot) and that previous signups still need a solution, but she thinks historical signup data should be imported.

topic: Historical signups need related deal records
statement: To import historical signups, a version of the related deal (and operator) must exist in Salesforce; otherwise signups have no relationships.

topic: Phased migration approach
statement: Kobi proposed a phased approach: start with anything active, record new signups going forward, and work backwards on historical data later. Joyce said 'Sure', then said to bring in inactive records too (next item).

topic: Import inactive deals and operators too
statement: After Kobi's explanation, Joyce said it makes sense to bring in all inactive deals and operators too, if the UI hides them or puts them in a separate tab. Kobi said 'That makes sense.' Overall migration scope was later parked until the CMS integration is final.

topic: Hide inactive/old deals from default view
statement: Inactive/old deals must not clutter default working views. Kobi offered an additional deal status (Joyce: 'Inactive is fine') or another status for very old deals, or a pinned active list view; Joyce left the mechanism to Jumpr.

topic: Data needed in Salesforce for agency site test
statement: For agency-website signup/SLC testing, Salesforce needs operators and partners with the external IDs used in the CMS, the deals, and the deal rep assignments.

topic: Test DRAs created on Salesforce side only
statement: Deal rep assignments should eventually be created from the CMS, but for this test they will be created on the Salesforce side only, for just the links activated for that agency website.

topic: Provide BAs and deals to test first
statement: WagerTech (Joyce) to tell Jumpr which brand ambassadors and deals to test first, with the related operators and partners and their CMS IDs.

topic: Only players, BAs, DRAs originate IDs in CMS
statement: Joyce's understanding: only players, brand ambassadors and rep assignments have originating IDs on the CMS side.

topic: Salesforce owns operators and partners
statement: Joyce stated Salesforce owns creation and management of operators and partners, so IDs should be created in Salesforce and the CMS ingests them.

topic: CMS has no operator/partner table
statement: The CMS has no UI to create operators; Emily said the CMS reacts at a deal level. Joyce said they had not planned to configure operator/partner records in the CMS but can accommodate. A new or changed operator cannot be configured on the CMS side.

topic: Inbound flow maps by external ID or name
statement: The Salesforce flow takes an external ID or a name and tries to match the operator/partner record. Both work; IDs are better because they persist through name changes and typos.

topic: Future state: Salesforce sends deal info to CMS
statement: Future state: deals are created in Salesforce and sent to the CMS with operator IDs; on a study link click the CMS pulls info from the deal, so no separate CMS table is needed. An interim solution is needed until then.

topic: SLC mapping test plan
statement: For SLC mapping the CMS deal record must carry operator name and/or ID and partner name and/or ID. Plan: list the deals to test via the agency website, configure matching operators, partners, deals and DRAs in Salesforce, then let people click through to test the mapping. Joyce agreed.

topic: Jumpr to suggest ID naming convention
statement: Joyce said WagerTech can add IDs and keep a table of them, but asked Jumpr to suggest the IDs and naming convention (deal, operator, all IDs) as part of the list.

topic: OP- and PT- ID conventions
statement: Operator IDs use an 'OP-' prefix with a counter; partner IDs use 'PT-' plus the existing partner code. Market is the country or state name. Joyce confirmed.

topic: Add proposed operator/partner IDs to sheet
statement: Kobi to put proposed operator and partner IDs on the ID mapping sheet as a starting point.

topic: Provide deal data for test import
statement: Kobi asked WagerTech to provide the deals (country etc.) to import for testing, reproduced on the spreadsheet; Kobi will make sure it is in Salesforce. Later Kobi and Joyce agreed to work on the deal import sheet together.

topic: Agency site click tracking not ready
statement: Hooking the agency site up to track clicks for live testing: WagerTech is not there yet but aligned with it as a requirement.

topic: Data migration questions parked until CMS integration
statement: Kobi said the remaining data migration questions do not need to be solved now; they are in flux and depend on the CMS integration fields and payloads. Joyce had only small comments and no red flags.

topic: DRA import from Airtable only for initial test
statement: Deal assignments will be imported from Airtable for the initial test only; after the test they will be configured fresh by flowing deals into the CMS and assigning them to users. Kobi: that is the next phase of testing; aligned.

topic: Sales view removed; Wagertech console is main app
statement: The sales view was removed to avoid confusion; the main app everyone uses is the Wagertech console.

topic: Partner info hidden from reps on deal
statement: Partner information on the deal is hidden for reps (visible only to admin/ops).

topic: Reps work from DRA record page
statement: The deal rep assignment record page now shows the key deal info a rep needs (operator name, market, vertical, signup attainment fields, deal status) and its related signups, so reps may not need the deal page.

topic: Lean deal page for reps, full for ops
statement: Intended design: the deal details page is lean for reps; ops users see the full set of fields to create or modify a deal.

topic: Deposit range separate from redeposit range
statement: Deposit range is different from redeposit ranges and belongs under commission terms. Kobi had thought they were the same (renamed in the last PRD) and will add deposit range back.

topic: Redeposit types and conditional range
statement: Deals specify redeposit types (assigned and/or immediate). A redeposit range is required only if immediate redeposit applies; then min/max range fields appear.

topic: Deposit range as two fields plus formula
statement: Because WagerTech wants to see where logged deposits land within the range, the deposit range will be two separate fields (min/max) for configuration, plus a formula field that displays the range in list views.

topic: Market single field with state/country
statement: Market is now a single short-code field combining state and country (with flag). Kobi assumes no state value with a country means multi-state. Highlights panel not yet updated.

topic: Hide deal name / partner from reps
statement: Joyce asked if the deal name can be hidden in rep-facing views. Kobi said a universal deal name is still needed (shown as the related deal on signups); an ops-only name field with partner info is possible but adds duplicate list views.

topic: Global deal name includes partner code
statement: The single global deal name will include the partner code (not the partner name), including in rep-facing views. Lina confirmed keeping it.

topic: Deal name format with vertical
statement: Default deal name: state (or country if multi-state), operator, partner code, then vertical. Lina asked to keep the vertical; Kobi will make it the default and can change it later.

topic: Short-form deal name used everywhere
statement: The deal name at the top of the record will use the mockup short form; it replaces the meaningless numeric deal ID everywhere.

topic: Bonus config moves from deal to partner
statement: Bonuses are configured at the partner level and apply across all deals for that partner. Kobi will move the bonus fields (bonus progress requirement, requirement type, status) from deal to partner.

topic: Bonus field population logic TBD
statement: There is no logic behind the bonus fields yet; Kobi wants to discuss later how they get populated. Joyce: in automations, anything tracked against deals must ladder up to the bonus view.

topic: Update deal list columns and fields to mockup
statement: Joyce asked whether Kobi can make the list view column and record field changes; Kobi said yes and will check fields match the mockup.

topic: Effective end date off list view
statement: Effective end date is removed from the deal list view; the field stays on the record and is filled when the deal is closed. Deals normally have no end date until shut down.

topic: Owner and deal version lower on page
statement: Owner and deal version are not needed near the top; they go under additional details / a more-info section, where lower-priority fields are bucketed.

topic: Priority tier picklist values
statement: Priority tier picklist options: primary, secondary, blacklisted (per the documentation Joyce sent). Kobi later said he will update the fields.

topic: Payout model with hybrid revshare field
statement: Payout model options include CPA, rev share, and hybrid (CPA plus revshare). A revshare percentage field should appear when hybrid is selected and not when only CPA is selected. Kobi agreed.

topic: Numeric monthly cap, zero = unlimited
statement: Monthly cap is a numeric field (always monthly), with 0 meaning unlimited, for reporting. It replaces the CPA target type (amount/unlimited) and related fields.

topic: Qualifying action, currency, deposit target
statement: Qualifying action is a text field for WagerTech's records; currency is set; a deposit target is needed in addition to the deposit range.

topic: Kobi to update deal fields per mockup
statement: Kobi will update the deal fields as walked through in Joyce's mockup; he called the changes straightforward.

topic: Keep the term 'bet credit'

topic: Referrer record shows its primary signups
statement: From the referrer record, users can see the signups where that referrer is the primary referrer.

topic: Cash payouts: batch or one-to-one
statement: Reps typically batch cash referral payments but must also be able to pay a single signup one-to-one.

topic: Mixed payout types per referrer allowed
statement: A referrer can have some signups paid as cash and others as bet credit (rare, about 1%), and the design must leave that open.

topic: No mixing cash and bet credit in payout
statement: A single payout record cannot combine cash and bet credit; mixed referrers need two separate payout records. Only one payout type can be batched together.

topic: Referrer-level select-and-batch payout screen
statement: Joyce described a screen at the referrer level where the rep sees all signups for that referrer, selects (for example) the cash ones and clicks a button to batch payout, which creates a separate payout record. Kobi later read back the same flow (select unpaid signups on the referrer, click create payout) and will design it.

topic: Cash payout tracks date sent
statement: For cash payouts the only tracking needed is the date sent (plus the BMO ID, see next item). Reps track this in a spreadsheet today.

topic: BMO transaction ID field, no screenshot
statement: Add a field for the BMO transaction ID on the cash payout so WagerTech can refer back to BMO for auditing. Lina does not want another screenshot proof. Kobi suggested just having the field there.

topic: Primary and secondary payouts kept separate

topic: No e-transfer email field on payout
statement: No e-transfer email field is needed on the payout; assume the email is on file for the player.

topic: Payout amount aggregated from signups
statement: The payout amount is the sum of the payout amounts on the signups rolled into the payout.

topic: Primary referral amounts from payment matrix
statement: Primary referral payout amounts come from a matrix (in the documentation; Kobi has it) based on the referrer's payout type and currency. The matrix sets the payout amount and currency on each signup (e.g. $50 USD).

topic: Payout record is single currency
statement: A payout record holds one currency. A referrer with signups in CAD and USD needs separate payout records; CAD and USD signups cannot be grouped into one payout.

topic: Referrer default currency, override per signup
statement: Each referrer gets a default currency on creation. The BA can override the referral payout currency at the signup level, similar to payout type, to leave room for ad hoc cases (e.g. dual citizen).

topic: Payout currency from selected signups
statement: The payout record currency comes from the payout currency on the selected signups (not directly from the referrer). The selection screen segregates signups by currency and blocks choosing multiple currencies. Two currencies exist per signup: the player's and the referrer's.

topic: Kobi to diagram currency payout flow
statement: Emily found the currency explanation confusing; Kobi said he will draw it out.

topic: Paid status closes signups, no double pay
statement: The payout record needs a status to show it has been paid. The rep marks it paid/complete with a button, which automatically updates the linked signups as paid and removes them from the payment queue so they are not paid twice.

topic: Phase 1: report amount and mark paid
statement: For Phase 1 scoping, Salesforce calculates and shows the payout amount and lets the rep mark it complete; the rep handles the actual payment outside Salesforce.

topic: Bet credit payout split by operator
statement: For bet credit, after batching (e.g. $500) the rep breaks the amount into smaller deposit amounts across the operators the referrer has signed up with, similar to redeposit assignment, so it looks like typical deposit behaviour.

topic: One bulk bet credit payout record
statement: Reps send the bet credit as one bulk payment and tell the referrer how to split it across books (usually one book). The payout record logs the total and the per-book split; it is not split into many payout records.

topic: Verify referrer signed up with books
statement: Joyce said ideally the system would verify that the referrer is signed up with the specific books before the split is logged.

topic: Book selection with multi-book option
statement: Lina suggested indicating the book, with a checkbox for multiple books that opens two or three options.

topic: Bet credit becomes redeposit records
statement: The bet credit payout record is related to redeposit records created by the rep (not ops/BM) and assigned to the referrer's player record. Each follows the normal redeposit process: proof of deposit, then close. All go to the same person.

topic: Guided workflow for payout allocation
statement: Joyce does not want a clunky process across many screens. Kobi proposed a guided, multi-step workflow: generate the payout, then allocate it into redeposits in the same process. Kobi will come back with the design.

topic: Kobi to design guided payout workflow
statement: Kobi will come back with a design for the guided payout-to-redeposit allocation workflow.

topic: Referral payout as redeposit type
statement: Joyce suggested adding 'referral payout' as a redeposit type for reporting on overall redeposit budgets. Kobi acknowledged; not explicitly confirmed.

topic: Same payout creation for cash and bet credit
statement: Payout record creation is the same for cash and bet credit. Afterwards, cash conceptually ties to bank transaction(s) (not necessarily required) and bet credit ties to redeposit records. The bet credit payout also captures date sent, BMO ID and currency, with redeposit allocation added on top.

topic: Secondary referral one-time bonus at 10
statement: Secondary referral: a global rule pays a one-time bonus when 10 eligible signups are reached, 200 in redeposit/bet credit or 100 in cash. No further bonuses at 20, 30, etc. Nothing else happens after it is paid.

topic: Secondary paid tracked at referrer level
statement: Kobi suggested marking the secondary bonus as paid at the referrer level rather than on the child signups, since it is one-time.

topic: Secondary payout follows primary flows
statement: Once the threshold is hit, the secondary payout follows the same flow as primary: cash requires logging that payment was sent and the BMO ID; bet credit follows the bet credit/redeposit path.

topic: Secondary counts all eligible signups
statement: Secondary counting ignores the signup's payout type: all eligible (completed) signups count toward 10. The payout type on the secondary payout may default from the referrer, and the rep confirms with the referrer before distributing.

topic: Signups past 10 marked not payable
statement: Emily asked whether signups after 10 would carry a status showing they were not paid; Joyce suggested 'not payable'. Not confirmed.

topic: Secondary is discretionary via eligibility flag
statement: Instead of always auto-creating a secondary payout at 10 signups (Joyce's ask, Kobi's earlier proposal), secondary payouts are at the rep's discretion. An 'eligible' flag on the referrer account shows eligibility and comes off once paid; the flag prevents auto-creation of the payout, and the rep creates it manually by picking the 10 signups like primary.

topic: Related lists for redeposits and payouts
statement: Emily asked that redeposits and their statuses be visible from the player/referrer. Kobi said any lookup relationship can have a related list on either side, so payouts tied to the referrer show signups and vice versa.

topic: BA commission outside Salesforce this phase
statement: Joyce asked whether a payment matrix should be in Salesforce or handled outside for this phase; Emily said outside and Joyce agreed. Joyce then corrected that she was thinking of commission and that this applies to BA commission. Kobi confirmed commissions are not being done now.

topic: No separate player payout workflow
statement: Player payouts (money sent for signup deposits and redeposits) need no separate workflow or batching; they are one-to-one and tracked on the signup and redeposit records, pulled into reports from the correct fields.

topic: Signup has deposit and actual deposit fields
statement: Kobi said the signup record already has fields for deposit amount and actual deposit amount; Emily confirmed players sometimes deposit a different amount.

topic: Reports use actual deposit, else expected
statement: For payout reporting, pull the actual deposit amount if completed; otherwise default to the deposit amount, for both signups and redeposits.

topic: Do not track money sent to players
statement: The system does not track that money was sent to a player for the signup deposit, and no BMO ID is captured for these deposits. Proof, amount and date are captured only when the player reports the deposit; a different actual amount is entered if needed.

topic: Payouts scope is referrers only
statement: The payouts build covers referrer payments based on the signups they bring in; referral payouts track only referral payments, at the referrer level, not signup payouts or a BA-level/ops view.

topic: Fraud-flagged signups block payment
statement: Signups flagged for fraud before payment must not be paid; signups still in review may be paid later if cleared.

topic: Remove signups from batch, cancel payout
statement: If a signup or referrer is flagged mid-batch, the rep must be able to take signups out of the batch and cancel or delete the payout. Later limited to unpaid batches.

topic: Flagged signups visible but not selectable
statement: Signups flagged for fraud (under review, not yet confirmed) stay visible in the payout selection list but cannot be added to a payout; this prompts the rep to check with ops.

topic: Confirmed fraud removed from selection list
statement: Joyce first wanted confirmed-fraud signups kept in the queue with a visual cue. Kobi raised that they would build up as noise; Emily said they should clear out. Kobi proposed showing confirmed fraud on the referrer record instead of the selection screen, and Joyce accepted as long as it is all visible in the same view (exact meaning of 'same view' not clarified).

topic: Ops report to manage fraud flags
statement: Emily wants a report for ops to manage and confirm flagged signups; Kobi said that will be separate from the payout selection.

topic: Fraud status values: confirmed vs dismissed
statement: Kobi described fraud outcomes on signups: 'confirmed' means confirmed fraud (a final status); 'dismissed' removes the fraud flag and reopens the signup, making it eligible. Lina described a 'confirmed success' vs 'confirmed fraud' concept, which caused some confusion.

topic: No minimum threshold for primary referrers
statement: Primary referrers have no minimum signup threshold before qualifying for payment.

topic: BA commission threshold logic not built
statement: A BA commission threshold rule was discussed (details omitted under data-handling rule 5). Joyce and Kobi agreed it is not logic to build now because commissions are not in this phase; it is for reference when reporting is built.

topic: Incomplete redeposits tracked at redeposit level
statement: When a bet-credit redeposit cannot complete, it is marked at the redeposit record level (cancel or write off, or cancel if funds come back), and amounts can roll up to the payout for reporting, instead of changing the payout status. The amount does not go back to the pool. Further handling can be added later if needed.

topic: Two incomplete outcomes on redeposits
statement: Emily said an incomplete redeposit has two outcomes to track: money lost (erosion / write-off) or funds returned, as two separate incomplete statuses.

topic: Paid payout locked; unpaid allows removal
statement: Once a payout is marked paid, the record is locked so reps cannot change it; fraud found later is eaten as a write-off. If the payout is not yet paid, reps can remove signups marked as fraud from the batch.

topic: Signup paid flag split primary/secondary
statement: The signup record is marked paid for the referral payout, with primary and secondary referral payments tracked separately; the rep records payment on the payout record.

topic: Deal commercial terms do not affect payouts
statement: Deal commercial terms are ops-level reporting only and have no impact on referral payouts.

topic: Separate financial reporting scoping session
statement: Financial reporting (total payouts across everything) needs a separate scoping session. Kobi said reports on existing objects/fields can be added afterwards and create no dependency now. No owner or date was set.

topic: Keep rep workflows simple for adoption
statement: Emily stressed that the workflows must be simple and logical for reps, who move between logging redeposits and signups, for adoption at launch. Kobi said edge cases and exception handling add complexity; V1 is iterative, the object model is the priority, and UI refinement comes after.

topic: Kobi to deliver design documents

topic: Two currencies and amounts per signup
statement: Each signup carries two currency concepts and two amounts: the currency/amount used to pay the player, and the referrer's payout currency/amount (from the referrer's payment preference and the matrix). The referrer's typical currency (e.g. Ontario vs New Jersey) should feed in automatically so the BA has one less field to choose. Kobi agreed; Emily said it is 'blurry' but accepted, and Kobi will diagram it (see item 33).

topic: Payout/commission calculation automation deferred
statement: Joyce said more automation of player payout and BA commission calculation (e.g. audit trails on bank account activity) is possible but not for now. Kobi agreed: get the data coming out of Salesforce first, then layer in automation later because commission rules change often.

topic: Signups leave selection list when batched
statement: Kobi described the happy path: once signups are added to a payout record, they are removed from the list of signups eligible for the next batch. This is triggered by adding to a payout, which is earlier than the 'paid' status update in item 34; how this interacts with removing signups from an unpaid batch (item 68) was not explicitly confirmed by the client.

topic: Update existing Jira stories to final design
statement: Kobi will update the existing Jira stories that change because of the final deal life cycle / CMS integration design.

topic: Epic scope: CMS integration plus deal life cycle
statement: The epic covers two things: the CMS integration and its prerequisite, the deal life cycle. This phase of the CMS integration syncs deals and affiliate links to the CMS.

topic: Deal creation via screen flow, not New button
statement: Deal creation moves away from the standard New button to a screen flow that holds the deal makeup fields.

topic: Deal makeup fields define deal uniqueness
statement: The deal makeup fields are operator, partner, market country, market state, vertical and source; together they make a deal unique. Kobi corrected himself that it is more than five fields.

topic: New default status 'New' for deals
statement: A new deal status 'New' will be introduced as the default status for every newly created deal; a Jira ticket will cover it because the status does not exist yet.

topic: Status changes only via controlled actions
statement: Users must not edit deal status directly; all life cycle moves (new to activated, activated to paused, retired, etc.) go through controlled action buttons, not standard record page edits. Kobi called this a constraint across the board.

topic: Lock deal ID fields read-only, incl. admins
statement: Deal ID fields that are user-editable today, even for admins, will be locked so users see a read-only version. Kobi said this is in the stories.

topic: Commercial terms section in creation screen flow
statement: Commercial terms fields on the deal will be their own section in the creation screen flow; the user can add them during deal creation or skip and add them later through a screen flow. Kobi said this design is not finished yet.

topic: Commercial terms as bolt-on after deal creation
statement: Cedrick should not focus on commercial terms for now; Kobi will treat it as a bolt-on after the new deal creation logic is in place.

topic: Pre-activation edits recompute keys with dup check
statement: Until a deal is activated, users can change any makeup field. On change, the deal external ID, deal name and makeup key must update, and validation must still flag when another deal with the same makeup already exists. Nothing goes to the CMS before activation.

topic: Must affiliate links exist before activation?
statement: Whether users must add affiliate links before activating a deal is to be clarified with the client. For now Kobi assumed at least one link is needed before the deal can be pushed to the CMS.

topic: Activation pre-check gate before CMS sync
statement: Clicking the activate button runs a final validation that the deal has everything needed for the CMS. If the pre-check fails, the deal does not move to Activated. This is a second gate after the minimum-required-fields validation at creation.

topic: Status date fields and first/last activation
statement: Kobi proposed a date field per status, set every time the deal enters that status, plus first and last activation dates.

topic: Lock makeup fields after activation for all
statement: Once a deal is activated, nobody (ops, management or admins) can edit the core makeup fields in the UI.

topic: Post-activation makeup edits stay manual
statement: Editing makeup fields after activation is a separate manual workflow with no automation now. Kobi is drafting a manual admin override process (for example through Inspector, with some validations).

topic: Activation triggers first CMS sync
statement: Deal activation is the starting point for the first CMS sync: build the payload, send it, capture and save the response, and handle the result. Kobi did not yet know the exact trigger mechanism.

topic: Non-critical fields stay editable post-activation
statement: After activation, fields not sent to the CMS stay editable, for example redeposit required, commercial terms and notes. Makeup fields and other mission-critical fields stay locked. Kobi said the list may evolve.

topic: Are effective start/end dates sent to CMS?
statement: Kobi was unsure whether effective start and end dates are sent to the CMS; he said it is TBD.

topic: Post-activation status changes trigger CMS sync
statement: Only fields in the CMS payload should trigger a re-sync. Every post-activation status change (paused, inactive, closed, review required, retired), including the automated inactive moves, triggers a CMS sync with the latest deal makeup.

topic: Auto inactive / reactivate based on signups
statement: Similar to the player automation, a deal moves to Inactive if it has no signup records for a defined period, but only when its current status is Active. A counterpart moves an Inactive deal back to Active when a signup comes in. The time period was not defined.

topic: Simple screen flows per status change
statement: Kobi suggested simple gated screen flows for each status (for example pause, close), with a reason field if the client needs one, and possible validations per status.

topic: Retired status releases deal makeup key
statement: Because the CMS cannot delete a deal, a Retired status is used. Retiring is the only time the makeup key changes: '-R' plus the Salesforce deal ID is appended, which releases the makeup so a new deal with the same makeup can be created. Cedrick agreed.

topic: CMS keys on deal external ID, not makeup
statement: Kobi recalled from the last meeting that the CMS side will not enforce unique deal makeup and will operate on the deal external ID; a retired deal keeps its external ID, so changes upsert into the existing CMS record.

topic: Makeup key internal-only; external ID increments
statement: The deal makeup key is internal, unique, used for deduplication and not sent in the API payload. Kobi believes the deal external ID formula is already built to append an increment (e.g. 001) so a new deal with a reused makeup gets a unique external ID; the retired deal's external ID stays the same.

topic: Closed deals reactivated, same record reused
statement: The current approach discussed with the client: a Closed deal can be reactivated, and if the same partner combination resumes later, the same deal record is reused and keeps receiving signups. Kobi called it the closest they got with the client and named versioning as the alternative if it does not work.

topic: DRA handling on reactivated closed deals
statement: Handling of updated deal rep assignments sent by the CMS when a closed deal is reactivated has not been figured out.

topic: Retirement replaces need for deal versioning
statement: Kobi had proposed deal versioning to the client as an alternative. In this meeting he concluded the Retired status covers creating a new deal with the same makeup, so versions are needed only if the client needs multiple non-retired deals with the same makeup active at the same time. Cedrick agreed. Client confirmation is still pending (see the separate action to confirm with the client).

topic: Document retirement as the versioning answer
statement: Kobi will update the documents after the call to say explicitly that retirement handles same-makeup new deals and versions are only for simultaneous active duplicates.

topic: Commercial terms as dated child object
statement: Commercial terms will become a dated child object to track changes, with no overlapping dates. Whether commercial terms are required before activation is still to be decided.

topic: Other deal fields that change over time
statement: Other deal attributes, such as redeposit requirements, may change over the deal life cycle; this was not discussed with the client. Such cases may need a new deal with the same makeup.

topic: Confirm changeable deal fields and versioning with client
statement: Kobi will raise it with the client again: confirm commercial terms points, whether anything else on the deal could change and need tracking, and whether adding a version makes sense.

topic: Activated deal cannot return to New
statement: Once activated, a deal cannot go back to New by any user method; each other status has its own defined path.

topic: Retired is terminal; Closed can reactivate
statement: Retired is the only status that fully locks a deal; nothing is editable after retirement. Closed means the deal is not actively pursued but can be reactivated later.

topic: CMS-side handling of synced statuses
statement: What the CMS does with each synced status needs to be coordinated with the client.

topic: Affiliate link changes trigger CMS resync
statement: Besides status changes, adding, removing or changing the status of affiliate links must flag the deal for a CMS resync every time.

topic: Sync trigger mechanism on the deal
statement: The mechanism to request a sync is not decided; Kobi thought a checkbox or date on the deal, to be confirmed in the user stories.

topic: Save CMS response on deal; error email
statement: When a sync runs, the CMS response is saved to a field on the deal. On errors, an email notification with the initial payload and the response is sent for troubleshooting. Kobi restated the notification email at the end.

topic: Store result only, not payload, on deal
statement: Kobi first said payload information would also be stored on the deal, then corrected himself: only the result/response is captured on the deal, not the payload.

topic: DRA push from CMS is Phase 2
statement: Phase 2 of the CMS integration: the CMS will send deal rep associations (rep, deal, effective from/to, assignment status) back to Salesforce after managers assign links to reps. It is not scoped yet and needs client input; DRA work starts after Phase 1 is live and tested.

topic: Staging object for inbound DRA calls
statement: Kobi is leaning toward a staging object that captures raw DRA API calls and a Salesforce process that maps external IDs (rep, deal, affiliate link) to create DRA records, instead of direct upserts. He plans to propose to the client what their system should send. Final call deferred to Phase 2.

topic: Diagram the DRA flow once mapped
statement: Kobi will add a diagram for the DRA (Phase 2) flow once it is mapped out.

topic: Phase 1 sends deals and links; group tickets
statement: For this phase the CMS integration strictly sends deals and affiliate links. The related deal tickets (new statuses, conditions, screen flows) are prerequisites in the same epic and will be done together.

topic: Link DRAs to affiliate links?
statement: Whether DRAs link to specific affiliate links: ideally yes, but historically one link was shared by several reps; in a recent call the client said it is now one link per person. They will try to capture the link in the DRA and decide at DRA scoping. Kobi said the linkage should be informational and not block processes.

topic: Add link ID to SLC/signups for reporting
statement: The SLC does not send the link today. Kobi suggested adding the link ID (not the URL) so signups can be tied to a specific affiliate link and reported by link.

topic: Link code is required, not unique
statement: Cedrick said the link code field is only required, not unique.

topic: Link external ID = link code + deal ID
statement: Add a link external ID to the JSON payload and requirements if not already there: link code plus deal ID as the unique identifier. Like the deal external ID, once set it cannot change even if the link code changes; changing it needs an intentional admin task that clears it so a new one is generated.

topic: Scope and add link external ID
statement: Kobi will scope the link external ID and add it after the call.

topic: Retry rules by CMS response type
statement: Business rejections and 400 (payload) errors do not auto-retry; timeout, network and other reason codes auto-retry.

topic: Progressive retry window then notify
statement: Kobi suggested a progressive retry window (a couple of minutes, then 10 minutes, then an hour), up to three or four retries, then notify someone for a manual retry. He was not sure how this works with flows.

topic: Manual retry checkbox, single and bulk
statement: Ops/management need a way to retry a sync without a status change, usually a checkbox, which also supports bulk retry. The automation entry criteria are a status change or this checkbox being true.

topic: Add retry checkbox story if missing
statement: Kobi will add the manual/bulk retry story if it is not already defined in the user stories.

topic: Unknown payload limits may force Apex
statement: The API spec accepts up to about 200 deals per call but gives no limit on affiliate links per deal or total JSON characters. Payload size could decide Flow versus Apex.

topic: Check Airtable for max links per deal
statement: Kobi will try to find the upper limit of affiliate links per deal from the current Airtable data.

topic: Verify Flow nested-array limit
statement: Cedrick thinks Flow has a limit of about 13 nested arrays within an object but is not sure and needs to check.

topic: Send full link list; absence = CMS removal
statement: Current design: every sync sends the entire affiliate link list; a link deleted in Salesforce is simply absent from the payload, which implies it should be removed in the CMS.

topic: Future card: skip synced closed links
statement: Link lists grow as deals cycle between closed and active, making payload size unpredictable. A possible future ticket would stop syncing affiliate links already sent in a closed status; the CMS would then need to stop treating absence as deletion. Kobi will take it as a future enhancement card; no change to current design.

topic: Store sync errors on deal, not new object
statement: Sync errors are stored on the deal object (in a separate sync tab), not in a new error object. A sync error does not change deal status (sync status decoupled), a retry clears the error fields, and field history tracks failures. Cedrick agreed given the timeline.

topic: Dedicated error object deferred to later phase
statement: A separate error object is pushed to a possible later phase if it becomes a problem; Cedrick said it is not doable for the October 9 target because it would also need client input.

topic: Working target date October 9
statement: Cedrick referred to an October 9 target when assessing the error object; the transcript does not say what exactly is due on October 9.

topic: Reports on outstanding failed syncs
statement: Kobi will build reports, which can be subscribed to, that show deals that have not synced.

topic: Flow vs Apex left to Cedrick
statement: Kobi left the Flow versus Apex choice to Cedrick, based mainly on payload size and whether batching works.

topic: Add New and Retired status values
statement: The existing statuses are fine except that New and Retired must be added as statuses, with user stories.

statement: Kobi will review the stories and push them to Jira tonight so Cedrick can pick them up tomorrow; some will amend existing tickets. Kobi will message Cedrick when they are pushed.

statement: Cedrick will start with the prerequisites (field creation and tracking) tomorrow, then the integration. Kobi agreed: prerequisite deal updates first, then the CMS integration, then UI components; screen flows and guided paths can come later but must be ready before the client tests.

topic: Validations deferred until UI build
statement: Validations are deferred to the UI work unless one blocks the automations; big stories go first so validations do not get in the way of testing.

topic: Confluence first, then Jira is source
statement: Kobi works in the Confluence page first, creates Jira tickets and adds the Jira links back to Confluence; once a ticket is in Jira, the Jira ticket is kept updated so there are not two sources.

A Slack-integrated bot is a goal but Kobi has no time for it yet. Cedrick said he will connect it once he works on the CMS integration.

topic: Post-activation statuses mostly informational in Salesforce
statement: Kobi said that, for the most part, setting the post-activation statuses has no further effect on the Salesforce side; they are visual or informational. Inactive is the exception with its signup-based automation. Closed is the ops way to show that no more signups should be sent to the deal.

topic: Deal versioning would ripple into client CMS
statement: Kobi said adding a deal version would also require the client's CMS and end-user workflows to change, and he thinks the client may not fully see the implications until they use the process. His approach is to build enough now, leave room to expand later as a follow-up, and get feedback from real use first.

statement: Kobi assumed that when a deal is closed all its existing affiliate links are deactivated (not deleted) and a new set of links is created on reactivation, which makes the link list grow. This is his assumption and was not confirmed.

statement: Kobi listed five items that still need design refinement, grooming and user stories: deal lifecycle and CMS sync, commercial terms, VIP workflow, redeposits, and referral payouts (the last two not complete).

statement: Kobi recommended V1 use standard Salesforce list views and filters, and building custom LWC interfaces only after use validates the need. The client did not explicitly confirm.

statement: Custom LWC list interfaces are a heavier build even with AI and need deterministic acceptance criteria.

statement: Joyce offered WagerTech dev resources (with Jumpr code review); decision deferred until work is broken into tickets.

statement: Emily asked for quick navigation buttons (my signups, my redeposits) and preconfigured views such as October Ontario and October Alberta; Kobi was unsure the nav dropdown lists can be configured.

statement: The non-console tab view may not support the split view used for the signup experience.

statement: Separate Salesforce apps can be set up for reps and for admins/managers; Joyce said 'We should do that.' Emily wants reps to be able to choose.
