statement: Kobi will create a standard (non-console) app with the same objects so the team can compare console and non-console.

topic: Deal lifecycle blocks signup logging
statement: Kobi said deal lifecycle and CMS sync is the most critical item because it blocks the whole signup logging experience.

topic: Nav dropdown lists may not be configurable
statement: Kobi will check, but thinks the navigation dropdown list contents are standard and cannot be customized.

topic: Budget per deal per month with entries
statement: Kobi presented a model of a budget per deal per month containing budget entries (each allocation batch) and allocations.

topic: Automated requirements not under monthly budget
statement: Automated redeposit requirements (e.g. a redeposit required days after signup) are not tracked under the monthly budget; they are independent.

topic: Manual allocation first; CSV later
statement: Manual allocation is built first to set the guardrails and fields; the CSV upload is bolted on afterwards.

topic: Scope CSV mapping; update client tool
statement: CSV import needs scoping; WagerTech's tool may need extra fields so Salesforce can map rows to the right person and deal. Emily said they will make it happen; Joyce suggested a Claude skill for the mapping.

topic: Personal redeposit eligibility window
statement: Personal redeposits may allow a longer look-back; Emily will confirm with Owen. Joyce suggested a universal 6-month maximum for personal redeposits.

topic: Eligibility windows vary by deal and batch
statement: Emily said eligibility windows are not global at deal level; mid-month budget additions can open extended windows (e.g. 3-4 months).

topic: Bet credit payouts not budget entries
statement: Referral bet credit spans books across deals, so it is not tracked as deal-level budget entries; it relates to a deal-month and is distributed freely.

topic: Remove middle budget entry object
statement: Monthly targets are forecasts, not caps, so no guardrails are needed; the budget-entry layer is removed and allocations go directly under the monthly budget.

topic: Budget alerts deferred to reporting
statement: Over-budget alerts and total redeposit spend (assigned, immediate, personal) will be discussed when reporting is built.

topic: Simplify new deal creation to core fields
statement: To protect the CMS integration, new deal creation will be simplified to core (makeup) fields with gates and controls.

topic: Eligibility dates on allocation record
statement: Start and end dates for eligible signups are saved on the redeposit allocation, filtering selectable players; a default on the deal pre-populates them (Emily asked for 'select for all').

topic: Allocation types assigned and personal
statement: Allocation types are mainly assigned and personal; 'additional' is kept for now; types are informational with no logic.

topic: Get back to Kobi on wager winner type
statement: Joyce suggested a wager winner type; Emily will re-read how they pull from budgets and get back to Kobi with Joyce.

topic: Company budget tracked outside Salesforce
statement: Spend versus company budget is reported outside Salesforce; no total budget is tracked in Salesforce.

topic: Bet credit goes to referrer
statement: A bet credit payout is allocated to the referrer, not via a rep or player; it happens inside the payout flow, not the rep queue.

topic: Bet credit counted as redeposit spend
statement: The bet credit payout must be recognized as redeposit money, rolling up by period and deal.

topic: Secondary bonus automated; payout type edit
statement: The secondary one-time bonus is to be automated (to revisit); changing a payout type after creation is not built yet.

topic: Allocate bet credit by book and month
statement: Bet credit is allocated by book and month from the payout total and becomes a redeposit record; the process still needs to be worked out.

topic: Book eligibility for referral bet credit
statement: Default eligible books are those the referrer signed up for; Emily noted they sometimes use other books and will get back on how strict this must be for launch.

topic: Payout flow feels clunky
statement: Emily said the referral payout flow feels clunky; Kobi said the UI can still be cleaned up.

topic: Delete before activation; CMS sync tab
statement: A deal can be deleted until it is activated; after activation it syncs to the CMS and cannot be deleted. A new CMS sync tab tracks integration-critical fields (live updating, for admins/ops troubleshooting).

topic: Stamp paid signups; write-off TBD
statement: Paid signups get stamped to prevent duplicate payouts; confirmed fraud marks a signup written off. How write-offs affect redeposits and payouts is TBD; Kobi will get back.

topic: Separate referral payout queue
statement: Referral redeposits get a separate, streamlined queue/tab (no player selection) apart from regular redeposits.

topic: Referrals/redeposits least developed
statement: Kobi said referrals and redeposits need more work but the team is mostly aligned on the data model; the biggest change is removing the middle budget entry.

topic: Kobi update prototype in next couple days
statement: Kobi will try to update the prototype with all the changes in the next couple of days and share it; after approval it will be broken into user stories.

statement: A meeting on CMS updates and deal/DRA alignment is set for tomorrow afternoon; Kobi will confirm his availability.

statement: Emily will send Joyce the product redeposit flow to discuss further.

topic: Deal data needed for rep testing
statement: Emily wants reps to test the deal endpoint and work in progress, and said deals need to be uploaded so testing does not error or show missing information.

topic: Makeup editable before activation
statement: Until activation the deal is like a draft; editing the makeup updates the IDs and external IDs.

topic: Reactivate behaviour differs by prior status
statement: Joyce said reactivating a closed deal could require updated data (commercial terms may differ). Kobi said the reactivate action applies to both paused and closed deals but can have different outcomes by previous status, and asked whether reactivation from closed should deactivate existing links/DRAs.

topic: Client principle: do not limit functionality
statement: Joyce stated a general rule for the build: stay open to any scenario and limit functionality as little as possible. Stated as a guiding principle, not a specific requirement.

topic: VIP signup otherwise same as standard
statement: Kobi's understanding: once a VIP signup record exists, logging, completion and fraud work the same as standard signups, with no other linkages; the only difference is the VIP indicator. He asked if anything else differs; no one named a difference.

topic: Rename budget objects; drop budget entries term
statement: Joyce asked not to call them 'budget entries' and suggested 'monthly redeposit budget' (or 'redep budget') for the budget record; Kobi said 'Sure'. The budget-entry layer was later removed (item 118); the final object names were not confirmed.

topic: Guided flow for monthly budget setup
statement: Kobi said the budget setup is broken into steps in the prototype and he would do it all through one guided flow (pick deal month, then add allocations), like the other flows.

topic: Kobi relate allocations to bet credit payout
statement: With the budget-entry object removed, Kobi will think through the best way to relate redeposit allocations to the bet credit payout.

topic: Kobi follow up on write-off logic
statement: Kobi will think through how a confirmed-fraud write-off on a signup rolls back into redeposits and payouts, and get back to the client.

topic: Deals design expected okay for next week
statement: After deferring the build estimate, Kobi said once the overall approach and behaviour are agreed, 'we should be okay for at least deals for the next week'. What is due next week is not stated.

topic: Proof upload per book for bet credit
statement: Emily asked that referral bet credit redeposits be finished in the referral list by uploading proof at the book level, where the payout is broken down; Kobi said he understood and offered a streamlined referral queue (item 131).

topic: Activation confirmation screen
statement: Activation uses a confirmation screen to review the makeup fields required for the CMS integration; after sending, changes need delete-and-recreate or the retire-and-replace process.

topic: Affiliate links not required before first push
statement: Client confirmed a deal can be pushed to the CMS without affiliate links; Kobi: if no link is needed, no activation error.

topic: Kobi share list of open questions
statement: Kobi will put his list of open questions (commercial terms, affiliate links) in the doc and share it for later clarification.

topic: Duplicate deal makeup error
statement: Creating a deal with the same makeup as an existing deal should show an error; Kobi still needs to confirm where that control sits.

topic: Affiliate link URL as long text field
statement: Because some Airtable URLs exceed 255 characters (DraftKings, Golden CTM), the link URL uses a long text field; if those URLs are not legitimate, the standard URL field (with built-in validation) could be used instead.

topic: Emily confirm long URLs are legitimate
statement: Emily will confirm whether the over-255-character URLs (Golden CTM, DraftKings) are legitimate.

topic: Exclude from CMS toggle on links
statement: An 'exclude from CMS' toggle was added on affiliate links (for the VIP workflow) for links that do not sync to the CMS.

topic: Links deactivate only after activation
statement: Once a deal is activated and synced, affiliate links cannot be deleted, only deactivated; new links queue a re-sync.

topic: Sync errors on record plus admin alerts
statement: Sync errors show on the deal record, with reports and email notifications to an admin.

topic: Which deal fields lock after activation
statement: After activation the makeup fields are locked and non-sync fields stay editable; what can and cannot be deleted is still TBD.

topic: Payload omission deletes links; size limits
statement: Per the current API design, a link missing from the payload is treated as deleted, which Kobi called super risky; growing link lists may also exceed payload size limits.

topic: Kobi summarize link strategy for Stra
statement: Kobi will summarize the link deactivation/deletion and payload strategy and send it to Stra to review.

topic: Status changes gated by action buttons
statement: Direct status editing is removed; deal status transitions go through specific action buttons.

topic: Is a pause reason required
statement: Kobi asked whether pausing a deal needs a reason captured.

topic: Notify on signups for paused deals
statement: Pause is informational in Salesforce; reports or notifications for signups on paused deals can be set up if needed.

topic: Pause status syncs to CMS to hide links
statement: Kobi's assumption: pausing syncs the status to the CMS and the CMS hides the deal's links without removing assignments; the hide logic sits on the CMS side. Joyce agreed in principle but asked for time to think it through.

topic: Higher permission to reactivate closed deals
statement: Joyce suggested closed deals lock functionality and only a 'super ops' tier (Alina, Jess, Emily) can reactivate, while pause/unpause stays at ops level; Emily agreed pause can be broad and reactivation needs a higher permission. Joyce said she was unsure it is required.

topic: Automated pause on caps later
statement: Emily said automated pausing when caps are hit will probably be built later.

topic: Closed-deal history kept as inactive
statement: Historical links and DRAs on a closed deal are not removed (to keep reporting); they can be put in an inactive/gated status. Emily agreed.

topic: Deal versions under a parent container
statement: Kobi proposed deal versions grouped under a parent container that rolls up numbers; Joyce and Emily said it makes sense, but it must be aligned with the CMS side first.

topic: Set up call on versioning with CMS side
statement: Emily will set up a call to talk through how versioning affects CMS workflows.

topic: CMS batch on/off and pause behaviour
statement: Joyce explained the CMS batch operator assigns one link to many people; ideally clicking pause in Salesforce turns links off in the CMS automatically. She asked for time to think it through.

topic: Link active/inactive flag is sufficient
statement: Links keep a simple active/inactive status; Emily said this is sufficient.

topic: Archive links instead of deleting
statement: Users get only the ability to archive links, keeping a trail in Salesforce; Kobi agreed.

topic: Exclude archived links from payload
statement: Plan: send inactive first, then exclude archived links from later payloads. Needs confirmation with Stra that an omitted link is not deleted, because the current endpoint removes omitted links. Kobi said this is not blocking.

topic: Retire as terminal status with replacement
statement: Retire is a terminal status: everything locks, the makeup is released, and a replacement deal can be created with a retired/replaces lookup.

topic: Cloning replacement deal may be V2
statement: Kobi said the cloning/replacement deal experience might be a V2 enhancement.

topic: Rename retire status to archive
statement: Joyce asked to rename 'retire' to 'archive' for consistency; Kobi agreed.

topic: Archive status need if versioning
statement: If versions are introduced, archive may only be needed as a terminal status, distinct from closed (an extended pause that can be reactivated).

topic: Inactive status after 90 days without signups
statement: A deal with no signups for 90 days (configurable setting) moves to an informational inactive status and returns to active when a signup comes in.

topic: Does deal inactive status affect CMS
statement: Kobi needs confirmation whether the deal inactive status should do anything on the CMS side.

topic: Remove review required status
statement: The 'review required' deal status is removed because activation is already gated.

topic: Close/archive sets deal links inactive
statement: When a deal is closed or archived, its links go to inactive (or archived); DRAs come from the CMS. CMS behaviour on archive still to be discussed.

topic: Pause deactivates links; resume restores
statement: Pausing deactivates all deal links; resuming reactivates only links that were active before the pause. Emily and Joyce agreed; Emily noted it may need adjusting after CMS alignment.

topic: DRAs change often and come from CMS
statement: Assignments change often (e.g. monthly recalibration) while links stay; Salesforce does not create DRAs because the CMS drives them.

topic: Kobi provide build estimate
statement: Emily asked for a build estimate; Kobi will provide it after the updates and user stories are fleshed out.

topic: Versioning decision needed ASAP
statement: Kobi said versioning changes many design decisions and gates built around a unique makeup, so it must be decided ASAP (possibly with Stra).

topic: Single living deal without versions
statement: Joyce suggested managing one deal record via internal archive processes instead of versions; Kobi said versions are not needed, then said the commercial terms design might help decide between versions and one deal.

topic: Commercial terms stamped on signup
statement: Commercial terms (payout model, deposit range, currency, rev share/hybrid) must be stamped on the signup as of the first bet; Kobi believes this is for operational reporting only.

topic: Custom object for dated commercial terms
statement: Field history is limited, so commercial terms history is a custom object under the deal; Kobi concluded the separate object is warranted.

topic: Commercial terms required at deal creation
statement: Deal creation lets the user add commercial terms now or skip; Kobi does not know if terms are required at creation.

topic: New term closes prior term
statement: Adding a postdated commercial term closes the previous one with an end date one day before the new start date.

topic: Signup linked to term by first bet date
statement: Signups link to the commercial term whose effective dates contain the signup's first bet date.

topic: CPA and payout model drive new terms
statement: Emily said the CPA amount (and payout model) are the main changes that create a new commercial term; some deals change CPA as of October 1.

topic: Report deposit range compliance by period
statement: Reporting must check whether signups in a term period hit the deposit range.

topic: Correct existing term or create new
statement: A 'manage commercial term' path lets users correct the existing term (mistakes) or create a new term with a later start date; CPA changes should be a new term.

topic: One active commercial term, no overlap
statement: Only one commercial term can be active for a time period; overlapping dates throw an error.

topic: Signups after term start tie to new term
statement: Signups from a new term's effective date tie to that term (e.g. a payout model change to rev share); Joyce agreed.

topic: Per-field term tracking deferred
statement: Independent tracking of individual fields (e.g. deposit ranges) is not built now; if needed, track it on a spreadsheet tied to deal ID and revisit later.

topic: Date changes recalculate signup links
statement: Changing a term's effective dates recalculates which signups link to it.

topic: Notify on deal without commercial term
statement: If a deal is completed without a commercial term, someone is notified to add one.

topic: Kobi share prototypes after cleanup
statement: Kobi will clean up and share the clickable mockups for feedback.

topic: Emily forward Lightning licensing email
statement: Emily will send Kobi the Salesforce product email so he can confirm whether Lightning needs extra licensing.

topic: MCP access may incur credits
statement: Kobi said the out-of-the-box Lightning interface should be free, but MCP access (connecting Claude) may start using paid credits; not in use yet.

topic: Agent seats and Owen MCP use
statement: Salesforce is adding agent user seats with own permissions; Joyce wants to keep in mind letting Owen use MCP during testing and rollout.

topic: Admin tasks via AI/spreadsheets
statement: Admin tasks like commercial terms or adding links could be done by feeding a spreadsheet to a bot instead of a polished interface; reps still need simple interfaces.

topic: Book session on AI/MCP workflow
statement: Emily proposed booking a session to talk through the AI/MCP approach; Joyce agreed. No owner named.

topic: Recorded walkthrough offered
statement: Kobi offered a recorded walkthrough of the redeposit/referral/payout objects; the group chose to continue in the meeting instead. No one accepted the offer.

topic: Design documents updated toward build-ready
statement: Kobi keeps updating the design documents with feedback so they are build ready for the team.

topic: Redeposit requirements tracked over time
statement: Redeposit requirements can change over a deal's life and need their own lifecycles and effective dates, similar to commercial terms.

topic: Multiple requirements with thresholds
statement: Deals can have first and secondary immediate redeposit requirements with different thresholds (e.g. 80%/90% and 50%), which must be reportable.

topic: Overlap rule for requirement terms
statement: Kobi proposed a commercial-terms-like framework for redeposit requirements and will confirm whether no-overlap must be enforced.

topic: VIP signup guided screen flow
statement: A guided flow with a 'New VIP signup' button lets users pick a new or existing player for manual VIP signups.

topic: VIP BA defaults to current user
statement: The brand ambassador on a VIP signup defaults to the current running user, with the ability to pick another person kept.

topic: Include paused deals in VIP deal lookup
statement: The VIP deal lookup will list active and paused deals because reps log late; other statuses are excluded.

topic: DRA requirement for VIP signups
statement: Open: bypass the DRA requirement for VIP signups or auto-create DRAs for VIP users on every deal; for now assume a DRA is required.

topic: VIP duplicate = same player and deal
statement: A duplicate signup is the same player and same book/deal regardless of rep; the VIP flow blocks it and routes to the existing signup.

topic: Different rep same player/book is fraud signal
statement: Emily said the same player and book with a different rep is more an indicator of fraud.

topic: Kobi verify SLC duplicate logic
statement: Kobi will double-check the existing SLC duplicate logic to confirm it matches.

topic: VIP tag/icon at player and signup
statement: A VIP indicator is wanted at signup and player level; the VIP flag exists but icons are still part of the build.

topic: New VIP-flow players default to VIP
statement: Players created in the VIP flow default to VIP; converting an existing player in an edge case is allowed.

topic: Referrers on VIP signup set to VIP
statement: A referrer added to a VIP signup who is not already VIP can be set to VIP; Emily said it is fine.

topic: Create VIP link inside VIP flow
statement: Users can create a link inside the VIP signup flow; it attaches to the deal and is automatically tagged VIP.

topic: Default VIP link set at deal creation
statement: If there is one VIP link per deal, Owen can add it at deal creation and the flow ties it automatically; if no link exists, raise an error or allow creating it in the flow.

topic: Payout-to-redeposit entry not built
statement: The payout that becomes a redeposit is not added to the deal yet (TBD).

topic: Monthly deal budget as container
statement: Each deal has a monthly redeposit budget that acts as a container rolling up entries/allocations added during the month.

topic: CSV upload and manual allocation
statement: Two ways to distribute redeposits to reps: CSV upload (parsing the client tool output) and a manual path, which is always needed.

topic: Bulk allocation lines with volume
statement: Allocation input takes rep + amount + volume (e.g. 10 at $50, 5 at $30), and automation creates the individual allocation records.

topic: Eligible signup date range set by ops
statement: Reps see assigned redeposits in a queue and select players; only signups within an ops-configured date range are selectable. Kobi will add it.

topic: Redeposit completion fields and lock
statement: To complete a redeposit the rep enters proof and the actual amount; player, book, date and region auto-populate. Completed records move to a locked, non-editable completed queue.

topic: Fraud flags/write-offs not in redeposits yet
statement: Fraud flags and write-offs are not yet in the redeposit completion flow; Kobi will advise when added.

topic: Can't-complete reasons TBD
statement: Reps will have a 'can't complete' option; the reasons are TBD.

topic: No return to ops; reps can release
statement: Reps may not refuse an allocation (return to ops) but can release it for another player; Kobi will remove the return-to-operations option.

topic: Gate send-back; validate with Lena
statement: Emily said they can validate with Lena what reps should be able to do; Kobi proposed time-gating the send-back option or unlocking it after several failed player assignments.

topic: Request reallocation with mandatory notes
statement: The return option is renamed 'request reallocation' (ops reviews it) with mandatory notes; notes are not mandatory for 'try a different player'.
